opportunities.title: CVPR 2027 Call for Papers
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Full papers for CVPR 2027 are due 16 November 2026 (11:59 pm AoE) with supplementary material by 23 November; no travel funding is stated on the call.
opportunities.description:
CVPR 2027, the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition, is calling for papers. CVPR is the largest and most selective annual meeting in computer vision, and its proceedings are published openly by the Computer Vision Foundation.

Paper enrolment closed on 10 November 2026 and full papers were due by 16 November 2026 at 11:59 pm AoE, with supplementary material due a week later. Reviews come out on 25 January 2027, authors can respond during a rebuttal week, and final decisions are released on 25 February 2027.

For African researchers in computer vision, machine learning and robotics, CVPR is the venue with the widest reach, and submitting authors also take part in reviewing, which is a valuable way to join the community.
opportunities.benefits: Publication in the CVPR 2027 proceedings on the CVF open-access site and the chance to present at the conference.
requirements: Paper must have been enrolled by 10 November 2026
All co-authors need up-to-date OpenReview profiles (new profiles without an institutional email can take up to two weeks to approve)
Authors must serve as reviewers when asked
Dual-submission rules apply from 16 November 2026 to 22 February 2027
documents: Paper PDF following the CVPR author guidelines
opportunities.selection_process: Double-blind peer review followed by an author rebuttal period, then final decisions by the area chairs and programme chairs.
opportunities.about_provider: CVPR is co-sponsored by the IEEE Computer Society and the Computer Vision Foundation (CVF), a non-profit that organises major computer vision conferences and makes their papers freely available.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit through the CVPR 2027 conference group on OpenReview by the deadline, which is fixed and will not be extended.
opportunities.notes: Rules on the use of large language models in writing and reviewing were still being finalised when the call was published.

opportunities.title: Cancer Genomic Epidemiology (course bursary, Mar 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Bursaries are available for researchers and clinicians attending this course at the Wellcome Genome Campus, 15-18 March 2027.
opportunities.description:
Wellcome Connecting Science is running a four-day residential course on cancer genomic epidemiology, subtitled Understanding Mutational Signatures of Cancer to Inform Prevention, at the Wellcome Genome Campus in Hinxton, near Cambridge, UK, from 15 to 18 March 2027. It is organised with the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) of the WHO and the Wellcome Sanger Institute.

The course is for early and mid-career scientists in genomics, epidemiology, clinical or public health who want to learn how mutational signatures in tumour genomes can reveal causes of cancer and guide prevention. Places are limited and awarded on merit, with preference for applicants working on related projects.

The course fee covers accommodation and meals, and merit-based bursaries can halve the fee, which helps African researchers in cancer epidemiology attend. The organisers can also provide letters for UK visa applications.
opportunities.benefits: Course fee £810, including accommodation and all meals. Limited merit-based bursaries reduce the fee by up to 50%.
requirements: Early or mid-career scientist in genomics, epidemiology, clinical or public health
Supporting statement from a scientific or clinical sponsor
Preference for applicants working on related projects
documents: Online application form (including the bursary request, if needed)
Sponsor's supporting statement as a PDF from a supervisor, line manager or head of department
Bursary justification from the applicant and sponsor
opportunities.selection_process: Places and bursaries are awarded on merit by a committee, usually within a month of the deadline. The committee's decision is final.
important_dates: Application and bursary deadline: the page gives both 16 November and 23 November 2026, so apply by 16 November to be safe
opportunities.about_provider: Wellcome Connecting Science is the training and events arm of the Wellcome Sanger Institute, funded by Wellcome. It runs courses and conferences in genomics and biomedical science on the Wellcome Genome Campus and worldwide.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the event's applicant portal on eventsair and upload your sponsor's statement; applications without it are not considered. Tick the bursary option in the same form if you need fee support. The fee is requested only after acceptance.
opportunities.notes: Contact events@sanger.ac.uk or courses@wellcomeconnectingscience.org with questions. Many nationalities need no UK visa for short courses; the organisers can send a visa support letter.

opportunities.title: Marlène and Paolo Fresco Fellowship for African Studies (Jan-Jun 2028)
opportunities.provider: Villa I Tatti, Harvard University Center for Italian Renaissance Studies
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Six-month residential fellowship in Florence for PhD holders researching African-Mediterranean exchange (c. 1250-1750), with USD 5,200 a month plus relocation support and housing where possible.
opportunities.description:
Villa I Tatti, the Harvard University Center for Italian Renaissance Studies in Florence, offers the Marlène and Paolo Fresco Fellowship for African Studies, a six-month residential postdoctoral fellowship for the spring term of January to June 2028. It supports research on exchanges between Africa and the Mediterranean world between about 1250 and 1750, with a preference for projects on early modern links between Africa and Italy.

Fellows live in the Florence area, spend at least three days a week at I Tatti and work on their own research alongside a community of scholars, with access to the centre's library and collections. They cannot teach or hold other fellowships during the term.

This is an unusual opportunity for African historians with a PhD whose work touches on Africa's historical ties with Italy and the Mediterranean.
opportunities.benefits: A stipend of US$5,200 per month, a one-time relocation supplement of up to US$1,800, and a rent-free apartment (utilities charged) or a housing subsidy.
requirements: PhD already awarded (not pursuing a second PhD)
Fluent in English, Italian or French
Solid background in African history
Research on Africa-Mediterranean exchange c. 1250-1750, ideally Africa-Italy
No other fellowship, award or teaching during the term
Must live in the Florence area and be at I Tatti at least three days a week
Not previously appointed at I Tatti (former Graduate Fellows excepted)
documents: Online application in English or Italian
Two recommendation letters in English, French or Italian, uploaded by referees
important_dates: Application deadline: 16 November 2026 (midnight, Cambridge MA time)
opportunities.about_provider: Villa I Tatti is Harvard University's research centre for Italian Renaissance studies, located in the hills outside Florence. It hosts postdoctoral fellows each year and holds a major library and art collection.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through I Tatti's SlideRoom portal and ask your two referees to upload their letters online by 21 November 2026. Only one type of I Tatti fellowship can be applied for in an academic year.
opportunities.notes: The fellowship cannot be deferred and can be held only once.

opportunities.title: Princeton PIIRS Fung Global Fellows Program 2027/2028
opportunities.provider: Princeton Institute for International and Regional Studies (PIIRS)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Early-career scholars with a PhD awarded after 1 September 2017 who hold a faculty or research post outside the USA can apply for a year in residence at Princeton on the theme Democracy in Crisis?
opportunities.description:
The Fung Global Fellows Program at the Princeton Institute for International and Regional Studies (PIIRS) brings a small group of early-career scholars from outside the United States to Princeton University for a ten-month residential fellowship. The 2027-2028 cohort will work under the theme Democracy in Crisis?, with fellows appointed as Visiting Research Scholars.

Fellows spend the academic year on campus pursuing their own research, taking part in a shared seminar and contributing to the intellectual life of PIIRS. They must hold a faculty or research post outside the US and return to it afterwards.

African social scientists and humanists who earned their PhD after September 2017 and whose research engages with democracy, governance or political change are well placed to apply.
opportunities.benefits: A ten-month residential appointment at Princeton as a Visiting Research Scholar. The page does not list the stipend amount.
requirements: PhD or equivalent, generally received after 1 September 2017
Faculty or professional research appointment outside the US, with a plan to return
Current PhD students and postdocs are not eligible
Research related to the theme Democracy in Crisis?
Able to obtain a suitable US visa (H-1B processing is not available)
documents: Cover letter of up to 1.5 pages
Research proposal of up to 3 single-spaced pages
One writing sample of up to 50 pages
Three referees, who are invited by email to upload letters
opportunities.selection_process: Selection is based on the strength of the project, its fit with the theme, the applicant's scholarly record, their likely contribution to the programme, and work experience outside the US. Finalists have a virtual interview.
important_dates: Finalist interviews: mid-December 2026 to early January 2027
opportunities.about_provider: PIIRS is Princeton University's institute for international and regional studies. It supports research and teaching on global issues and runs the Fung Global Fellows Program for international early-career scholars.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit all materials in English through the programme's Interfolio page (apply.interfolio.com/191685) before the portal locks at the deadline. Supplementary materials are not accepted.
opportunities.notes: Late applications are not accepted. Interfolio's helpdesk handles technical problems.

opportunities.title: TWAS-SISSA-Lincei Research Cooperation Visits Programme
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Funded research visits to SISSA in Trieste for researchers aged 40 or under who are nationals of a least developed country, hold an MSc or higher and hold a research position in an LDC.
opportunities.description:
The TWAS-SISSA-Lincei Research Cooperation Visits Programme funds three-month research visits to centres of excellence in Trieste and Udine, Italy, for scientists from the world's least developed countries. It is run by UNESCO-TWAS together with the Accademia Nazionale dei Lincei and SISSA, and paid for by the Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Italian Agency for Development Cooperation.

Visitors work with a host laboratory on a joint project linked to the UN Sustainable Development Goals. Host institutions include SISSA, ICGEB, INFN, OGS, the Universities of Trieste and Udine, IOM-CNR, Area Science Park and Elettra. The deadline, originally 31 October 2026, was extended to 16 November 2026.

Many African countries are on the least developed countries list, so researchers under 40 in those countries who hold a research post at home are the main target group.
opportunities.benefits: Travel costs and living expenses for a three-month research visit in Trieste or Udine, Italy (amounts not stated).
requirements: National of a least developed country
MSc or higher
Holds a research position in a least developed country
Aged 40 or under on 31 December of the application year
Not already in the host country; part-time visits not eligible
Must show the intention to return home after the visit
Only one TWAS/OWSD programme per calendar year
documents: Statement of scientific interests and SDG-related plans for the home country
Invitation letter from an eligible host lab confirming a 3-month visit
opportunities.selection_process: A selection committee assesses applications on scientific merit. Applications must be in English, and only the fields listed on the form are considered.
opportunities.about_provider: UNESCO-TWAS, The World Academy of Sciences, promotes scientific capacity in developing countries through fellowships, grants and exchanges. SISSA is an international school for advanced studies in Trieste and the Accademia dei Lincei is Italy's national academy of sciences.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Contact a potential host supervisor in Trieste or Udine early and obtain an invitation letter, then apply through the TWAS online form (onlineforms.twas.org/apply/310). Questions go to exchanges@twas.org.
opportunities.notes: Women scientists are encouraged to apply. Unsigned recommendation letters are not accepted.

opportunities.title: The Web Conference 2027 Short Papers Call (Dublin, May 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Short papers for the ACM Web Conference in Dublin (12-14 May 2027) are due 16 November 2026 with abstracts by 9 November; no travel funding is stated on the call.
opportunities.description:
The ACM Web Conference 2027, the long-running conference formerly known as WWW, is accepting short papers for its research track. The conference takes place at the Dublin Royal Convention Centre in Ireland, with workshops, tutorials and Web4All on 10 and 11 May 2027 and the main conference from 12 to 14 May 2027.

Short papers are limited to four pages including references and appendices, written in English in the ACM double-column template and reviewed double-blind. Each author can submit up to seven papers per submission type, and work already under review or published at another peer-reviewed venue is not allowed, although preprints are fine.

The conference is one of the top venues for research on the web, search, social media, data mining and online systems, and African researchers in these areas can use the short-paper track to present focused results to a global audience.
opportunities.benefits: Publication of accepted short papers in the conference proceedings and the chance to present at the Web Conference 2027 in Dublin.
requirements: Maximum 4 pages including references and appendix
ACM double-column template, single PDF, in English
Anonymous submission for double-blind review
Abstract must have been registered by 9 November 2026; no author changes after that
No concurrent submission to another peer-reviewed venue
Maximum 7 submissions per author per type
documents: Up-to-date OpenReview profile for every author
opportunities.selection_process: Papers are peer reviewed double-blind by the programme committee. Deadlines are strict and no extensions are given.
opportunities.about_provider: The ACM Web Conference is an annual international conference on the future of the World Wide Web, run under the Association for Computing Machinery (ACM), the world's largest computing society.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit through the Web Conference 2027 group on OpenReview before the deadline. Make sure all co-authors have current OpenReview profiles, and do not use placeholder abstracts.
opportunities.notes: Preprints are allowed and need not be cited. The full-paper deadline is end of day Anywhere on Earth.

opportunities.title: USask SIOS Financial Need Scholarship for International Students (Winter 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Continuing USask international or refugee students in second year or above, in good standing, who face unexpected financial hardship.
opportunities.description:
The University of Saskatchewan runs a financial need scholarship for its international and refugee students, funded through the Saskatchewan Innovation and Opportunity Scholarship (SIOS). It is meant for students who are already studying at USask, are in good academic standing, and face an unexpected money problem that threatens their ability to continue or finish their degree.

This round covers the 2027 Winter term within the 2026-27 academic year, and awards are made until the available funds run out. It is not an entrance award: students in their first year cannot apply, while those in second year or above, at undergraduate or graduate level, can. For African students already enrolled at USask, it is a practical safety net when family support or sponsorship falls through mid-degree.
opportunities.benefits: A need-based award whose amount is not published; it is paid straight into the student's university account and may be held back until the student proves they will register for the next term.
requirements: Current international or refugee student at the University of Saskatchewan
Second year of study or higher (first-year students are not eligible)
Undergraduate or graduate student
Good academic standing
Facing unforeseen financial barriers to continuing or completing studies
Past recipients may reapply, but first-time applicants are prioritised
documents: Completed Financial Need Calculator and application in PAWS
opportunities.selection_process: A committee reviews the financial need shown in the PAWS calculator and gives priority to students who have never received this scholarship before. Awards continue until funds are exhausted.
important_dates: Decisions emailed through PAWS: by 11 January 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Saskatchewan (USask) is a public research university in Saskatoon, Canada. Its Student Finance and Awards office manages scholarships and bursaries for domestic and international students.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Log in to PAWS and open the Scholarships and Bursaries channel (paws2.usask.ca/awards), start a new application for award year 2026-2027, choose the Fall and Winter terms and select the SIOS International Student Scholarship. Complete every section of the financial need calculator and submit before the deadline; if the calculator still shows 2025-2026, complete it anyway.
opportunities.notes: Questions go to USask Student Finance and Awards through its online help portal. The listing's list of eligible African countries does not appear on the official page: all current international students are eligible.

opportunities.title: University of Sydney Vice-Chancellor's International Scholarships Scheme 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: AUD 5,000 to 60,000 tuition awards for international applicants with an unconditional offer for a bachelor's or coursework master's; Semester 1 2027 Round 3 closes 16 Nov 2026 and Semester 2 rounds close 15 Feb, 22 Mar and 3 May 2027.
opportunities.description:
The University of Sydney Vice-Chancellor's International Scholarships Scheme rewards high-achieving international students starting a bachelor's or coursework master's degree. Awards range from A$5,000 to A$60,000 and are given once, in the first year of study, without a separate application.

Students are considered automatically if they hold an unconditional offer by the close of a selection round. For Semester 1 2027 the final round closes on 16 November 2026, with extra consideration for IB and International UAC students after their December results. For Semester 2 2027 there are rounds closing on 15 February, 22 March and 3 May 2027.

African students applying to Sydney do not need to do anything extra beyond securing an unconditional offer early, which makes this a useful award to aim for when planning a 2027 start in Australia.
opportunities.benefits: One-off awards of A$60,000 or A$40,000 (paid over one year in two instalments), or A$20,000, A$10,000 or A$5,000 (one semester). Recipients of a Sydney International Student Award can receive at most A$40,000.
requirements: International student as defined by Australian law
Applied for, but not yet started, a bachelor's or coursework master's degree at Sydney
Unconditional offer by the round deadline
Not receiving an Australian Government scholarship
Not a previous recipient of this scholarship
documents: No separate application; the admission application is used
opportunities.selection_process: Recipients are selected on academic merit from their admission application and nominated by a selection committee.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Sydney is Australia's first university, founded in 1850, and a member of the Group of Eight research-intensive universities.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for admission to an eligible Sydney degree and meet all conditions so that you hold an unconditional offer before the relevant round closes. You will be considered automatically and contacted if selected.
opportunities.notes: To keep split payments, recipients must have a semester average of at least 65 and no outstanding fees. Accepting another Sydney scholarship worth over A$20,000 a year ends this award.

opportunities.title: EMBO | EMBL Symposium: Mechanisms of Drug Resistance and Tolerance in Bacteria, Fungi and Cancer 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers at any career stage can submit an abstract by the deadline to attend this hybrid meeting at EMBL Heidelberg (9-12 March 2027). Financial assistance (registration fee waiver, travel grant up to EUR 1000 from outside Europe, childcare grant) is requested with the abstract.
opportunities.description:
EMBO and EMBL are holding the second edition of their symposium on the mechanisms of drug resistance and tolerance in bacteria, fungi and cancer at the EMBL Advanced Training Centre in Heidelberg, Germany, from 9 to 12 March 2027, with an option to join online. The keynote speaker is Eduard Batlle, and the meeting brings together researchers from around the world.

The programme covers how microbes and tumour cells survive drugs, with talks, poster sessions and an online platform. Only on-site participants can submit abstracts, and abstract selection is also how financial support is allocated.

EMBO and EMBL offer limited fee waivers, travel grants of up to €1,000 for people travelling from outside Europe, and childcare grants, so African researchers in microbiology, infectious disease or cancer biology can apply for support by submitting an abstract.
opportunities.benefits: Registration fees: on-site €750 (academia), €650 (PhD students), €950 (industry); virtual €240, €190 and €290. Financial help: limited registration fee waivers, travel grants covering transport, accommodation and visa costs up to €400 from within Europe or €1,000 from outside Europe, and childcare grants (priority to early-stage researchers).
requirements: Researchers working on drug resistance or tolerance in bacteria, fungi or cancer
Abstract submission is for on-site participants only
Financial help requires explaining why the lab cannot fund attendance
documents: Short statements on funding need and career impact for financial assistance
opportunities.selection_process: Abstracts and grants are chosen together on scientific merit, place of work or study, financial need and career impact. Results come about three weeks after the abstract deadline.
opportunities.about_provider: EMBL (European Molecular Biology Laboratory) is Europe's intergovernmental life-sciences research institute, with its main site in Heidelberg. EMBO is an organisation of leading life scientists that funds fellowships, courses and meetings.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Register on the EMBL events portal and submit an abstract by the deadline. On-site applicants receive an emailed link to apply for financial help after registering. The fee is paid up front even when a waiver is later granted, and travel costs are reimbursed after the meeting against receipts sent within two months.
opportunities.notes: Contact events@embl.de with questions. Hotel rooms are held until 9 February 2027 with booking code EES27-05.

opportunities.title: Hoover Fellows Program 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Salaried one- to three-year early-career position at Stanford's Hoover Institution for scholars with a PhD in a policy-relevant field completed by 1 September 2027, open to any nationality.
opportunities.description:
The Hoover Fellows Program at the Hoover Institution, Stanford University, recruits early-career scholars to spend between one and three years doing policy-relevant research and publishing. The 2027 position is a research post with no teaching load, based on the Stanford campus in California.

Fellows are expected to produce scholarly work on public policy in fields such as economics, history, international relations, national security, political science and public policy. The salary is high for a postdoctoral-level role and comes with a yearly housing allowance.

The page sets no nationality restriction, so African PhD holders or candidates finishing by September 2027 whose work speaks to policy questions can apply.
opportunities.benefits: A 12-month base salary of US$169,950 to US$230,000, plus a US$20,000 annual housing allowance.
requirements: PhD or equivalent in a relevant field (economics, history, international relations, national security, political science, public policy, etc.)
Degree completed by 1 September 2027
Research agenda relevant to public policy
documents: Cover letter or statement of interest describing academic background and experience
One or more recent publications, working papers or draft book chapters
Research plan of no more than two pages
opportunities.about_provider: The Hoover Institution is a public policy research centre at Stanford University that hosts fellows working on economics, governance, security and history, and runs a large archive and library.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit the application online through Hoover's SurveyMonkey Apply portal (hoover.smapply.us) and arrange three recommendation letters. Questions go to hooverfellowship@stanford.edu, which is checked only periodically.
opportunities.notes: The page body describes appointments of one to three years.

opportunities.title: DPH 2027 Digital Public Health Conference Call for Papers (London)
opportunities.provider: UCL Centre for Digital Public Health in Emergencies
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers worldwide working on digital public health can submit papers or abstracts.
opportunities.description:
DPH 2027, the 12th International Digital Public Health Conference, will take place in London from 15 to 17 June 2027, hosted by the UCL Centre for Digital Public Health in Emergencies, with a student day on 14 June. The main track invites research papers and extended abstracts on digital technologies, data and AI for public health.

Accepted work is published only if the presenting author registers and attends in person. African researchers can look at the external travel support listed on the conference's grant page, such as the Connect Africa scholarships for researchers at certain African institutes.
opportunities.benefits: A chance to present and publish research at an international digital public health conference; the conference itself does not fund travel, but its grant page lists outside schemes.
requirements: Original research on digital public health
Full papers of 4 to 8 pages in IEEE double-column format, anonymised, or extended abstracts of up to 1,000 words excluding references
Presenting author must register and attend in person in London
documents: Anonymised full paper or extended abstract
opportunities.selection_process: Submissions are peer reviewed, with notifications on 28 January 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: The UCL Centre for Digital Public Health in Emergencies studies how digital data and tools can improve public health, particularly during crises. University College London is one of the UK's leading research universities.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Prepare an anonymised paper or abstract in the required format and submit it through the conference's EasyChair site before 18 November 2026. Contact support@dphconf.org with questions.
opportunities.notes: Check the grant schemes page for travel support aimed at researchers from Africa and other low- and middle-income regions.

opportunities.title: US-MEPI Tomorrow's Leaders Program 2027/2028
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Full four-year undergraduate scholarship at AUB or LAU in Lebanon for high school seniors or 2026 graduates from MENA countries, so in Africa only Algerian, Egyptian, Libyan, Moroccan and Tunisian nationals qualify.
opportunities.description:
The Tomorrow's Leaders Undergraduate Program, funded by the U.S.-Middle East Partnership Initiative (MEPI) of the U.S. Department of State, gives secondary school graduates from the Middle East and North Africa a full scholarship for a bachelor's degree at the American University of Beirut or the Lebanese American University in Lebanon. Each student can also spend a semester at a university in the United States.

Alongside their degree, scholars receive leadership training, career workshops, internships, faculty mentoring and academic advising. The next cohort starts in August 2027 and recruitment is managed by FHI 360 for MEPI.

North African students from Algeria, Egypt, Libya, Morocco and Tunisia are eligible, making this one of the few fully funded undergraduate packages open to them in the region.
opportunities.benefits: Full tuition for up to four academic years, enrolment fees, university housing (double room), health insurance, visa and residency fees, a monthly living allowance, a yearly book allowance, a laptop, two return flights a year where applicable, a study-abroad semester in the US, plus internships, mentoring and leadership training.
requirements: Citizen of Algeria, Egypt, Jordan, Lebanon, Libya, Morocco, Tunisia, Syria, Yemen or Iraq, or a West Bank/Palestinian applicant legally resident in a third country
High school senior or 2026 graduate (2025 graduates also eligible from Iraq, Libya, Syria, Yemen and West Bank/Palestine)
Strong grades and a pass in the high school leaving exam
TOEFL iBT of at least 80, taken less than two years before the start
Leadership potential, maturity and flexibility
US citizens and permanent residents are not eligible
opportunities.about_provider: MEPI is a U.S. Department of State programme that supports education, civil society and economic opportunity in the Middle East and North Africa. FHI 360, a non-profit development organisation, runs recruitment for the Tomorrow's Leaders programme.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Read the full eligibility rules and apply through the Tomorrow's Leaders website (tomorrowsleadersprogram.org), which is linked from the MEPI page.
opportunities.notes: Up to one year of intensive English can be provided if needed before degree study.

The University of Edinburgh's Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program funds young Africans to take postgraduate degrees, on campus in Edinburgh or online, starting in September 2027. Only invited candidates can now submit the main application, which closes on 19 November 2026.

Attended a mandatory virtual information session (15-24 September 2026)
Received an invitation to apply (sent 13 October 2026)

opportunities.description:
The Planet Health Film Fund, created by the climate storytelling studio Earthrise and the health company Bupa, with BAFTA albert as sustainability partner, commissions short documentaries about how the health of the planet affects human health. For 2027 it will fund five films of about ten minutes, each with a two-minute social media cut.

The five selected teams join an online development programme in January 2027, produce their films between January and May 2027, and premiere them at SXSW London on 26 May 2027, followed by an audience award in June. The extended deadline for applications is 6 pm GMT on 19 November 2026.

The call is open internationally, so African documentary directors with a registered production company and a track record of festival or broadcast work can apply to tell climate and health stories from their own communities.
opportunities.benefits: Five awards of £20,000 each to make a roughly 10-minute documentary and a 2-minute social version, plus a development programme and a premiere at SXSW London. The award is paid to the production company and must cover the whole production.
requirements: Aged 18 or over; open internationally
Lead applicant must be the director (co-directors allowed); one entry per person
A previous film selected by a recognised festival or commissioned or distributed by an established broadcaster or platform
A legally registered production company at the time of applying
Documentary only, not yet in production or post-production
Application in English; no AI-generated content in audience-facing material
Available for online development sessions in early 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Earthrise is a creative studio that produces films and campaigns on climate and nature. Bupa is an international health insurance and healthcare group that supports the fund as part of its sustainability work.

opportunities.description:
The A.S. Hornby Educational Trust, together with the University of Exeter's School of Education, funds up to ten experienced English language teachers from low- and middle-income countries to take the one-year MEd in Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages (TESOL), starting in September 2027.

The scholarship is fully funded and is aimed at teachers who will return to strengthen English language teaching in their own countries. Most African countries are eligible as OECD DAC recipients, but Exeter cannot accept applicants from countries where the UK does not issue student visas, which currently includes Cameroon and Sudan. Undergraduate degree equivalent to a UK upper second class or better
Not already holding a doctorate or a UK master's in TESOL, applied linguistics, English or a related field
No language test needed to apply, but English proficiency must be stated
documents: Online application form (31 questions) covering employment history, a supporting statement on an English teaching initiative you led, and your fit with the MEd

Birkbeck, University of London offers the International Excellence Scholarship to self-funding international students starting a full-time postgraduate programme in January 2027. opportunities.eligibility_summary: Full-time undergraduates in actuarial, data, computing, finance, economics, maths or statistics majors who live and study in Canada, Ireland, the UK, South Africa or Australia and have a birth parent from a listed under-represented group can apply by 25 November 2026 for up to USD 5,000.
opportunities.description:
The Milliman Opportunity Scholarship Non-U.S. Program is funded by Milliman, a global actuarial and consulting firm, and administered by Scholarship America. It supports high-achieving undergraduates from under-represented groups who are studying quantitative fields outside the United States.

Awards are up to USD 5,000 and are not renewable, though students can reapply each year they remain eligible. Eligibility depends on the country where the student lives and studies and on the ethnic background of at least one birth parent: for example, students of African descent in Canada, Black African or Black Caribbean students in the UK and Ireland, and Black or Coloured students in South Africa.

For African students this is relevant to those already living and studying in one of the five countries, including South Africa and the African diaspora in Canada, the UK and Ireland. Financial need is not required; selection rests on academic performance and an essay.
opportunities.benefits: Up to USD 5,000 (non-renewable; students may reapply in later years). Paid in February, by wire transfer outside Canada.
requirements: Live and attend university in Canada, Ireland, the UK, South Africa or Australia

At least one birth parent from a listed group: Canada - African descent, Latino/Hispanic, Native North American or Pacific Islander; UK/Ireland - Black African, Black Caribbean, Irish Traveller or Romani; South Africa - Black or Coloured; Australia - Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander
Full-time undergraduate at an accredited institution
Major in actuarial science, computer science, data analytics, data science, economics, finance, mathematics, programming or statistics
High academic achievement
Enrolled for Spring 2027 (Canada, Ireland, UK) or the first semester of 2027 (South Africa, Australia)
documents: Current, complete official transcript showing name, school, grades and credit hours per course and term (grade reports not accepted)
Required essay on how the award would affect your academic career and goals
Optional essays on personal identity and heritage and on passion for your field
opportunities.selection_process: Scholarship America selects about 20 to 30 finalists based on academic performance and the essay; Milliman then chooses the recipients and award amounts, and may also consider leadership and disadvantage such as first-generation status. Financial need is not required.

opportunities.about_provider: Milliman is a global actuarial, risk management and technology consulting firm. Scholarship America is a US nonprofit, based in Minneapolis, that designs and runs scholarship programmes for companies and foundations.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Click Apply on the Scholarship America page, create an account on its application portal using a personal email address, and upload your transcript and essays before the deadline. Incomplete applications are not considered.
opportunities.notes: Contact millimanopportunitynonus@scholarshipamerica.org or +1 507-931-1682.

opportunities.title: Barts Charity Doctoral Training Programme 2027
opportunities.provider: Queen Mary University of London / Barts Charity
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduates with at least a UK 2:1 BSc (or equivalent) in a relevant subject can apply by 26 November 2026 for a four-year funded biomedical PhD at Queen Mary University of London starting autumn 2027; overseas candidates must cover the Home/Overseas fee difference.
opportunities.description:
The Barts Charity Doctoral Training Programme is a four-year PhD programme run by the Faculty of Medicine and Dentistry at Queen Mary University of London (QMUL) with funding from Barts Charity. It trains future biomedical researchers whose work addresses health inequalities affecting the diverse communities of East London, and it recruits five PhD students a year over five years.

Students apply to the programme as a whole rather than to one project. After recruitment they choose a project from the programme's list, and they spend four years based in London with a tax-free stipend, research budget, conference travel funds and a laptop. The 2027 cohort is expected to start in late September or early October 2027.

The programme welcomes both home and overseas candidates, so applicants from African countries can compete. The key financial point is that the studentship pays tuition only at the Home rate: overseas students must show at interview how they will pay the difference to the Overseas fee for the whole PhD, as well as visa costs and the Immigration Health Surcharge.
opportunities.benefits: Tax-free stipend starting at GBP 28,700 a year with annual increases; tuition fees at the QMUL Home rate; research consumables of up to GBP 30,000 over the PhD; up to GBP 1,000 for conference travel; an additional research training and student experience fund; a laptop; eligibility to apply to the QMUL Postgraduate Research Fund. Not covered: the Home/Overseas fee difference, visa fees and the Immigration Health Surcharge.
requirements: At least a UK upper second-class (2:1) BSc or equivalent in a relevant discipline
A master's degree and research experience are advantages but not required
QMUL minimum English language requirement for the programme
Home and overseas candidates accepted; overseas candidates must fund the Home/Overseas fee difference for the full PhD
Only one Stage Two application per person (duplicates are disqualified)
documents: Stage One QMUL MySIS online application (course code RFQM-W6XF-09) with a personal statement typed into the form
Stage Two anonymised Barts DTP application form (Word template) quoting the 9-digit Stage One reference
Evidence of how overseas costs will be covered (if invited to interview)
opportunities.selection_process: Applications go through two stages. The anonymised Stage Two form is scored by a shortlisting panel, and shortlisted candidates are interviewed in early February 2027. Candidates are judged on their potential to carry out or support world-leading biomedical research, as shown in the application and interview.
important_dates: Start: late September or early October 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Queen Mary University of London is a research-intensive university in East London whose Faculty of Medicine and Dentistry includes Barts and The London School of Medicine and Dentistry. Barts Charity is a health charity that funds research and care linked to the hospitals and communities of East London.
opportunities.how_to_apply: First submit the Stage One application on QMUL's MySIS portal for course RFQM-W6XF-09 and note the 9-digit reference you receive. Then complete the anonymised Stage Two form on the programme's online form, leaving identifying details out of sections 4 and 5. Questions go to bartsdtp@qmul.ac.uk; fee-status and visa questions go to QMUL Admissions.
opportunities.notes: Browse the published project list before applying, since projects are chosen after recruitment. Budget carefully: overseas students pay the fee difference, visa costs and the Immigration Health Surcharge themselves.

opportunities.description:
Berea College, a small liberal arts college in Kentucky, USA, gives every international student it admits a combination of financial aid and scholarships covering 100% of tuition, housing, food and fees. There is no separate scholarship competition: being admitted is what triggers the funding.

In return, all students take part in the college's Work Program, working at least ten hours a week on campus. Students pay their own personal expenses, and a deposit of US$2,200 is required before the college issues the I-20 form needed for a student visa; this deposit can later go towards some expenses, and the college can adjust it for students who genuinely cannot afford it.

Berea is unusually generous for a US college, which makes it one of the few realistic routes to a fully funded American bachelor's degree for African school leavers. Competition is intense, because the college admits about 40 or fewer new international students each year, and entry is only for the fall term.

The scholarship amount is not fixed and depends on the candidate's record. African applicants with strong engineering, computing or science degrees can apply through the CUHK Graduate School online system; tuition for 2027-28 is HK$284,000 for full-time study, so the award is a partial reduction.

opportunities.description:
The Kroc Institute for International Peace Studies at the University of Notre Dame hosts visiting research fellows each year, drawn from scholars around the world. Fellows spend either one semester or a full academic year in residence in Indiana, USA, starting at the beginning of a semester in August or January, and pursue their own research while taking part in the Institute's academic life.

For 2027-28 the Institute is looking for projects in three themes: the intersection of gender, race, class and peacebuilding; international mediation; and sustainability, climate change and peace. Applicants must say in their cover letter which theme they fit and whether they want one semester or two.

The fellowship is a strong option for African researchers working on conflict, mediation, governance or climate security, because it is open to all nationalities and pays a generous stipend with housing, giving time to write and to build links with a leading peace studies centre.
opportunities.benefits: A stipend of US$30,000 per semester, a furnished Institute apartment at no cost, and access to the university library, internet and document retrieval services.
requirements: Completed doctoral or equivalent degree before the fellowship begins (PhD students must finish first)
Research fitting one of the three 2027-28 themes
Past Kroc visiting fellows must wait seven years before applying again
Open to scholars from any country

Research proposal of up to 10 double-spaced pages, including bibliography
Two confidential recommendation letters submitted through Interfolio
opportunities.selection_process: A committee of Kroc faculty reviews the applications and recommends fellows to the Institute's Director. They look at academic excellence, how closely the project connects with the Institute's research, and how actively the applicant is likely to take part in Institute life. Applicants hear the outcome in February 2027.

opportunities.description:
NorthWest Biosciences is a doctoral training partnership funded by the UK's Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council (BBSRC). It recruits a new cohort of PhD students each year to work on projects supervised across its partner universities, and the 2027 cohort starts on Monday 4 October 2027.

Projects sit under four research themes: animal biology in health and disease, underpinning bioscience discovery, understanding pathogens from molecules to phenotypes, and plant health, resilience, yield and growth. Applicants browse the project list and may pick up to three projects, each based at a different institution. Only one student is recruited for each project.

For African graduates the key point is that the partnership sets aside roughly 30% of every cohort for international candidates, and international studentships pay full tuition fees as well as the stipend. International applicants also have an earlier window than home applicants: theirs runs from 1 October to 30 November 2026.
opportunities.benefits: Full tuition fees (including international fees for international students), a stipend of £21,805 a year at the UKRI 2026/27 rate (£30,488 for holders of a veterinary degree), laboratory expenses and a small annual research training support grant. Visa and Immigration Health Surcharge costs are not covered.
requirements: First or upper-second class UK honours degree, or the international equivalent, in an appropriate science
International candidates compete for around 30% of the cohort
IELTS 6.5 (or an approved SELT) for candidates whose first language is not English; evidence can follow later but is needed before an offer is confirmed
Choose up to three projects, each at a different partner institution

opportunities.title: Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships 2027-2028 (research fellowships and PhD)
opportunities.provider: Swiss State Secretariat for Education, Research and Innovation (SERI) / Federal Commission for Scholarships for Foreign Students (FCS)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers born after 31 December 1991 who hold (or will hold by 31 July 2027) a master's degree and have a host professor in Switzerland can apply through GO ESKAS by their country's deadline (27 or 30 November 2026 for the African countries still open).
opportunities.description:
The Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships are the Swiss Confederation's flagship awards for foreign researchers. For the 2027-2028 academic year the scheme funds two kinds of stays for applicants from African countries: research fellowships of 6 to 12 months, and PhD scholarships of 12 months that can be renewed up to a total of 36 months. All awards start on 1 September 2027 at a Swiss university, federal institute of technology or other recognised Swiss higher education institution.

The programme is run by the State Secretariat for Education, Research and Innovation (SERI), and candidates are selected by the Federal Commission for Scholarships for Foreign Students (FCS). Deadlines are set separately for each country. For the African countries whose calls are still open, applications close on 27 November 2026 (for example Nigeria, Ghana, Cameroon, Côte d'Ivoire, Benin, Togo and Madagascar) or on 30 November 2026 (for example Kenya, Uganda, Rwanda, Senegal, South Africa, DR Congo, Namibia and Botswana). Countries such as Egypt, Ethiopia, Morocco, Tanzania, Zambia, Zimbabwe, Tunisia, Algeria and Mozambique have already closed for this cycle.

The scholarship is a strong option for African master's graduates and doctoral candidates who already have a research idea and a Swiss professor willing to supervise it, because it pays a monthly living allowance and health insurance for a full research stay in Switzerland. It does not pay tuition, so applicants should check the fees of their host institution.
opportunities.benefits: A monthly allowance of CHF 2,450 for living costs; compulsory Swiss health insurance paid by the FCS for holders from outside the EU/EFTA; a one-time grant of CHF 600 towards a housing deposit; a half-fare travelcard for Swiss public transport; and a return-flight allowance whose amount depends on the country. Tuition and semester fees, conference costs and fieldwork are not covered.
requirements: Citizen of an eligible country whose call is open (for Africa: deadline 27 or 30 November 2026)
Master's degree (or equivalent) completed by 31 July 2027 (30 June 2027 for ETH Zurich)
Born after 31 December 1991
A professor at a Swiss institution who agrees to supervise the research and writes a letter of support
A research project of your own linked to the host's work
No more than three earlier unsuccessful applications
documents: Research plan on the FCS/ESKAS form (maximum 5 pages)
Letter of support from the Swiss supervisor, plus the supervisor's CV
Email addresses of two professors who will send recommendation letters
Swiss residence permit, if already living in Switzerland
opportunities.selection_process: The FCS assesses complete applications on three main criteria: the candidate's academic profile and motivation, the originality and methodology of the research project, and the quality of the supervision and the prospect of future research collaboration. Incomplete applications and applications without a Swiss supervisor are rejected. Results are announced by the end of May 2027 at the latest.
opportunities.about_provider: SERI is the Swiss federal government's specialised agency for national and international matters of education, research and innovation policy. The Federal Commission for Scholarships for Foreign Students (FCS) assesses applications and awards the Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships every year.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Find a professor in Switzerland who agrees to host your project and obtain a signed letter of support. Check your country's deadline in the SERI country list, then submit the full application online through the GO ESKAS portal linked from the SERI scholarships page; paper and email applications are not accepted. Your two referees receive a request by email to upload their letters.
opportunities.notes: Only research fellowships and PhD scholarships are offered to African countries (the art scholarships are limited to other countries). Research fellowships cannot be extended. Check the latest version of the SERI country list, which was updated in October 2026, before applying.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Journalists aged 18+ from the 44 Least Developed Countries, with at least two years of published work, can apply for a fully funded trip to report on the UN Midterm Review in Doha (25-27 March 2027).
opportunities.description:
The UN Office of the High Representative for the Least Developed Countries, Landlocked Developing Countries and Small Island Developing States (UN-OHRLLS) is selecting ten journalists to cover the Midterm Review of the Doha Programme of Action, to be held in Doha, Qatar, from 25 to 27 March 2027.

The Doha Programme of Action is the UN's ten-year plan for the world's Least Developed Countries. Fellows attend the review, receive briefings and produce reporting that brings the discussions to audiences in their own countries. Each fellow must publish at least three pieces of journalism and send the links by 30 April 2027.

Most of the eligible countries are in Africa, including Ethiopia, Senegal, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Mozambique, DR Congo and many others, so this is a valuable chance for African reporters covering development to gain international exposure with costs paid.
opportunities.benefits: Round-trip economy-class flights to Doha, a daily subsistence allowance for accommodation and meals under UN rules, pre-conference orientation where applicable and access to briefings. The exact support is set out in the award letter; there is no cash alternative. Fellows pay for passports, visas and accreditation unless the award letter says otherwise.

Interest in sustainable development and the DPoA priority areas
documents: Two published work samples, at least one on development issues
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are screened for eligibility and scored between 22 November and 17 December 2026. Only successful candidates are notified, a reserve list may be used, and decisions are final.

opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit the online application form linked from the UN-OHRLLS page with your biography, two work samples and reporting proposal. There is no application fee; late or incomplete applications are not considered.
opportunities.notes: Ten fellowships are available. Contact: Ms Sithembile Siziba (sithembile.siziba@un.org). Fellows also file a short report within six weeks after the Review.

For many programmes the main round closes on 1 December 2026, with a clearing round on 31 March 2027, but deadlines differ between programmes, so applicants should check their own programme.

For African graduates with excellent master's or bachelor's records, the scheme offers one of the most generous PhD packages in Asia and a research degree at one of Hong Kong's leading universities.

opportunities.description:
The Echidna Global Scholars Program is a six-month visiting fellowship at the Brookings Institution's Center for Universal Education (CUE) in Washington, DC. Each cohort brings together mid-career leaders from the Global South who carry out research on gender-transformative education, meaning education policy and practice that tackles the gender norms holding girls and women back.

The programme has run since 2012 and is funded by Echidna Giving. It has completed 14 cohorts and has 48 alumni from 25 countries. Applications for the 2027 visiting fellowship are open now and close on 1 December 2026.

Fellows spend their time producing policy research with the support of Brookings experts, then take it back to their own country. That makes the programme especially relevant to African education researchers, NGO leaders, academics and civil servants who already work on girls' education and want a global platform for their work.

Good command of English

The Graduate Ellison Scholars Programme funds full-time doctoral (DPhil) study at the University of Oxford for students who will work on research projects linked to the Ellison Institute of Technology (EIT) in Oxford. EIT, founded and funded by Larry Ellison, works on science and technology for global challenges such as health, food security, climate and AI.

Depending on the project, candidates either apply through the EIT portal (pathogen, MDLS, plant biology and economics projects) or through Oxford's own route (the AI and robotics centre for doctoral training, the generative biology doctoral training programme and correlates of immunity). opportunities.description:
The Jim Leech Mastercard Foundation Fellowship on Entrepreneurship is a free, fully virtual eight-month programme run by the Dunin-Deshpande Queen's Innovation Centre (DDQIC) at Queen's University in Kingston, Canada, with support from the Mastercard Foundation. It helps African students and recent graduates turn business ideas into ventures through online courses, coaching and a pitch competition.

The 2027 cohort runs from January to August 2027 in phases: Explore (January to February), Ignite (March to April) and Launch and Fellowship (May to August), ending with graduation in August. More than 1,000 candidates start the first phase, about 180 finalists progress, and up to 60 are named Fellows. Applications close on 1 December 2026 and results are announced in late December.

Because it is online and open to any discipline at any African post-secondary institution, the programme is an accessible way for young African founders to gain business training, mentors and a chance at seed funding without leaving home.
opportunities.benefits: Free courses, coaching and micro-credentials; a stipend for up to 60 Fellows (stated as CAD 500 on the page and FAQ, and as USD 350 in the timeline); pitch competition prizes of up to CAD 15,000; and seed funding for Fellows who reach the Launch phase.

opportunities.about_provider: The Dunin-Deshpande Queen's Innovation Centre is the entrepreneurship hub of Queen's University in Kingston, Ontario. It runs venture programmes for students and, with the Mastercard Foundation, this fellowship for African students and graduates.

opportunities.title: Justus & Louise van Effen Excellence Scholarships 2027-2029 (TU Delft MSc)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Excellent non-EU applicants aged 35 or under who have applied to a two-year regular TU Delft MSc programme by 1 December 2026 can be considered for one of 16 full scholarships.
opportunities.description:
The Justus & Louise van Effen Excellence Scholarships are TU Delft's main full scholarships for international master's students. For the 2027 intake the university offers 16 awards, two per faculty, to outstanding applicants admitted (or conditionally admitted) to one of its two-year regular MSc programmes in Delft, the Netherlands. Each award runs for the full 24 months of the programme.

The scholarships are paid from a fund left by Justus van Effen, a TU Delft graduate from the 1940s, and his wife Louise. They are intended for applicants who rank roughly in the top 10% of their bachelor's class, although applicants do not need to prove a ranking. The deadline for both the MSc application and the scholarship form is 1 December 2026 at 23:59 CET, and applicants hear the outcome by email by the end of March 2027.

For African engineers, scientists and designers this is one of the few awards in the Netherlands that covers both full non-EU tuition and a living allowance, so it is worth applying early: the English test result and all admission documents must already be in the MSc application when the scholarship deadline passes.
opportunities.benefits: Full tuition fees for the two years of the MSc (at the statutory or institutional rate that applies to the student's nationality) plus a monthly contribution towards living costs for 24 months; the exact monthly amount is set in the scholarship contract. The second year continues only if the student earns at least 48 of the 60 ECTS credits of year one.

opportunities.description:
The Project on Managing the Atom at Harvard Kennedy School's Belfer Center offers ten-month research fellowships in Cambridge, Massachusetts, from 1 September 2027 to 30 June 2028. Fellows work on nuclear policy, with priority given to research on rethinking nuclear deterrence and reducing its dangers, and on resolving regional nuclear proliferation crises.

The fellowship is open to pre-doctoral researchers in the dissertation stage, postdoctoral researchers, university faculty and mid-career professionals from academia, national laboratories, government and industry. Applications opened on 1 October 2026 and close on Tuesday 1 December 2026, with recommendation letters due by 15 December 2026.

The Belfer Center welcomes applicants from all over the world and runs an application mentorship programme for applicants from developing countries and other under-represented groups, which makes this a realistic opportunity for African scholars of nuclear energy, security and diplomacy.
opportunities.benefits: A 10-month stipend of USD 50,000 for pre-doctoral fellows or USD 60,000 for postdoctoral fellows, health insurance, discounted public transport passes, shared office space and modest administrative support. opportunities.provider: UC Berkeley Center for African Studies with the Mastercard Foundation
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Citizens of African countries who apply to an eligible UC Berkeley master's programme of two years or less in its first application round can be considered for the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program.
opportunities.description:
The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at the University of California, Berkeley supports talented young Africans who are admitted to Berkeley master's degrees of two years or less. It is run by Berkeley's Center for African Studies in partnership with the Mastercard Foundation, and the university is recruiting scholars through autumn 2028. The programme is not open to undergraduates or doctoral students.

There is no single scholarship deadline. Applicants apply to one of the eligible Berkeley master's programmes (including the MBA, Master of Journalism, MPH, MPP and several Master of Engineering degrees) by that programme's first-round deadline, which falls between September and early January, mostly in December. Programmes then nominate candidates, who are invited to a supplemental application in February, interviewed online in March and told the final decision in late March or early April.

The programme looks for academic excellence, leadership potential, a commitment to community and an intention to return to Africa, and gives priority to applicants with an African first degree, no earlier postgraduate degree and no previous Mastercard Foundation support.
opportunities.benefits: The scholarship supports the full cost of a Berkeley master's degree for selected scholars; the pages read do not list amounts. African applicants can also request a waiver of the Berkeley graduate application fee.

Applying to an eligible UC Berkeley master's programme of two years or less, in its first application round (before January)
Academic excellence and leadership potential
Commitment to community and intention to return to Africa

opportunities.description:

Separately, international undergraduates with a GPA of 2.5 or higher and full admission are considered automatically for an international merit scholarship of USD 5,000 to USD 12,000 a year.

RAND's Graduate Student Summer Associate Program places advanced graduate students on real, funded RAND research projects for 12 weeks (60 working days) in summer 2027. Each summer associate is matched with a project and a mentor and produces research that feeds into RAND's policy work.

Associates can work in person at RAND's offices in Santa Monica, Washington DC, Pittsburgh or Boston, or remotely from home, but they must live in the United States for the whole assignment. US citizenship is not required except for particular projects, so international students, including Africans studying at US universities or able to be in the US for the summer, can apply. The programme is highly selective: RAND receives more than 600 applications a year and expects about 15 to 20 placements for 2027.
opportunities.benefits: Approximately USD 15,000 (before taxes) for the 12-week placement, paid every two weeks. Relocation costs are not provided. RAND supplies documentation to a student's international office where work authorisation is needed.

opportunities.title: TU Delft Faculty Scholarship: MSc Electrical Engineering (Microelectronics) 2027
opportunities.provider: Delft University of Technology (TU Delft), Faculty of EEMCS
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International applicants with a bachelor's grade average of at least 80% of the maximum who apply to the MSc Electrical Engineering (Microelectronics track) by 1 December 2026 can win one of up to two partial tuition scholarships.
opportunities.description:
TU Delft's Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science (EEMCS) offers up to two partial scholarships to excellent international students who start the two-year MSc in Electrical Engineering, track Microelectronics, in September 2027. The award is given through the faculty's Microelectronics department, where the scholarship holder also carries out the master's thesis.

The scholarship reduces the tuition fee (at the statutory or institutional rate that applies to the student) and can be renewed for the second year if the student keeps an average grade of 8.0 out of 10 in year one. An outstanding thesis project (grade 9 or higher) can lead to the offer of a PhD position in the department.

The award suits African electrical and electronic engineering graduates with very strong grades who want to specialise in chip design, circuits and microsystems. Because it is partial, applicants should plan other funding for living costs or apply for the Justus & Louise van Effen Excellence Scholarship at the same time.
opportunities.benefits: A partial waiver of the tuition fee for year one (at the statutory or institutional rate), renewable for year two if the student keeps an average grade of 8.0 (80%). No monthly allowance is stated.

Grade average of at least 80% of the maximum of the grading scale
English language certificate uploaded before the deadline unless exempt

opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for the MSc Electrical Engineering (Microelectronics track) through TU Delft's online application system with all documents, including your English test result, before 1 December 2026. opportunities.description:
The University of Missouri in Columbia, Missouri, gives international first-year students two main merit awards for the 2027-28 academic year: the International Honors Scholarship of USD 20,000 a year and the International Merit Scholarship of USD 10,000 a year. Both are applied to the non-resident part of tuition.

To be considered for these and the university's other freshman scholarships, fall 2027 applicants must apply and send all required application materials by 1 December 2026. Offers are sent by late January. Students then use the Mizzou Scholarship Application Portal to be matched with general and departmental scholarships, and admitted students can also apply to the Honors College.

The awards make a large public research university more affordable for African students, but they are not combinable with most other Mizzou scholarships and do not cover the whole cost of attendance, so applicants should plan the rest of their budget.
opportunities.benefits: International Honors Scholarship: USD 20,000 per year. International Merit Scholarship: USD 10,000 per year. Both reduce the non-resident portion of tuition and generally cannot be combined with other Mizzou awards. Transfer students can receive USD 20,000 (3.90 GPA) or USD 10,000 (3.00 GPA) with 24 or more transferable credit hours.

Fall 2027 first-year applicant with all application materials submitted by 1 December 2026
Proof of English proficiency
SAT or ACT scores preferred for the honors and merit awards
Stamps Scholarship not open to international applicants living outside the US (in-person interview required)
documents: Completed Mizzou admission application with all required materials
Award letter from any government or outside sponsor, sent to the MU Sponsored Student Program
opportunities.selection_process: Admitted international applicants are reviewed holistically for the honors and merit awards. General and departmental scholarships are matched through questions in the Mizzou Scholarship Application Portal. Offers are sent by late January 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Missouri is the flagship public research university of the state of Missouri, founded in 1839 and based in Columbia. It offers more than 300 degree programmes and has an Honors College for high-achieving students.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for admission through the Mizzou application site and send all required materials by 1 December 2026. opportunities.title: Vanderbilt Ingram Scholars Program 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: First-year applicants to Vanderbilt for fall 2027, including international applicants, can apply for the Ingram Scholarship through MyAppVU by 1 December 2026.
opportunities.description:
The Ingram Scholars Program at Vanderbilt University in Nashville, Tennessee, is a full-tuition merit scholarship for students who combine academic strength with a deep commitment to civic service. It was created in 1993 by E. Bronson Ingram and is run by Vanderbilt's Office of Student Financial Aid and Scholarships.

Ingram Scholars do about 20 hours of community service a month and design a summer service project after their second year, for which they receive extra funding. The scholarship is renewed each year to graduation as long as scholars keep a 3.0 GPA and meet the service requirements. First-year applicants for fall 2027 must submit the Ingram application electronically through their MyAppVU account by 1 December 2026.

Vanderbilt's scholarship FAQ confirms that international applicants can receive any of its merit scholarships, so this is a realistic route for African students with strong service records to study at a leading US university with tuition, fees and housing paid.
opportunities.benefits: Full tuition, all required fees and the value of on-campus housing each year, renewable to graduation; a stipend for a summer service project; and additional need-based aid if a student's need exceeds full tuition.
requirements: Applicant for first-year admission to Vanderbilt for fall 2027 (transfer students not eligible)
International applicants eligible for Vanderbilt merit scholarships
Strong record of civic-minded service, entrepreneurial spirit, character and leadership
Ingram application submitted via MyAppVU by 1 December 2026
To renew: 3.0 GPA and about 20 hours of service a month
opportunities.selection_process: The selection committee reviews the Ingram application together with the full admission file and invites finalists to interview. Selection looks for civic-minded service, entrepreneurial spirit, strength of character and leadership potential.
important_dates: Current first-year students: application mid-January 2027, due 28 February 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Vanderbilt University is a private research university in Nashville, Tennessee, founded in 1873. Its signature merit scholarships, including the Ingram and Cornelius Vanderbilt scholarships, go to about 1% of first-year applicants.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply to Vanderbilt for first-year admission, then complete the Ingram Scholarship application in your MyAppVU account before 1 December 2026. Finalists are invited to interview with the selection committee.
opportunities.notes: Vanderbilt is test-optional for fall 2027 applicants. The Cornelius Vanderbilt Scholarship has the same 1 December 2026 deadline.

They include the Carell Family Scholarship, the Clark Scholars Program for engineering students and the Curb Leadership Scholarship, plus other merit awards worth from USD 8,000 a year.

There is no separate form for these awards: students are considered when they submit the Cornelius Vanderbilt Scholarship application, which is due on 1 December 2026 for fall 2027 entry. Vanderbilt confirms that international applicants can receive any of its merit scholarships, and most winners hear in late March.

For African students aiming at a top US university, these awards add to Vanderbilt's other aid and can make the cost of study much lower.
opportunities.benefits: Carell Family Scholarship: full tuition and fees. Clark Scholars Program: USD 20,000 per year plus support for a summer immersive experience. Curb Leadership Scholarship: USD 8,000. Other additional merit awards start from USD 8,000 per year (limited number).

International applicants are eligible

Curb: creative leadership that has changed a community
Submit the Cornelius Vanderbilt Scholarship application by 1 December 2026

opportunities.about_provider: Vanderbilt University is a private research university in Nashville, Tennessee, USA. It offers several merit scholarship programmes to first-year undergraduates.

opportunities.title: CISAC Fellowships 2027-28
opportunities.provider: Stanford University, Center for International Security and Cooperation
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Pre-doctoral, postdoctoral and early-career scholars of any nationality working on international security topics, with degree rules that vary by track.
opportunities.description:
Stanford's Center for International Security and Cooperation (CISAC) is recruiting fellows for the 2027-28 academic year. The fellowships place early-career researchers at Stanford for a year (two years for one track) to work on security questions alongside the center's faculty and fellows.

For this cycle the center lists several project-linked tracks: AI and the laws of armed conflict, AI in strategic stability, the geopolitics of AI, Indo-Pacific security (a two-year postdoc), and India-US security studies for pre-doctoral, postdoctoral and junior faculty scholars. The page also describes CISAC's long-standing International Security, Natural Sciences or Engineering, and Nuclear Security fellowships.

CISAC says it considers applicants from the US and abroad without regard to citizenship, which makes this a real option for African scholars working on security, technology policy, arms control or regional security in Asia.

documents: Online application submitted through the CISAC SlideRoom portal
opportunities.about_provider: CISAC is part of Stanford University's Freeman Spogli Institute for International Studies. It brings together scientists, engineers and social scientists to study international security problems such as nuclear weapons, emerging technologies and conflict.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Read the track descriptions on the CISAC fellowship page, then submit an application through the center's SlideRoom portal (cisacstanford.slideroom.com) before 2 December 2026. Questions go to CISACfellowship@stanford.edu.
opportunities.notes: The page does not state stipend amounts; check the SlideRoom call for details of each track.

opportunities.title: John S. Knight Journalism Fellowships 2027/2028
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Journalists and journalism professionals of any nationality with at least five years of experience at editorially independent organisations.
opportunities.description:
The John S. Knight Journalism Fellowships give working journalists, and people whose jobs support journalism, nine months at Stanford University to step back from daily work, learn and think about the problems facing news. The fellowship runs full time and in residence from September to May. Fellows are not asked to deliver a set project, and no university degree is needed to be selected.

Applications for the 2027-28 cohort are open now, and there are separate tracks for US-based and international applicants. The programme is a good fit for African reporters, editors and newsroom managers with solid experience, because it pays a large stipend and covers Stanford tuition and health insurance, so a fellow can take a full academic year away from work.

The fellowship is aimed at people already established in the field. Students, interns, PR staff, government employees and full-time academics are not the intended audience, and applicants must work for media that is editorially independent.
opportunities.benefits: A stipend of US$135,000 for the nine months; Stanford tuition and health insurance; a health supplement for dependants who enrol in Stanford coverage; help with finding housing; coaching and workshops during the year.
requirements: At least five years of professional experience (student work and internships do not count)
Work directly on journalistic content, or in operations or strategy at a news organisation, or at an organisation that supports journalists
Freelancers must earn more than half their work from journalism
Must work for editorially independent organisations
Not open to people seeking a degree, PR or corporate communications staff, government employees or full-time academics
Citizens of countries under a US suspension of J visas cannot be offered a place unless they hold another unrestricted citizenship
documents: Online application form completed in the SurveyMonkey Apply portal
Profile answers that place you in the US or international track
opportunities.selection_process: Applications go through several rounds of review over a few months. A small group of finalists is invited to a Zoom interview. The selection team includes the JSK directors and alumni, and for the US fellowships the JSK Selection Committee.
opportunities.about_provider: JSK is a long-running fellowship programme based at Stanford University in California. It brings together journalists and journalism innovators from the US and around the world each year, with coaching, workshops and access to Stanford courses.

Late applications and extensions are not accepted.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: International secondary-school students with top grades and documented financial need, applying to their first UBC undergraduate degree for September 2027, can apply by 2 December 2026 (12:00 PT).
opportunities.description:
The Karen McKellin International Leader of Tomorrow Award is one of four awards within the University of British Columbia's International Scholars Program. It supports outstanding international students entering UBC directly from secondary school who could not afford a UBC degree without significant help. The award is based on both financial need and merit, so the amount is set after a financial assessment rather than being a fixed sum.

Applicants must have earned superior grades (all As or the equivalent), show leadership and involvement beyond the classroom, and be nominated by their school or a qualifying non-profit organisation. A school can nominate up to two students for UBC Vancouver (including Vantage College) or one for UBC Okanagan.

For African school leavers, this is one of the most generous need-based awards in Canada. The 2027 cycle is open now, with the deadline extended to 2 December 2026.
opportunities.benefits: A need-and-merit award whose value is set by UBC's financial assessment of each student's need; the official page does not give a fixed amount.

Entering UBC directly from an accredited secondary school, graduating no earlier than June 2026
Applying for a first undergraduate degree

Significant documented financial need
Meet UBC admission and English Language Admission Standard by 31 January 2027
Nomination by a school or qualifying non-profit
Not eligible: Nursing, Dental Hygiene, Medical Laboratory Science, Bachelor + Master of Management, dual and joint degrees
