The award is worth CA$1,500 and is open to Canadian citizens, permanent residents and international students. That means African students already studying science or engineering at Concordia in Montreal can apply on the same terms as Canadians.

It is a one-off award for current students rather than an entrance scholarship, so it suits African students in their second year or later who want to have their resilience and results recognised.
opportunities.benefits: A one-time award of CA$1,500.

Full-time in fall 2026 and winter 2027
Canadian citizen, permanent resident or international student

opportunities.title: MCW Global Young Leaders Fellowship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Young people aged 18-26 from any country with fluent English who commit to a year-long community leadership programme.
opportunities.description:
The MCW Global Young Leaders Fellowship is a year-long leadership programme for people aged 18 to 26 who want to tackle problems in their own communities. It runs in three phases: a one-month community needs assessment in June 2027, a 10-day in-person training in New York City and Burlington, Vermont from 20 to 29 July 2027, and then ten months of carrying out a community project with an alumni mentor, ending in July 2028.

Projects focus on education, health or economic security. The programme has no geographic restrictions, so young Africans can apply and then run their projects at home with support from MCW's alumni network.

The first-round deadline is 3 December 2026; a second round closes on 8 January 2027.
opportunities.benefits: Economy return international flights; housing from 19 to 29 July 2027; three meals a day from 20 to 29 July; round-trip travel between New York City and Burlington; mentoring by alumni during the project year. Passport, visa and in-country costs are not covered, and no stipend is mentioned.
requirements: Aged 18 to 26 on 1 June 2027 (no exceptions)
Open to all countries
Fluent written and spoken English
Able to obtain a visa and travel documents
Commitment to all three phases
Reliable email and internet access
documents: Online application in English with two essays (a community issue and a leadership challenge)
Resume of no more than one page
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are reviewed in two rounds, followed by interviews with alumni. MCW warns that answers written with AI tools will hurt an applicant's chances.
important_dates: First-round deadline: 3 December 2026, 11:59 p.m. New York time
opportunities.about_provider: MCW Global is a non-profit based in New York that trains young leaders and supports community projects around the world, with a strong presence in Africa.

opportunities.title: Simons Postdoctoral Fellowships in Plant Biology 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Recent PhD holders of any nationality with a sponsor at a US non-profit institution, doing basic plant biology research.
opportunities.description:
The Simons Postdoctoral Fellowships in Plant Biology fund three years of basic research on fundamental questions in plant biology at a US non-profit university or research institute. The 2027 call supports two kinds of fellow: plant biologists who want to learn new skills from a mentor outside their field, and researchers from other fields who want to bring their expertise to plant biology. Up to two mentors are allowed.

The awards are generous: an US$85,000 annual stipend plus up to US$35,000 a year for research and related costs. Both US citizens and foreign applicants may apply, so African PhD holders who find a US host can compete.

Fellows start between July and October 2027 after decisions in May 2027.
opportunities.benefits: Up to US$360,000 in total over three years: a stipend of US$85,000 per year, an annual allowance of up to US$35,000 (for health insurance, supplies, travel and similar costs) and up to US$2,000 for relocation. No indirect costs are paid.
requirements: PhD (or equivalent) awarded no earlier than three years before the deadline, or expected by the start date
US citizens and foreign nationals may apply
Must be hosted by a US non-profit research university or institution
The sponsor cannot be the applicant's thesis adviser
Only one application per sponsor per year
Cannot hold another postdoctoral fellowship at the same time
documents: Proposal narrative on the Simons template
Sponsor biosketch (max 5 pages) and other-support document
Four confidential letters: thesis adviser, two research scientists and the sponsor
Institutional assurances (IRB, IACUC or biosafety) where relevant
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are reviewed by Simons Foundation scientific staff and an external expert committee.
important_dates: Start: the first of a month between 1 July and 1 October 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The Simons Foundation is a private foundation in New York that funds research in mathematics and the basic sciences. Its Life Sciences division runs this plant biology fellowship.
opportunities.how_to_apply: The applicant creates the application in their own Simons Award Manager (SAM) account at sam.simonsfoundation.org, uploads the documents and arranges the four letters. The host institution's signing official must approve it before final submission by noon Eastern time on 3 December 2026.

opportunities.title: IMF Economist Program (EP) 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: New or near-completion macroeconomics PhDs under 34 from IMF member countries.
opportunities.description:
The IMF Economist Program (EP) is the Fund's entry route for new PhD economists. Recruits join IMF headquarters in Washington, D.C. as economists, starting in September 2027, and spend three years in two different departmental assignments. The IMF stresses that the EP is a regular job, not a training scheme.

Citizens of any IMF member country can apply, which includes every African country that is a Fund member. The programme is a strong career path for African macroeconomists finishing their doctorates.

Applications usually open in late September, with interviews from October to January and offers in early February.
opportunities.benefits: A three-year economist appointment at IMF headquarters; the IMF provides G-4 visa documentation for non-US citizens. Salary is not stated on the posting.
requirements: Recent PhD, or within one year of completing a PhD, in macroeconomics or a related field
Under 34 years old when the programme starts in September 2027 (exception only for mandatory military service)
Citizen of an IMF member country
Excellent written and spoken English
Strong analytical, quantitative and computer skills
documents: Online application on the IMF careers site
If asked after the first interview: PhD transcript, three academic references (not from current IMF staff), and a publishable research paper or one or two dissertation chapters
opportunities.selection_process: A 30-40 minute preliminary interview, then submission of supporting materials, then an in-person panel with senior economists and HR plus a 90-minute written test, and finally an internal committee review. The panel and the research paper weigh most.
opportunities.about_provider: The International Monetary Fund is an organisation of 190 member countries that works on global monetary cooperation, financial stability and economic policy advice.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the 'Economist Program 2027' posting on the IMF Workday careers site. Shortlisted candidates are invited to a preliminary interview and then asked for transcripts, references and a research paper.
opportunities.notes: Apply as early as possible; the posting does not show a fixed closing date.

African applicants with foreign citizenship qualify if they meet the admission requirements and apply through an examination that includes scholarship selection.

Paid in two instalments per year after enrolment; cannot be used for the admission fee or first-semester tuition. Master's tuition is JPY 650,000 per year and the admission fee JPY 200,000.

opportunities.provider: Harvard Center for Population and Development Studies
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Recent or soon-to-be PhD holders of any nationality working on population and development research.
opportunities.description:
The David E. Bell Postdoctoral Fellowship is a two-year fellowship at the Harvard Center for Population and Development Studies in Cambridge, Massachusetts. The call now open is for the 2027-2029 cohort. Fellows carry out their own research on population and development questions in an interdisciplinary setting at Harvard.

The programme is open to both US and international scholars, so African researchers who have recently finished or are about to finish a doctorate can apply. Applicants must have completed, or complete, all doctoral requirements between 13 August 2024 and 13 August 2027.

The fellowship is paid for from sources other than US federal funding.
requirements: Open to US and international scholars
Doctoral requirements completed between 13 August 2024 and 13 August 2027
Proof of degree completion by 13 August 2027
documents: Online application form with eligibility questionnaire and contact details
Three letters of recommendation on letterhead, with a ranking of the applicant
important_dates: Deadline (application and letters): 8 December 2026, 12:00 noon US Eastern time

opportunities.notes: Letters should say how long and in what role the referee knows you, rank you quantitatively (for example top 10%) and comment on writing, analysis, creativity and interdisciplinarity. Contact: popcenter@hsph.harvard.edu.

opportunities.title: Exeter EPSRC Doctoral Landscape Award Studentships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduates with a first or 2:1 (or equivalent) in science, engineering or technology, from the UK or abroad, applying to a listed Exeter PhD project.
opportunities.description:
The University of Exeter is offering up to 16 fully funded PhD studentships for September 2027 under its EPSRC Doctoral Landscape Award. Each studentship is tied to a listed research project in science, engineering or technology, and lasts up to three and a half years of full-time study.

Up to 30 per cent of places can go to international candidates, including Africans. International award holders have their full tuition covered through the home fee rate plus an Exeter fee waiver, and they receive the same stipend and research budget as UK students.

Applicants choose a project from Exeter's list and apply through the link in that project's description.
opportunities.benefits: Full tuition fees; an index-linked stipend for up to 3.5 years (currently £21,805 per year for 2026/27); a research training support grant of £5,000 over 3.5 years. International students pay their own visa, health surcharge and relocation costs.
requirements: First or upper second-class UK honours degree (or equivalent) in a relevant science, engineering or technology subject
Lower second considered with a master's degree or significant relevant experience
Home or international fee status (international places capped at about 30%)
Proof of English for nationals of non-majority-English-speaking countries
Some projects set extra requirements
documents: Personal statement naming the project at the top
Two references emailed by referees from institutional addresses to PGRApplicants@exeter.ac.uk
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are shortlisted, and shortlisted candidates are interviewed in February 2027. Offers are made in early March 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Exeter is a research-intensive UK university in south-west England and a member of the Russell Group. The Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council (EPSRC), part of UK Research and Innovation, funds the Doctoral Landscape Award.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Find a project on Exeter's EPSRC DLA project list, then apply only through the application link at the bottom of that project's PDF before midday on 8 December 2026. Applications sent by other routes are not considered.
opportunities.notes: Put the project title at the top of your personal statement and name each PDF with your surname. The official page mixes 2026 and 2027 in a few dates; the 2027 cycle is intended.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: New self-funded applicants to IUJ master's and PhD programmes in international relations and management.
opportunities.description:
The S. Nakayama Memorial Scholarship is the International University of Japan's own merit award for new self-funded students in its Graduate School of International Relations and Graduate School of International Management. Awards are made competitively at the time of admission and come in several tiers.

The top tier, Nakayama Premium, covers all tuition, part of the admission fee and pays a monthly stipend of JPY 100,000. Other tiers cover 100%, 90%, 70%, 50% or 30% of tuition.

IUJ teaches in English in rural Niigata and has a large share of international students, so the scholarship is a realistic route for African graduates to a Japanese master's or PhD in international relations, public management, economics or business.
opportunities.benefits: Nakayama Premium: 100% tuition, partial admission fee and JPY 100,000 per month. Nakayama 100/90/70/50/30: that percentage of tuition. For reference, tuition is JPY 3,200,000 per year (two-year programmes) and the admission fee JPY 300,000.

Most IUJ scholarships require holding a Japanese student visa
documents: IUJ online application with the scholarship section completed in Phase 2
opportunities.selection_process: Awarded competitively at the time of admission.
opportunities.about_provider: The International University of Japan (IUJ) is a private English-medium graduate university in Minamiuonuma, Niigata, focused on international relations and management.

Another stream, Doctoral Access Pathway (up to 3 places), is for applicants who identify as Black or of Black heritage, of any nationality.

For African researchers this is one of the few UK doctoral schemes that funds international fees in full. Deadlines are strict and early: the course application must be in by 7 December 2026 and the scholarship application by 10 December 2026, both at 16:59 UK time.
opportunities.benefits: Full academic fees and a tax-free maintenance stipend, with up to 8 weeks' annual leave. Faculty Chancellors' scholars receive the UKRI-rate stipend for 3.5 years and a £5,000 Research Training and Support Grant. Visa cost support is available to eligible international applicants.
requirements: Apply for an eligible Warwick research degree starting October 2027
Any nationality and fee status (Faculty Chancellors' stream)
Not a current Warwick postgraduate research student
Doctoral Access Pathway: self-identify as Black or of Black heritage
China Scholarship Council stream: PRC passport holders only
documents: Scholarship application in the Warwick scholarships portal
Supporting documents uploaded to the portal

opportunities.about_provider: Bangor University is a public university in north Wales, UK, known for environmental sciences, psychology and ocean sciences among other fields.
opportunities.how_to_apply: First obtain an offer from Bangor, then complete the online scholarship application form linked from the Vice-Chancellor Scholarships page before the deadline for your intake. Winners must return an acceptance form and tuition deposit within two weeks.
opportunities.notes: Only one award is available per level for January 2027, so competition is tight; the September 2027 round has ten awards per level. Undergraduate winners must make Bangor their firm choice.

opportunities.title: ESRC South East Doctoral Training Arc (SEDarc) Studentships
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants of any nationality with a social-science project that fits a SEDarc theme can apply for an October 2027 PhD at Reading, but international candidates must fund the gap between UK and international fees.
opportunities.description:
The South East Doctoral Training Arc (SEDarc) is a doctoral training partnership funded by the UK Economic and Social Research Council (ESRC). It brings together six universities, Royal Holloway, Kent, Kingston, Reading, Surrey and Sussex, and funds social-science PhDs that start in October 2027. This entry follows the University of Reading route, where candidates first apply to Reading and are then nominated to the partnership.

Projects must fit one of five SEDarc themes, such as Inclusive Economic Growth or Living Sustainably, and subjects include Economics, Education, Human Geography, Linguistics, and Politics and International Relations. A studentship lasts 3.5 years with a three-month placement, or 3.25 years without one, and some awards add a master's year for applicants who do not already hold a social-science master's.

For African applicants the award is a route into a fully structured UK PhD with a stipend, but it is important to plan finances carefully: the ESRC covers only the UK-rate fee, so international students must find the difference themselves.
opportunities.benefits: Tuition at the UK (home) rate; the UKRI stipend of £21,805 a year (2026/27 rate); a £1,000 travel fund for the placement. International students must pay the difference between home and international fees themselves (about £16,512 to £19,212 a year at 2026/27 rates). Visa costs and the NHS surcharge are not covered.
requirements: Open to UK and international applicants
Research project that fits one of the five SEDarc themes
Social-science subject area (e.g. economics, education, human geography, linguistics, politics and IR)
International candidates must fund the gap between UK and international fees
No more than 30% of SEDarc awards go to international students
documents: University of Reading PhD application via the RISIS portal
SEDarc application template (supplied to nominated candidates)
opportunities.selection_process: Candidates first talk to the relevant academic at Reading and apply for a Reading PhD with a draft proposal. Reading then nominates its strongest candidates, who submit a full application to SEDarc for a partnership-wide competition. Outcomes are expected in April 2027.
important_dates: Expressions of interest: end of November 2026
Final SEDarc applications from nominees: 29 January 2027
opportunities.about_provider: SEDarc is one of the ESRC's doctoral training partnerships in England, linking six universities in the south east to train social scientists. The University of Reading is a research-intensive UK university and one of the partners.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Contact the subject academic listed on the Reading page about your project, then apply for a PhD at Reading through the RISIS portal with a draft SEDarc proposal by 11 December 2026. If Reading nominates you, complete the SEDarc application template by 29 January 2027.
opportunities.notes: Reading's site also lists AHRC Doctoral Landscape Awards and Centenary PhD Bursaries, which may suit humanities applicants.

opportunities.title: FANE Research Support Fund for Master's Students (Université Sainte-Anne) 2026
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Full-time Canadian or international students starting their master's thesis in francophone cultures at Université Sainte-Anne can apply by 11 December 2026 for a one-off $3,500 research award.
opportunities.description:
The Fédération acadienne de la Nouvelle-Écosse (FANE) funds a research award at Université Sainte-Anne for a master's student who is beginning to write a thesis on a contemporary issue facing Acadian society. The award is a single, non-renewable grant of $3,500.

It is linked to the university's Master of Arts in francophone cultures and spaces (Maîtrise en cultures et espaces francophones). Projects focused on Acadian Nova Scotia get priority, but comparative approaches are welcome, which can suit international students who compare Acadian issues with francophone communities elsewhere, including in Africa.

The award is open to both Canadian and international students, so it is mainly relevant to African francophone students who are already enrolled, or about to enrol, in this master's programme.
opportunities.benefits: A one-off research award of $3,500 (not renewable).
requirements: Full-time student at Université Sainte-Anne
At the start of writing the master's thesis (MA cultures et espaces francophones)
Research on a contemporary issue in Acadian society; Nova Scotia Acadian projects prioritised
Canadian and international students eligible
Mandatory master's coursework completed
documents: Letter of intent of up to two pages (project, methodology, progress, how the award helps)
Letter of support from the thesis director
Transcript showing completion of the mandatory master's courses
opportunities.selection_process: A committee reviews the applications and selects one recipient.
opportunities.about_provider: Université Sainte-Anne is Nova Scotia's only French-language university, with its main campus at Church Point. It serves Acadian and francophone communities in Atlantic Canada and welcomes many students from francophone Africa.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Email the letter of intent, the thesis director's support letter and the transcript to the coordinator of the Maîtrise en cultures et espaces francophones before the deadline. The university's recruitment office (1-888-338-8337) can supply the coordinator's contact.
opportunities.notes: This is a small internal award for enrolled students rather than an entrance scholarship.

opportunities.title: Postgraduate Research Scholarship in Transnational Musical Exchange
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants with an unconditional offer for, or enrolment in, a full-time PhD or DMA at the Sydney Conservatorium of Music can apply for this stipend and fee scholarship in transnational musical exchange.
opportunities.description:
The University of Sydney offers a postgraduate research scholarship for a doctoral project on transnational musical exchange at the Sydney Conservatorium of Music. The award is funded by the George Wallace Henderson Bequest.

It pays a living stipend and, for international students, course fees for up to three years. The successful candidate works under one of three named lead supervisors (Coady, Harris or Case), so the project needs to fit their research.

No nationality restriction is stated, so African musicians and musicologists with a strong research proposal can compete.
opportunities.benefits: Stipend at the Research Training Program (RTP) rate for up to 12 research periods (three years) and, for international applicants, course fees for the same period. No other payments are made.
requirements: Unconditional offer of admission or current full-time enrolment in a PhD or DMA at the Sydney Conservatorium
Master's by research, a coursework master's with a substantial research component, or a bachelor's with First Class Honours
Must choose a lead supervisor from Coady, Harris or Case
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants are assessed on academic merit, the research proposal, CV and referee reports, followed by an interview; the nomination is made by Associate Professor Coady.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Sydney is Australia's oldest university and a member of the Group of Eight. The Sydney Conservatorium of Music is its music school.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for PhD or DMA admission at the Sydney Conservatorium, then complete the scholarship's online form linked from the official page, attaching the research proposal and CV and arranging two referee reports.

opportunities.title: Sophia University New Student and Benefactors' Scholarships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants to Sophia University's English-taught degree programmes who will hold a Student visa, have strong grades and need financial help can apply; the Adachi award is reserved for students from listed countries including several African ones.
opportunities.description:
Sophia University in Tokyo runs two first-year tuition scholarships for new international students in its English-taught programmes: the New Student Scholarship and the Benefactors' (Adachi) Scholarship. Both aim to help academically strong students who have chosen Sophia as their first choice but face financial difficulty.

The New Student Scholarship reduces first-year tuition by one third, one half or the full amount and is open to any nationality. The Adachi Scholarship pays full first-year tuition plus the education enhancement fee and is reserved for students from a list of Southeast Asian and African countries, among them Ethiopia, Ghana, Kenya, Nigeria, Mozambique and South Africa.

The undergraduate window covers the Autumn 2027 intake and the second Spring 2027 round, while graduate applicants have separate windows. For African students admitted to an English-taught programme, the Adachi award can remove the full cost of the first year's tuition.
opportunities.benefits: New Student Scholarship: one third, half or all of first-year tuition. Adachi Scholarship: full first-year tuition plus the education enhancement fee. Entrance and enrolment fees are not covered, and both awards apply to the first year only.
requirements: Applicant to one of Sophia's English-taught undergraduate or graduate programmes listed on the page
Must hold a Student visa at admission
Excellent academic record
Demonstrated financial hardship
Adachi award: citizen of one of the listed Southeast Asian or African countries
documents: Typed scholarship application form with signed pledge
Income certificate of the financial supporter for 2025, in English or Japanese
Applicants whose families live in Japan: original residence, tax and enrolment certificates
opportunities.selection_process: Sophia screens the documents and decides on the basis of the applicant's financial situation and academic grades.
important_dates: Undergraduate (Autumn 2027 and second-round Spring 2027): 11 November to 11 December 2026
Autumn 2027 graduate and transfer applicants: 10 March to 7 April 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Sophia University is a private Jesuit university in central Tokyo, known for its international programmes taught in English. Its Center for Student Affairs administers the scholarships.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Complete the scholarship form and gather the financial documents, then post them to the Center for Student Affairs by registered mail or EMS, separately from your admission documents. Email submission is accepted only if postal service is unavailable; questions go to scholarship-co@sophia.ac.jp.
opportunities.notes: Late applications are not accepted. The awards cover only the first year, so plan funding for later years.

opportunities.title: WGSSS ESRC Doctoral Studentships 2027
opportunities.provider: Welsh Graduate School for the Social Sciences (ESRC)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants with a first or upper-second UK-equivalent degree or a master's can apply for a WGSSS ESRC social-science PhD at the University of South Wales starting October 2027; up to 30% of the cohort may be international.
opportunities.description:
The Wales Graduate School for the Social Sciences (WGSSS) is the ESRC-funded doctoral training partnership for Wales. Through the University of South Wales it offers studentships starting in October 2027 in two pathways: Social Care, Social Work and Social Policy, and Law and Criminology.

The award runs for 3.5 years as a PhD, or as a 1+3.5 model with a master's first, and includes a compulsory three-month Research in Practice placement. Unlike some UK doctoral awards, international students are not charged the difference between UK and international fees.

This makes it one of the few UK social-science doctoral awards that can be fully funded for African applicants, although competition is strong because no more than 30% of the cohort can be international.
opportunities.benefits: Full tuition fees (international students are not charged the UK/international fee difference); a stipend at the UKRI minimum rate (£21,805 a year full-time in 2026/27); a Research Training Support Grant.
requirements: First or upper-second class UK honours degree or equivalent, or a master's degree
Meet UKRI eligibility rules (up to 30% of the cohort may be international)
Social-science project fitting the Social Care/Social Work/Social Policy or Law and Criminology pathway
English language proof where relevant
Applicants from non-traditional backgrounds are welcome
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are shortlisted, and shortlisted candidates are interviewed, giving a short presentation and answering panel questions.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of South Wales is a public university with campuses in Cardiff, Newport and Pontypridd. WGSSS is the ESRC's doctoral training partnership for Welsh universities.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Download the WGSSS application form from the University of South Wales funded-studentships page, complete it with your CV, transcripts and other documents, and arrange two references. Submit everything by 11 December 2026.
opportunities.notes: Incomplete applications are not considered. The same page lists AHRC Doctoral Landscape Awards (closing 31 January 2027) and a Welsh-medium psychology PhD.

opportunities.title: Sciences Po Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: African citizens under 35 without a master's degree, holding a bachelor's from a partner institution (or from a bridge programme, or with refugee status), can apply for full support for a two-year master's at Sciences Po.
opportunities.description:
The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at Sciences Po funds students from the African continent through a two-year master's degree at Sciences Po in Paris. It is a partnership between Sciences Po and the Mastercard Foundation, which supports young Africans committed to transforming their communities.

The programme covers the scholar's full financial needs during the master's and adds leadership development and mentoring. Applicants must first check their eligibility on the programme platform and then apply for a Sciences Po master's, choosing one of two deadlines depending on when they want their admission decision.

Selection looks beyond grades to the barriers the applicant has overcome, their commitment to Africa's development and their leadership potential.
opportunities.benefits: Full financial support for the two-year master's according to the scholar's needs (the official page does not give amounts), plus a waiver of the Sciences Po application fee.
requirements: Citizen of an African country (dual citizenship with a non-African country is not eligible)
Bachelor's degree from a listed partner institution, or completion of a bridge or mentoring programme, or UNHCR refugee status
Under 35 on 1 September of the year of application
No existing master's degree and first application to this programme
Not a current Sciences Po student or graduate of French higher education
Meet the minimum academic requirements and be admitted to a two-year Sciences Po master's (dual degrees, one-year master's and journalism excluded)
documents: Passport, national ID, UNHCR card or travel document
Bachelor's certificate or proof of current studies
Proof of refugee status if applicable
Written assignments set by the programme
opportunities.selection_process: Eligible applicants complete written assignments and a Zoom interview of about 25 minutes. Deadline for a master's decision by 1 April 2027: 14 December 2026

Submit everything before your chosen deadline; questions go to info.mcfsp@sciencespo.fr.
opportunities.notes: Scholarship offers are valid only for the academic year in which they are made.

opportunities.title: Surrey Business School PhD Fee-Waiver Studentships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK and international applicants who meet the entry requirements for Surrey Business School's PhD programmes can apply for a full fee waiver for an April 2027 start.
opportunities.description:
Surrey Business School at the University of Surrey offers PhD fee-waiver studentships for doctoral study starting on 1 April 2027. The awards are for the PhD in Management and Business and the PhD in Hospitality, Tourism, Transport and Events.

The studentship removes the full tuition fee, at the home or international rate, for 36 months full-time or 72 months part-time, and adds a small research training grant. It does not include a living stipend.

African applicants can apply on the same terms as UK candidates, but they need their own funding for living costs and visa expenses.
opportunities.benefits: Full waiver of home or international tuition fees for 36 months (72 part-time) and a research training grant of £750 a year (up to £2,250). No stipend, visa or accommodation support.
requirements: Open to UK and international candidates
Meet the entry requirements for the Management and Business PhD or the Hospitality, Tourism, Transport and Events PhD
Two supervisors from Surrey, with the primary supervisor in Surrey Business School
Start on 1 April 2027 (no deferral)
documents: Fee-waiver application form (DOCX) signed off by the proposed supervisors
Research proposal of up to 3,000 words
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are scored on the quality of the research proposal (60%) and the quality of the applicant (40%). Outcomes are expected by the end of February 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Surrey is a research university in Guildford, England. Surrey Business School is its business faculty, with research in management, hospitality, tourism and transport.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Find two Surrey supervisors, complete the fee-waiver form with their sign-off, submit an online PhD application and upload the form, then email it to the programme contact named in the guidance notes. All five steps must be finished by 14 December 2026 at 16:00 GMT.

opportunities.title: Toshizo Watanabe International Scholarship FY2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Students with a refugee background who live in Japan (or arrive through complementary pathways) and are, or will be, admitted to a Japanese university can apply for this need-based scholarship.
opportunities.description:
The Toshizo Watanabe International Scholarship (TWIS) is a donor-funded award administered by Pathways Japan, an NGO that supports refugee education. The FY2027 round helps students with a refugee background to study at Japanese universities and graduate schools.

It is a grant, not a loan: it pays tuition up to a set limit and a monthly living subsidy that varies with the year of study. Eligibility depends on refugee background and residence status in Japan rather than on nationality, so African refugees living in Japan can apply.

Applicants who live outside Japan cannot apply, unless they are admitted through one of the complementary pathways the programme recognises.
opportunities.benefits: Tuition up to ¥1,700,000 a year (decided case by case) and a monthly living subsidy of up to ¥70,000 (undergraduate years 1-2), ¥60,000 (year 3) or ¥50,000 (year 4 and graduate study). No repayment is required.
requirements: Refugee background, living in Japan with a qualifying status (for example Student or Designated Activities), or admitted through a complementary pathway, or unable to return home because of conflict
12 years of schooling
Demonstrated financial need
Japanese-medium undergraduate study: EJU/JLPT results; other programmes: an English test plus JLPT N4
Accepted, or expecting acceptance, at a Japanese university or graduate school
opportunities.selection_process: Pathways Japan screens the documents, then interviews shortlisted applicants in Tokyo or online.
opportunities.about_provider: Pathways Japan is a non-profit organisation that creates education pathways in Japan for refugees and displaced students. It manages the Toshizo Watanabe scholarship on behalf of its donor.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Read the FY2027 guidelines and FAQ on the Pathways Japan site, then submit the online application linked from the official page with the supporting documents before 14 December 2026. Shortlisted applicants are invited to an interview.
opportunities.notes: Applicants living outside Japan generally cannot apply. Check the official page for the exact steps, since one step mentions 12 January.

opportunities.title: EADA International Master's Scholarships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Admitted applicants to EADA's international master's programmes in Barcelona can apply for scholarships covering 10-35% of tuition, including an Africa Scholarship.
opportunities.description:
EADA Business School in Barcelona offers scholarships to applicants to its international master's programmes, such as the Master in Management and the Master in AI for Business. The awards reduce tuition and are decided alongside the admission decision.

Most scholarships cover 10 to 25% of tuition, the Scholarship for Excellence can reach 35%, and the diversity scholarships, which include an Africa Scholarship, cover up to 25%. The Master in Management costs €28,000, so the awards can make a real difference for self-funded African students.

Scholarships are awarded in rounds through the year, with earlier rounds for the January 2027 intake and later rounds for October 2027.
opportunities.benefits: Tuition reductions of 10-25%, up to 35% for the Scholarship for Excellence and up to 25% for diversity scholarships (including the Africa Scholarship). Living costs are not covered.
requirements: Complete EADA's admission process first
Programme aimed at talented candidates aged roughly 21-25
Excellence award: outstanding academic record or GMAT 700+
Enrol within 10 working days of the award and take part in an EADA project
Apply for at most two scholarships and receive at most one

important_dates: January 2027 intake: rounds closing 15 November and 15 December 2026
October 2027 intake: 20 December 2026 (MBA diversity only), then 20 January, 20 February, 20 March, 20 April, 20 May and 20 June 2027 (while funds last)
opportunities.about_provider: EADA Business School is a private business school in Barcelona, Spain, known for its management and MBA programmes with a strong international student body.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit the scholarship form with your master's application and email the documents to EADA admissions before the round's deadline. You receive the scholarship decision together with your admission result.

opportunities.title: ENS-PSL International Selection in Sciences 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International students under 26 who have completed at least one year of undergraduate study abroad can apply to enter ENS-PSL at L3 or M1 level with a monthly grant.
opportunities.description:
The École normale supérieure (ENS-PSL) in Paris runs an International Selection that admits a small number of foreign students each year into its diploma programme in the sciences. Successful candidates join at third-year bachelor's (L3) or first-year master's (M1) level.

Winners receive a grant of €1,000 a month for 36 months and can ask for a room in an ENS residence. Selection is highly competitive, with only 5 to 10% of candidates admitted, and includes a scientific oral exam and an interview.

For African students with outstanding science records, the selection offers a funded route into one of France's most prestigious research schools.
opportunities.benefits: A grant of €1,000 per month for 36 months, plus the option to request a room in an ENS campus residence.
requirements: Under 26 years old on the day applications open
At least one year of undergraduate study at a foreign university, and two years completed by enrolment
No registration in French higher education for more than six months in the competition year or the year before
Must not have applied before
Entry at L3 or M1 level
documents: Argued cover letter of 1-3 pages (Times New Roman 12, 1.5 spacing)
Two to four recommendation letters requested through the platform
opportunities.selection_process: A jury shortlists candidates from their files, then holds a scientific oral exam (weight 6) and an interview (weight 3). About 5-10% of applicants are selected.
important_dates: Applications: 16 October to 15 December 2026, 14:00 Paris time
opportunities.about_provider: ENS-PSL is a French grande école focused on research and teaching, part of Université PSL in Paris. It trains researchers and teachers across sciences and humanities.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply on the OnePSL30 platform (concoursens.candidature.onepsl30.fr), upload your documents and request your recommendation letters through the platform before the deadline.
opportunities.notes: Do not use an icloud.com email address. Incomplete applications are rejected. The same page covers an Arts and Humanities track, which requires French at B1.

opportunities.title: Folger Long-Term Public Humanities Fellowship 2027-28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Scholars, artists, writers, educators, community leaders and doctoral candidates of any nationality with a public humanities project on the early modern world can apply for a nine-month residential fellowship in Washington DC.
opportunities.description:
The Folger Shakespeare Library offers Long-term Public Humanities Fellowships for 2027-28 through its Folger Institute. They support projects that combine research on the early modern world, roughly 1400 to 1800, with public engagement.

Fellows receive $70,000 for a standard nine-month period in residence in Washington DC, of which up to three months may be spent working virtually. Each fellow must plan at least one public humanities activity developed with Folger staff, such as a programme, performance or exhibition.

No terminal degree is required and there is no nationality restriction, so African writers, artists and scholars whose work engages early modern history or literature can apply.
opportunities.benefits: $70,000 for a nine-month fellowship, intended to cover travel, housing and living costs; up to three months may be virtual.
requirements: Faculty, independent scholar, artist, writer, PhD candidate, postdoc, community leader, educator or similar
A terminal degree is not required, but equivalent training must be described
Project on the early modern world that uses Folger collections
At least one public humanities engagement developed with Folger staff
documents: Project description of up to 1,500 words, including the public humanities plan and any virtual time
List of Folger primary sources to be used (1-2 pages)
One recommendation letter submitted through the portal
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are reviewed by the Folger Institute; details of the criteria are in the fellowships FAQ.
opportunities.about_provider: The Folger Shakespeare Library in Washington DC holds one of the world's largest collections of early modern books and manuscripts. Its Folger Institute runs fellowships and scholarly programmes.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the Folger fellowships portal (onlineapplicationportal.com/folgerfellowships) with your abstract, project description, CV and source list, and ask your referee to upload a letter. Questions go to Ashley Buchanan (abuchanan@folger.edu).
opportunities.notes: The Folger does not provide studio space or archive the resulting materials; check the current COVID vaccination policy.

opportunities.title: Folger Long-Term Scholarly Fellowship 2027-28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Scholars of any nationality who hold a terminal degree can apply for a year-long or semester-long residential fellowship at the Folger Shakespeare Library for 2027-28.
opportunities.description:
The Folger Shakespeare Library's Long-term Scholarly Fellowships support advanced research on the early modern world using the Folger's collections in Washington DC. The 2027-28 round offers a year-long (nine-month) or a semester-long (five-month) fellowship.

The year-long award pays $70,000 and the semester-long award $35,000, with some time allowed virtually. Fellows join a scholarly community at the library and can stay in Folger housing or arrange their own.

There is no nationality restriction, so African historians and literary scholars with a doctorate can apply.
opportunities.benefits: Year-long fellowship (nine months): $70,000, with up to three months virtual. Semester-long fellowship (five months): $35,000, with up to one month virtual. The award is meant to cover travel, housing and living costs.
requirements: Terminal degree in the applicant's field
Research project that makes substantial use of Folger collections
Apply for either the year-long or the semester-long term, not both
documents: Project description of up to 1,500 words
List of primary sources or digital assets to be used (1-2 pages)
opportunities.selection_process: Proposals are judged on impact, relevance, originality and sophistication, feasibility and expected use of the Folger collections, with impact, relevance and approach weighed most heavily.
opportunities.about_provider: The Folger Shakespeare Library in Washington DC is a research library with one of the world's major collections of early modern materials. The Folger Institute manages its fellowships.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit the application through the Folger fellowships portal, choosing one fellowship term, and arrange for one recommendation letter. The portal opened on 15 September 2026.

opportunities.title: Harvard Scholars at Risk Fellowship 2027-2028
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Scholars, writers, artists and independent intellectuals who face persecution because of their beliefs, scholarship or identity, and who are not US citizens or permanent residents, can apply or be nominated.
opportunities.description:
Harvard's Scholars at Risk Program offers fellowships that let threatened academics and intellectuals spend up to ten months or a year at Harvard. Fellows continue their work in safety while the university hosts them.

The fellowship provides a stipend, insurance and travel, with the amounts set according to where the scholar is coming from and how many dependants they bring. It is not a degree programme, and fellows are expected either to return home or to find a longer-term placement afterwards.

African scholars who are at risk because of their research, beliefs or identity can apply directly or be nominated by someone else.
opportunities.benefits: A stipend, health insurance and travel costs, with amounts that depend on the scholar's location and number of dependants; no fixed amounts are published.

opportunities.title: Politecnico di Milano Merit-Based Scholarships for International MSc Students 2027-2028
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International students admitted to the first year of an English-taught MSc at Politecnico di Milano for 2027-28, who paid the application fee by 1 December 2026, can apply for one of 64 merit awards by 15 December 2026.
opportunities.description:
Politecnico di Milano, Italy's largest technical university, offers 64 merit-based scholarships to international students entering the first year of its English-taught Laurea Magistrale (MSc) programmes in the 2027-2028 academic year. The awards cover programmes on the Milan campus and on the regional campuses of Piacenza, Cremona, Lecco and Mantova.

Every award includes a waiver of the tuition fee, and most also pay a cash grant of EUR 2,500 to EUR 10,000 for the year. The application window ran from 1 October 2026 and closes at 12:00 noon Italian time on 15 December 2026; to qualify, students must have applied for admission and paid the application fee between 1 October and 1 December 2026.

The scholarships are a good fit for African engineering, architecture and design graduates who want a well-ranked European technical degree at moderate cost. Priority is given to students from countries affected by war or civil conflict, and the commission also considers geographic balance and gender balance.
opportunities.benefits: All awards waive the tuition fee for the year (students still pay an administrative fee of about EUR 170-190 and insurance). Platinum (10 awards, Milan): EUR 10,000 gross paid in two instalments of EUR 5,000. Gold (18, Milan): EUR 8,000 gross in two instalments. Gold Piacenza (16; SAL, LLH and RES programmes): EUR 5,000 gross in two instalments. Bronze (10, Piacenza; Mechanical Engineering and Mechatronics for Manufacturing): EUR 2,500 in one payment. Silver (10; Cremona, Lecco, Mantova and Piacenza): tuition waiver only. Awards can be renewed for year two if the student earns 1,000 points (Platinum) or 700 points (other awards) by 10 August 2028.
requirements: International student
Admitted to the first year of an English-taught MSc (Laurea Magistrale) for 2027-2028
MSc application fee paid between 1 October and 1 December 2026
Strong grade average and academic record
Valid English language certificate, verified by the International Students Office (by 4 March 2027 according to the page)
documents: Scholarship application form in Politecnico Online Services
Academic transcripts and degree documents from the MSc application
opportunities.selection_process: A university commission ranks candidates on academic merit (grade average and achievements), how well their previous studies match the chosen MSc, their documents and the form. Priority goes to students from countries affected by military aggression or civil war, and geographic origin, gender balance and age are also considered. Results come three to four months after the deadline.
important_dates: MSc application fee paid by: 1 December 2026
Scholarship form deadline: 15 December 2026, 12:00 noon Italian time
Results: about three to four months after the deadline
opportunities.about_provider: Politecnico di Milano is a public science and technology university founded in 1863, with campuses in Milan and several Lombardy and Emilia-Romagna cities. It teaches engineering, architecture and design and runs many MSc programmes entirely in English.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for admission to an English-taught MSc on the Politecnico Online Services portal and pay the application fee by 1 December 2026. Then fill in the merit-based scholarship form in the same portal before 12:00 noon Italian time on 15 December 2026. Questions go to international-scholarships@polimi.it.
opportunities.notes: The page and the official call give slightly different administrative fees (about EUR 170 versus about EUR 190). Egyptian, Ethiopian, Ghanaian and Tunisian students can also look at the Italian government's Invest Your Talent in Italy scheme.

opportunities.description:
The Institute of Formal and Applied Linguistics (ÚFAL) at Charles University in Prague offers pre-PhD research internships to students who are thinking about doctoral study in computational linguistics. The spring session runs roughly from March to May 2027.

Interns spend one to three months at ÚFAL as visitors, working with a supervisor on a research topic, and are expected to aim for a joint publication. Two sessions run each year, with one intern selected per session, and a successful internship counts in the candidate's favour in later PhD admission.

For African students interested in language technology, this is a supported way to test a research career in a leading European NLP group.
opportunities.benefits: Travel costs up to 15,000 CZK and accommodation up to 8,000 CZK per month (or actual costs if lower); a bonus may be paid at ÚFAL's discretion.
requirements: Master's degree completed or nearly completed
Excellent computer-science background and programming experience
Interest in NLP, machine learning, AI, data mining or music information retrieval
documents: CV naming your programme and university
Transcript with grades and the grading scale
Proposed topics or project proposal and preferred supervisors
opportunities.selection_process: ÚFAL reviews the applications and selects one intern per session.
important_dates: Internship period: roughly March to May 2027
opportunities.about_provider: ÚFAL is part of the Faculty of Mathematics and Physics at Charles University in Prague and is one of Europe's major centres for computational linguistics and natural language processing.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Fill in the online application form linked from the ÚFAL internships page, in English, with your CV, transcript and research interests. It helps to agree a possible supervisor first.
opportunities.notes: Emails asking whether your profile is good enough are not answered. Contact: zabokrtsky@ufal.mff.cuni.cz.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers of any nationality who completed, or will complete, a doctorate between June 2025 and September 2027 can apply for a two-year engineering postdoc at Notre Dame.
opportunities.description:
The University of Notre Dame's Provost's Postdoctoral Fellowships in Engineering fund early-career researchers for two years in the College of Engineering. Fellows design their own research with a primary mentor from the college and a co-mentor.

The fellowship pays a $75,000 annual stipend and a $15,000 allowance for research, training and professional development. Scholars of all nationalities can apply, which makes it open to African engineers who have recently finished, or are about to finish, a PhD.

The programme aims to develop future leaders in engineering research, so applicants need a clear research plan at the forefront of their field.
opportunities.benefits: A stipend of $75,000 a year for 24 months plus a $15,000 allowance for research, training and professional development.
requirements: Doctorate completed or expected between June 2025 and September 2027 (earlier dates allowed after parental or medical leave in the past two years)
Open to scholars of all nationalities
Primary mentor from the College of Engineering

PDF of up to five slides

opportunities.selection_process: Applicants are judged on scientific excellence and on a clear research plan at the forefront of engineering. Decisions are made by 31 March 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Notre Dame is a private research university in Indiana, USA. Its College of Engineering runs research across aerospace, chemical, civil, computer, electrical and mechanical engineering.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Agree a primary mentor in the College of Engineering and a co-mentor, then apply through the programme's Interfolio posting with your CV, research statement, slides and three letters, which referees upload directly.
opportunities.notes: Applicants whose mentor is in the College of Science should apply to the Society of Science Fellows instead. Contact: eng-postdocs@nd.edu.

opportunities.description:
The Undergraduate Scholars Entrance Scholarships are Simon Fraser University's main merit awards for students coming straight from high school. Both Canadian and international students can apply, and international winners can receive up to $140,000 across their degree.

There is no nationality rule, so African secondary-school students applying to SFU for fall entry can compete. A living allowance may be added for winners who show financial need. The application window opened on 1 October 2026 and closes on 15 December 2026.
opportunities.benefits: Entrance scholarships worth up to $140,000 for international students (from $20,000 up to $60,000 for domestic students). A living allowance may also be offered to students with demonstrated financial need.

Academic and extracurricular excellence

opportunities.about_provider: Simon Fraser University is a public research university in British Columbia, Canada, with campuses in Burnaby, Vancouver and Surrey. It is regularly ranked among Canada's leading comprehensive universities.

opportunities.provider: Graduate Association for African American History, University of Memphis
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduate and undergraduate students working on any topic in Black Studies can submit a paper or panel proposal by 18 December 2026 for the GAAAH conference in Memphis, 24-26 February 2027.
opportunities.description:
The Graduate Association for African American History (GAAAH) at the University of Memphis is inviting proposals for its 2027 annual conference, themed "Under Siege but Undefeated: Countering the Erasure of Black History". The conference takes place from 24 to 26 February 2027 at the Maxine A. Smith University Center on the Memphis campus in Tennessee, with historian and writer Dr Clint Smith as keynote speaker.

The organisers welcome papers on any subject within Black Studies, from any discipline and using any method, which makes the call relevant to students researching Africa, the African diaspora and transatlantic Black history. Both individual papers and complete panels can be proposed.

The meeting is run by graduate students for graduate and undergraduate presenters, so it is a supportive first conference for early researchers. Limited travel funding is available from the university's African and African American Studies programme on a first-come, first-served basis.
opportunities.benefits: Limited travel funding from the University of Memphis African and African American Studies (AAAS) Program, given first-come, first-served; no amounts are published. No registration fee is mentioned in the call.

opportunities.title: World Physiotherapy Congress 2027 Bursary (Guadalajara)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Qualified physiotherapists who are nationals and residents of a low or lower-middle income country whose national association pays World Physiotherapy's reduced membership fee can apply by 21 December 2026 for a bursary to attend the 2027 congress in Mexico.
opportunities.description:
World Physiotherapy offers a limited number of bursaries so that physiotherapists from low and lower-middle income countries can attend the World Physiotherapy Congress 2027, held in Guadalajara, Mexico, from 14 to 16 May 2027. The congress, hosted with the Mexican physiotherapy association AMEFI, is the main global meeting of the profession, with three days of scientific sessions, networking and professional development.

A bursary can be full or partial and pays the main costs of attending, from travel and hotel to registration and visa. Applicants do not need an accepted abstract. The application form closes at 23:59 UTC on 21 December 2026, and applicants are told the outcome in February 2027.

The award is designed for physiotherapists who will bring what they learn back to their workplace and country, so it suits African clinicians, educators and postgraduate physiotherapy students whose national association is a World Physiotherapy member paying the reduced fee.
opportunities.benefits: Full or partial support covering an economy return flight or ground transport, four nights' hotel with breakfast, full three-day congress registration, an allowance of USD 60 for local transport and meals, travel insurance, the visa fee and a social event ticket where applicable. Extra events, personal expenses and travel to embassies are not covered.
requirements: Qualified physiotherapist who is employed or enrolled in a relevant postgraduate programme (entry-level students are not eligible)
Member in good standing of a World Physiotherapy member organisation
National and resident of a low or lower-middle income country whose member organisation pays the reduced membership fee
Commitment to return to your home country after the congress
Not a previous bursary recipient
Evidence of efforts to find other funding
opportunities.selection_process: A World Physiotherapy panel reviews applications against five outcome-based criteria: the benefit to the applicant's professional development, how learning will be shared with the employer, the local impact, the contribution to developing the profession, and the applicant's efforts to secure other funding.
opportunities.about_provider: World Physiotherapy (formerly the World Confederation for Physical Therapy, WCPT) is the global body representing physiotherapists through its national member organisations. It organises the World Physiotherapy Congress every two years.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Complete the online bursary application on the congress's Oxford Abstracts portal, linked from the bursary page, before 21 December 2026. Explain how attending will benefit you, your employer and physiotherapy in your country, and what other funding you have sought.
opportunities.notes: Recipients must send a report within one month of the congress. The abstract call for the congress closed on 29 September 2026.

opportunities.title: Peking University Scholarships for New International Graduate Students 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-Chinese citizens applying to full-time master's or PhD programmes at Peking University for September 2027 can be considered for its scholarships.
opportunities.description:
Peking University (PKU) is accepting applications from international students for full-time master's and doctoral programmes starting in September 2027, and applicants can be considered for several scholarships at the same time. These include the PKU Scholarship for New International Students, the Chinese Government Scholarship (Type B, university programme) and the Beijing Government Scholarship.

Admission follows an 'application plus examination' model: the International Student Division checks the file, then each school's expert panel reviews it and runs a second-round assessment between January and March 2027. Programmes are offered in Chinese and in English across PKU's campuses in Beijing and its Shenzhen Graduate School.

For African graduates, this is a route to one of China's top two universities with funding that can cover tuition, housing, living costs and insurance. The first-round window runs until 25 December 2026, so documents such as authenticated degree certificates should be prepared early.
opportunities.benefits: Depending on the scheme: the Chinese Government Scholarship (Type B) offers full or partial cover of tuition, accommodation, living allowance and medical insurance; the PKU Scholarship for New International Students covers full or partial tuition, living expenses and medical insurance; the Beijing Government Scholarship (Types A, B, C) ranges from tuition and insurance up to tuition, housing, a living stipend and insurance. The page does not give amounts.

Master's: bachelor's degree recognised by China's Ministry of Education
PhD: master's degree (bachelor's holders may apply to some science and engineering PhDs)
Chinese-taught programmes: HSK level 6 with at least 200 (sciences) or 210 (humanities) and writing 65 or more
English-taught programmes: TOEFL, GRE (above 315) or other proof as each programme sets
Beijing Government Scholarship age limits: master's 35 or under, PhD 40 or under

Any extra materials required by the school
opportunities.selection_process: The International Student Division first checks eligibility, then school expert panels review the files and hold a second-round assessment (January to March 2027) of research ability, language and potential. opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Plant Health in Sustainable Cropping Systems (PlantHealth), first call
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Holders of a 180-ECTS bachelor's in agronomy, agriculture or a related field with some plant-health coursework and B2 English, from any country.
opportunities.description:
PlantHealth is a two-year Erasmus Mundus Joint Master (120 ECTS) on protecting crops in sustainable farming systems. It is run by a European consortium coordinated by the Universitat Politècnica de València (UPV), and students move between partner campuses: UPV in Valencia, AgroParisTech, the University of Göttingen, Institut Agro and the University of Padova. Teaching is in English and French and the programme is delivered in person.

The first application call is open from 1 October to 31 December 2026; online applications must be in before midnight (CET) at the start of 1 January 2027, and results are expected at the end of February 2027. The dates point to a cohort starting in autumn 2027. Only applicants in this first call can be considered for the EU-funded Erasmus Mundus (EMJM) scholarships or consortium grants. A second call (20 May to 15 June 2027) is only for self-funded or externally funded candidates.

For African graduates in agronomy or agriculture, the programme is a fully funded route to training in plant pathology, pest management and crop protection across several European countries, and the scholarship is open to non-EU students.
opportunities.benefits: The Erasmus Mundus (EMJM) scholarship covers 100% of the participation (tuition) costs, health insurance and mandatory academic costs, and pays €1,400 per month for up to 24 months. Without a scholarship, total participation costs are €10,000 for applicants from outside the EU/EEA/Switzerland (€9,000 for EU/EEA/Swiss students), paid in two instalments; self-funded students may receive an Erasmus+ grant of about €300 per month in the second year.
requirements: An official bachelor's degree of at least 180 ECTS in agronomy, agriculture or a related field
At least 4 ECTS of coursework in plant health or crop protection
Final-year students may apply if they will graduate before the end of August
English at B2 level shown by IELTS, TOEFL, Cambridge (FCE/CAE/CPE), Trinity ISE, ESOL, OTE or PTE (Duolingo, TOEIC and university certificates are not accepted)
Native speakers or graduates taught entirely in English are exempt with proof
Applicants who already received an EMJM scholarship, or who hold another EU grant at the same time, cannot get the scholarship
documents: Two signed and stamped recommendation letters with referee contact details
Motivation statement of up to 1,000 characters in the online form
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are scored on academic record (GPA and merits) for 60%, the recommendation letters for 20% and the applicant's motivation for 20%. Scholarships are awarded only to applicants of the first call.
important_dates: First call closes: 31 December 2026 (before 1 January 2027, 00:00 CET)
Second call (self-funded only): 20 May to 15 June 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The PlantHealth consortium is a group of European universities offering an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master co-funded by the European Union. It is coordinated by the Universitat Politècnica de València in Spain, with AgroParisTech, Institut Agro, the University of Göttingen and the University of Padova as partners.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Create an applicant account and submit the single online form on the PlantHealth portal (planthealth.upv.es/user/create_applicant); the same form is used for scholarship and self-funded applications. Upload your diplomas, transcripts, CV, English certificate and two recommendation letters, and write the short motivation statement in the form before the first-call deadline.
opportunities.notes: Apply in the first call if you need funding: second-call applicants cannot receive scholarships. Check the consortium's financial support page and the University of Padova's scholarships for second-year students at Padova.

opportunities.description:
The Eric and Wendy Schmidt AI in Science Postdoctoral Fellowship at Nanyang Technological University (NTU) in Singapore supports early-career researchers who want to apply artificial intelligence to problems in engineering, the natural sciences or the mathematical sciences. It is part of a global programme funded by Schmidt Sciences to speed up the use of AI across STEM research.

The fellowship targets scientists whose PhD is not in computer science, which makes it a good fit for African researchers in fields such as chemistry, physics, biology, materials or civil engineering who want to add AI methods to their work. The page sets no nationality limit.
opportunities.benefits: Up to two years of postdoctoral employment at NTU with an attractive remuneration package (amount not published), travel allowances, and AI training through at least one AI module per year.

Excellent academic record and research potential
Research project applying AI to engineering, natural sciences or mathematical sciences
An NTU faculty member who agrees to mentor the project and writes a support letter

Official transcript or degree certificate in English
Research proposal of up to 2 pages (using the template on the page)
Support letter from the NTU mentor, attached to the proposal
Names of two referees, one of them the PhD supervisor (NTU contacts them)
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are judged on academic record, research potential and the quality of the AI-in-science proposal with its NTU mentor. The page does not describe interview stages.

opportunities.notes: Computer science PhDs are not eligible. NTU also lists other postdoctoral schemes on its research careers pages, such as the NTU AI-for-X Postdoctoral Fellowship and the Presidential Postdoctoral Fellowship.

opportunities.provider: International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Students with at least three years of university study or recent graduates, usually aged 32 or under, with good English or French and an interest in international law.
opportunities.description:
The International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea (ITLOS) in Hamburg runs a three-month, full-time internship programme for students and recent graduates interested in international law. The call now open is for the July to September 2027 period, with applications due by 31 December 2026; applications for later periods can also be submitted.

Interns support the Registry in areas such as law, international relations, political science, public relations, library science and translation. About 20 internships are offered each year, and since 1997 the Tribunal has hosted 420 interns from 106 States.

The internship itself is unpaid, but a trust fund gives a limited number of allowances for travel and living costs to nationals of developing countries in financial need, which includes many African countries. This makes it a realistic way for African law and international relations students to gain experience at an international court.
opportunities.benefits: Internships are unpaid. The Trust Fund for the Law of the Sea gives a limited amount of funding to cover travel and living costs, paid as a monthly allowance, for selected interns who are nationals of and normally live in an OECD DAC developing country and are in financial need. Funding must be requested in the online application form; late requests are not considered.
requirements: At least three years of university study completed
Enrolled in a degree or postgraduate course during the internship, or graduated within 12 months before applying
Normally aged 32 or under
Good English and/or French
Interest in international law; background in law, international relations, political science, public relations, library science or translation
Not currently in employment
documents: Cover letter of up to one page
Optional: research or writing sample up to 10 pages
Optional: proof of enrolment, degrees and transcripts
Translations of documents not in English or French
opportunities.selection_process: An Internship Selection Committee reviews complete applications, and the Registrar decides with the approval of the President. Geographic diversity and gender balance are taken into account, and applicants hear the result about one month after the deadline.
important_dates: Results: about one month after the deadline
opportunities.about_provider: ITLOS is an independent international court set up under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea. It sits in Hamburg, Germany, and settles disputes about the interpretation and application of the Convention.

Nusa Putra University in Sukabumi, West Java, Indonesia, offers international undergraduate scholarships for its English-taught bachelor's degrees starting in the 2027/2028 academic year. The awards last for the full eight semesters of a degree.

There are three schemes. The Genusian Scholarship is the most complete, covering tuition, a monthly living allowance, housing help, visa sponsorship and health insurance. The International Islamic Boarding Scholarship offers the same support with full residence in the university's pesantren (Islamic boarding school). The Berlian Scholarship covers tuition and language and academic support only.

International Islamic Boarding Scholarship: the same, plus a full pesantren dormitory place. Berlian Scholarship: 100% tuition for 8 semesters, BIPA classes, airport pick-up and academic mentoring (no living allowance, visa fees, housing or insurance). None of the schemes pays for the passport, international flights or medical checks.

opportunities.title: Takemi Program in International Health Fellowship 2027-2028
opportunities.provider: Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Mid-career health professionals and researchers with a graduate degree, publications and already-collected data, from any country.
opportunities.description:
The Takemi Program in International Health at the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health in Boston is a one-year, in-person research fellowship for mid-career health professionals and researchers, mainly from low- and middle-income countries. It describes itself as the oldest continuing mid-career research and training programme in global health, and since 1983 it has hosted 330 fellows from 62 countries, about 70 of them from Africa.

Fellows spend an academic year (1 August to 30 June) analysing data they have already collected, writing papers, attending seminars and building networks. Applications for the 2027-2028 year are open until 31 December 2026 at midnight US Eastern time, with decisions in February and applicants informed by March.

Applicants should note that the programme itself does not fund fellows: most must bring their own funding, and only very limited internal support exists for two fellows from low-income countries. It suits African health researchers who already have funding or an employer's support and want a year at Harvard to turn their data into publications and policy.
opportunities.benefits: The programme gives a year of in-person research time at Harvard, seminars, mentoring and a certificate, but it does not provide funding. Limited internal support (from a Japan Pharmaceutical Medical Association donation) may cover two fellows from low-income countries, decided at acceptance. Fellows must show at least US$36,410 a year for the J-1 visa; the page estimates real costs at US$60,000-77,000 a year (2024-25 figures).
requirements: A completed graduate (advanced) degree in any discipline
Significant work and research experience, including publications in internationally recognised journals
Leadership potential in your home country
Good English (TOEFL, IELTS, or a transcript from an English-medium university)
Commitment to a career in health
Data already collected before the fellowship (active data collection is not supported)
Able to attend in person for the full year
documents: Research proposal of up to 5 pages (single-spaced, 12-pt Times New Roman, with aims, background, data sources and methods)
Statement of interest answering five set questions
Publications list and one sample English-language publication
opportunities.selection_process: A committee reviews applications and meets in mid-February to choose fellows; applicants are told by March. Reapplying in later years is allowed.
important_dates: Deadline: 31 December 2026, midnight US Eastern time
Fellowship year: 1 August 2027 - 30 June 2028 (orientation late August)
opportunities.about_provider: The Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health is Harvard University's school of public health in Boston. The Takemi Program, named after Dr Taro Takemi of the Japan Medical Association, has trained mid-career global health leaders there since 1983.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Complete the online application form (Harvard Qualtrics link on the apply page), uploading your CV, proposal, statement and publications, and ask three referees to email their letters. Start looking for funding early, using the programme's list of possible funding sources. Questions go to takemi@hsph.harvard.edu.
opportunities.notes: There is no programming in January and no remote option. Plan funding in advance: most fellows are supported by their employer, government or an external funder.

opportunities.title: Wallenberg-NTU Presidential Postdoctoral Fellowship 2027
opportunities.provider: Nanyang Technological University and Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers of any nationality within 5 years of their PhD proposing AI, data, software, security or autonomy research.
opportunities.description:
The Wallenberg-NTU Presidential Postdoctoral Fellowship is a two-year independent research fellowship split between Singapore and Sweden. Fellows spend the first year at Nanyang Technological University (NTU) and the second year with a research group in the Wallenberg AI, Autonomous Systems and Software Program (WASP) in Sweden. The scheme is supported by the Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation.

Five fellowships are offered in this call, and research must fall in one of five areas: artificial intelligence, machine learning, big data and analytics, software and security, or mobility and autonomy. Applications close on 31 December 2026 at 23:59 Singapore time, referee reports are due by 7 January 2027, and fellows must be able to start by 31 December 2027.

The fellowship is open to researchers from Singapore and around the world, with no nationality list, so African computing and data scientists within five years of their PhD can compete for a well-funded start to an independent research career on two continents.
opportunities.benefits: In the Singapore year: an annual salary of up to SGD 80,000, a research grant of up to SGD 100,000, and a relocation allowance and housing grant for the fellowship. In the Sweden year: an annual support package covering salary, supervision and travel at WASP's standard postdoctoral level.
requirements: PhD or equivalent obtained within the last 5 years
Intellectual excellence and the maturity to lead independent research
A research proposal in AI, machine learning, big data and analytics, software and security, or mobility and autonomy
Available to start no later than 31 December 2027
Open to applicants of any nationality
documents: Official transcript or PhD certificate in English
Research proposal of up to 2 pages (template on the page)
Top 3 publications in PDF and other supporting documents
Two referees, one of them the PhD supervisor
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are reviewed on academic excellence, independence and the research proposal, together with referee reports due one week after the deadline. Five fellows are chosen.
opportunities.about_provider: Nanyang Technological University is a leading research-intensive university in Singapore. The Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation is Sweden's largest private research funder and finances WASP, Sweden's major national programme in AI and autonomous systems.
