opportunities.eligibility_summary: Humanities and social-science scholars based in a World Bank low- or lower-middle-income country can apply by 1 January 2027 (and each 1 May and 1 September) for help with conference or research travel.
opportunities.description:
The Institute of Global Value Inquiry (IGVI) runs a travel grant programme for scholars in the humanities and social sciences whose work deals with questions of value, preferably with a philosophical focus. Grants help pay for attending conferences and workshops or for research trips.

There are three application rounds every year, closing on 1 January, 1 May and 1 September, and applications are usually processed within about two weeks. The next round closes on 1 January 2027.

The programme is aimed specifically at scholars based in World Bank low- and lower-middle-income countries, which covers most of Africa, and there is no career-stage limit, membership requirement or abstract requirement.
opportunities.benefits: Contribution to travel costs for conferences, workshops or research trips, assessed against IGVI's flat-rate cost tables.
requirements: Based in a World Bank low- or lower-middle-income country
Working in the humanities or social sciences on value inquiry (philosophical focus preferred)
Proof that you have applied to the event or research activity
Any career stage
documents: Proof of application to the event or activity
Cost evidence (for example a travel agent quote or screenshot)
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are judged on the relevance of the research project and of the trip, and on available funds in that round.
important_dates: Later rounds: 1 May and 1 September each year
Decision: about two weeks after the deadline
opportunities.about_provider: IGVI is a research institute that supports inquiry into values across the humanities and social sciences, with a focus on including scholars from the Global South. It funds travel, research grants and research positions.

opportunities.title: Northeastern State University International 50% Tuition Waiver (Spring 2027)

opportunities.description:
Northeastern State University (NSU) in Oklahoma, USA, offers a Non-Resident 50% Tuition Waiver to international students working towards their first bachelor's or master's degree. For the Spring 2027 term the application deadline is 1 January.

The waiver halves the non-resident part of tuition, bringing costs closer to in-state rates. Students must be fully admitted (not on conditional or probationary admission) and must live on campus, unless they are legacy students whose parent, grandparent or sibling holds an NSU degree.

NSU also lists a General International Student Scholarship and merit awards of USD 500 to 5,000 for new international students, so African students can combine support to make study in the US more affordable.
opportunities.benefits: Waives 50% of the non-resident portion of tuition for first bachelor's and master's degrees. Published rates: non-resident USD 334.25 per credit hour (undergraduate) and USD 365.25 (graduate), against in-state rates of USD 245.25 and USD 309.75. Separate merit awards for new international students range from USD 500 to 5,000 for one year.
requirements: International student pursuing a first bachelor's or master's degree
Full regular admission (not conditional, alternative or probationary)
Live in on-campus housing (legacy students exempt)
Incoming freshmen: GPA of at least 3.0
Transfer students: GPA of at least 2.75
Graduate students: must live on campus
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants who meet the admission, GPA and housing conditions and apply by the deadline are considered for the waiver.
opportunities.about_provider: Northeastern State University is a public regional university in Tahlequah, Oklahoma, with campuses in Tahlequah, Muskogee and Broken Arrow. It is the oldest institution of higher learning in Oklahoma.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Gain regular admission to NSU, then complete the Apply Now waiver form linked from the international scholarships page before 1 January for Spring 2027. For the other international scholarships, email international@nsuok.edu.
opportunities.notes: The waiver covers only part of non-resident tuition. Fall 2027 applicants have later deadlines (1 August), and the NSU Foundation scholarship for new international students has a priority deadline of 1 March 2027.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: International applicants to an eligible TU/e master's for September 2027 with a GPA of at least 7.5/10 and no prior Dutch degree study.
opportunities.description:
Eindhoven University of Technology (TU/e) in the Netherlands offers the TU/e Scholarship for Excellence to top students starting a full-time master's on 1 September 2027. The 2027-2028 edition, titled 'Shaping the Future of Microchip Innovation', is funded by the Dutch national Beethoven Program and supports master's programmes linked to the semiconductor and high-tech industry.

Eligible programmes include Applied Physics, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science and Engineering, Data Science and AI, Embedded Systems, Industrial and Applied Mathematics, Systems and Control, Sustainable Energy Technology, Automotive Technology, Nuclear Fusion, and Artificial Intelligence and Engineering Systems. About 35 awards are made, 15 of them for students from outside the EEA, and only about 2% of applicants succeed.

The award is €7,500 a year for two years, so it is a partial scholarship rather than full funding. Non-EEA winners also receive part of the NL Scholarship in their first year. Strong African engineering and science graduates with a GPA of 7.5/10 or better can apply as part of their master's application by 1 January 2027.
opportunities.benefits: €7,500 per academic year for two years (€15,000 in total). Non-EEA recipients also receive a share of the NL Scholarship in year one (not applied for separately). It is not a full scholarship; keeping the year-two award needs at least 45 ECTS in year one.
requirements: Applied for a full-time TU/e master's starting 1 September 2027 in an eligible programme
High-school diploma or bachelor's obtained outside the Netherlands
No previous Dutch higher education (exchange periods allowed)
GPA of at least 7.5 out of 10 (or equivalent) on the latest transcript
Able to meet Dutch visa and residence-permit rules
Not a JADS joint master's or European double degree, and not admitted on an earlier intake's decision
documents: Confirmation in the application that you want to be considered
opportunities.selection_process: The International Office checks eligibility, then a Scholarship Selection Committee ranks candidates. Results are confirmed by the end of March 2027 and cannot be appealed.
opportunities.about_provider: Eindhoven University of Technology is a Dutch research university focused on engineering, science and technology. It sits in the Brainport Eindhoven region, home to ASML and other high-tech and chip companies.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for an eligible TU/e master's and, in that application, indicate that you want to be considered for the scholarship and add a brief motivation. Submit the complete application by 1 January 2027 at 23:59 CET. Questions go to io@tue.nl with 'TU/e Scholarship' in the subject line.
opportunities.notes: About 2% of applicants are selected. TU/e also lists the Changemaker Scholarship (housing for 10 months, same deadline) and external schemes such as the ASML Technology Scholarship.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants with a 2:1 bachelor's or a master's in a relevant science who apply to a listed CENTA project; international places are capped at 30%.
opportunities.description:
CENTA, the Central England NERC Training Alliance, is recruiting for its project-based PhD studentships starting in autumn 2027. CENTA is a doctoral training partnership funded by the UK's Natural Environment Research Council (NERC) and led by the University of Birmingham with partner universities and research centres across central England.

Applicants choose a specific project from CENTA's list, covering environmental and earth sciences, and apply to the host university. Studentships last 3.5 years and include a tax-free stipend and a research training grant. Applications close at 23:59 GMT on Wednesday 6 January 2027.

International applicants, including Africans, can apply, but UK rules limit them to 30% of the cohort, and CENTA only pays fees at the home rate, so international students face a fee shortfall to cover themselves.
opportunities.benefits: For 3.5 years: a stipend of £21,805 a year (2026/27 rate) paid monthly, tuition fees at the UK home rate (international students will likely face a fee shortfall), and a research training support grant of £8,000. Visa, health surcharge, flights and relocation costs are not covered.
requirements: At least a 2:1 UK bachelor's or a pass in a UK master's, or equivalent
Application to a specific CENTA project
International students are capped at 30% of the cohort
International students must cover the gap between home and international fees
Only one project per university
documents: CENTA Studentship Application Form (2027 version) - applications without it are rejected
CV with at least two referees
Equality, diversity and inclusion (EDI) survey receipt number
opportunities.selection_process: Each host university's recruitment team shortlists applicants, online interviews are normally held in early February, and conditional offers go out in late February or early March 2027. Offers depend on the host university's admission offer.
opportunities.about_provider: CENTA is a NERC-funded doctoral training partnership that trains PhD researchers in environmental science. It is hosted by the University of Birmingham with partner universities and research organisations in central England.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Pick a project from the CENTA projects list, then apply through the host university's online portal, attaching the CENTA Studentship Application Form, your CV with two referees and the EDI survey receipt. Submit before 23:59 GMT on 6 January 2027.
opportunities.notes: The separate CENTA Science Opportunity Scholarships (CSOS) are closed for 2027 and not open to international students. One Cranfield project (2027-C03) starts earlier, by 6 June 2027.

opportunities.title: French Government Eiffel Excellence Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International master's candidates aged up to 29 and doctoral candidates aged up to 35 can be nominated by a French higher-education institution for the 2027 Eiffel call.
opportunities.description:
The France Excellence Eiffel scholarship is the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs' flagship award for bringing top international students to French universities and grandes écoles. Campus France runs the programme on the ministry's behalf, and the 2027 call opened on 2 October 2026.

The award supports two tracks: master's study and doctoral study (usually a mobility period within a co-supervised or co-directed doctorate). Students do not apply to Campus France themselves. Instead, a French institution that has admitted or is admitting the student puts the candidate forward, and the institution files the application with Campus France.

For African students this is one of the most visible French government awards, and it is open to applicants from any country outside France. Because the institution must nominate you, the practical first step is to apply for admission early to a French programme and ask its international office whether it nominates candidates for Eiffel.
opportunities.benefits: The programme funds a monthly allowance and related support for the master's or doctoral stay in France; the exact amounts and coverage are set out in the 2027 programme regulations published by Campus France.
requirements: Nominated by a French higher-education institution (no direct student applications)
Master's track: aged 29 or under
Doctoral track: aged 35 or under
Admitted to, or being admitted to, a programme at the nominating institution
documents: Application file prepared with the host institution (following the Campus France filing guide)
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are scored by expert evaluators drawn from French university teacher-researchers, using separate published grids for the master's and doctoral tracks. Results are announced by Campus France.
opportunities.about_provider: Campus France is the French national agency for promoting higher education, hosting international students and managing government scholarships. It administers the Eiffel programme for the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for admission to a French institution and ask its international office about its internal Eiffel deadline, which falls before 6 January 2027. The institution prepares and submits the file to Campus France; new institutions contact candidatures.eiffel@campusfrance.org to get access.
opportunities.notes: Check the host institution's own deadline, which is earlier than the Campus France date. An English version of the programme page is available on campusfrance.org.

opportunities.description:
ACCE+ is a NERC Doctoral Landscape Award partnership that trains PhD researchers in ecology, evolution and the wider environmental sciences. It is led by the University of Liverpool with the Universities of Sheffield and York and research partners including the UK Centre for Ecology & Hydrology, the Natural History Museum and the National Oceanography Centre.

For 2027/28 entry the partnership is advertising projects from early November 2026 and funds at least 13 studentships a year. Students join a cohort-based programme with shared training across the partner institutions alongside their individual research project.

International students, including applicants from Africa, may apply, but UKRI rules cap international candidates at 30% of studentships and interview places, and not every ACCE+ department is taking international applicants this year. Check each project advert before applying.
opportunities.benefits: NERC-funded PhD studentship for 2027/28 entry with cohort training across the partnership; the funding package is detailed on the ACCE+ financial-support page.
requirements: Degree in a subject relevant to the project
Liverpool, Sheffield and York generally expect the equivalent of a UK 2:1 or better (exceptions for demonstrated excellence)
International applicants limited to 30% of studentships and interviews
Some departments are not accepting international applicants for 2027/28: check the project advert
English proficiency evidence if requested by the host institution
documents: Host institution's online application form with the ACCE+ proforma questions (replaces CV and personal statement)
Details of referees, including at least one academic
Transcripts, passport and English test certificate if requested
Mandatory equality, diversity and inclusion form
opportunities.selection_process: Applications receive a holistic, contextualised review against the published ACCE+ rubric, followed by interviews in the weeks of 15 and 22 February 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: ACCE+ (Adapting to the Challenges of a Changing Environment) is a doctoral training partnership funded by the UK Natural Environment Research Council. It brings together Liverpool, Sheffield and York with national research centres and museums.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Choose one or two projects at a host institution and apply through that institution's online form, adding the ACCE+ proforma answers, referee details and the EDI form. Applications to different institutions are made separately. Questions go to acce.dtp@liverpool.ac.uk.

opportunities.description:
Johns Hopkins SAIS Europe in Bologna, Italy, offers financial aid to students entering its Master of Arts in International Affairs (MAIA). Awards range from partial tuition funding to a small number of full-tuition scholarships, and the school reports that more than 70% of its entering class receives aid.

The MAIA is a graduate degree in international relations and international economics taught at the SAIS Europe campus. Aid is considered as part of the admission application, so candidates must apply for admission and complete the financial aid section by the Regular Decision deadline.

Aid is open to students of every nationality, which makes it relevant for African applicants interested in diplomacy, development, international economics and policy careers. Some donor-funded awards carry their own nationality restrictions or separate applications.
opportunities.benefits: Merit and need-based awards from partial tuition funding up to a limited number of full-tuition scholarships; second-year support is possible for strong students. No application fee.
requirements: Applying for the SAIS Europe MAIA, Fall 2027 entry
Grade of B- or better in introductory microeconomics and macroeconomics (or one course covering both) before enrolling
English test for non-native speakers
Interview required for all MAIA candidates
GRE/GMAT optional
documents: Online application with the financial aid section completed
opportunities.selection_process: Admission is decided on the full application and an interview; aid is awarded at admission on merit and need. Some donor awards require a separate application.
important_dates: Regular Decision and aid deadline: 7 January 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The Johns Hopkins School of Advanced International Studies (SAIS) is the graduate school of international affairs of Johns Hopkins University, with campuses in Washington DC, Bologna and Nanjing.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online for the MAIA by 7 January 2027 and answer yes to the scholarship question in the financial aid section; otherwise you will not be considered. Send proof of income by 15 February and prepare for the admission interview.

opportunities.description:
The Great Western Four+ Doctoral Training Partnership funds PhD research across the environmental sciences. It links the Universities of Bristol, Bath, Cardiff and Exeter with research partners including the British Antarctic Survey, British Geological Survey, UK Centre for Ecology & Hydrology, Natural History Museum and Plymouth Marine Laboratory.

Studentships start in September 2027 and are funded for three and a half years full time, with up to four years to complete. Students pick a project advertised by one of the partner schools and join a cross-institution training cohort.

The programme is mainly for UK students, but a limited number of full studentships are available to international applicants, which makes it a realistic route for strong African graduates in earth, ocean, climate, ecology and related fields.
opportunities.benefits: Tax-free stipend of £22,437 a year; tuition fees paid (international awardees are charged at the home fee rate); research and training support grant of £11,000; training budget of £1,000. Visa, immigration health surcharge and relocation costs are not covered.
requirements: Upper second-class degree or higher (or international equivalent) in a discipline related to the project
Master's degree encouraged but not required
English at University of Bristol profile level E if English is not your first language
Only one project application allowed across all partner institutions
documents: Online application for the PhD linked to the chosen project
Personal statement on the Bristol GW4+ template
Supporting documents listed in the 2027 How to Apply guide (transcripts, references, English evidence)
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are assessed by the partner schools hosting each project; shortlisted candidates are interviewed. Full criteria are in the How to Apply guide.
opportunities.about_provider: GW4 is an alliance of four research-intensive universities in the west of England and Wales. The GW4+ partnership is funded by the Natural Environment Research Council and includes national research centres.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Find a project on the GW4+ site, then apply for the related PhD through the University of Bristol online application (or the host partner's system) by 7 January 2027, attaching the GW4+ personal statement template. Contact uob-pgradmissions@bristol.ac.uk with questions.

opportunities.title: DHET Japan Scholarship Programme at Tokyo Metropolitan University 2027
opportunities.provider: South Africa DHET / Tokyo Metropolitan University
opportunities.eligibility_summary: South African citizens with a strong bachelor's (master's track) or master's (PhD track) can apply to DHET by 8 January 2027 for fully funded study at Tokyo Metropolitan University from October 2027.
opportunities.description:
South Africa's Department of Higher Education and Training (DHET) runs this scholarship with Tokyo Metropolitan University (TMU) so that South African graduates can complete a master's or doctoral degree in Japan. Study starts in October 2027; master's degrees last two years and PhDs three years.

The call covers a set list of fields at TMU: Biological Sciences (PhD only), Geography, Civil and Environmental Engineering, Applied Chemistry for the Environment and Tourism Science (master's and PhD).

opportunities.benefits: Full tuition; one return economy airfare plus one mid-term airfare; a monthly stipend for living costs, accommodation and local transport; a once-off settlement allowance; health and medical insurance; visa costs; pre-departure orientation and psychosocial support.
requirements: South African citizen in good health (medical examination required)
Master's track: bachelor's or NQF 7 with GPA of at least 2.30 out of 3.00 (about 78%)
PhD track: master's degree with the same GPA
GPA confirmed with the official DHET GPA calculator
Proficient in English and meets TMU programme requirements
Available to start in October 2027
Foreign qualifications evaluated by SAQA or Umalusi
documents: Degree certificate or proof of completion
Publication abstracts and nomination letter, if any
opportunities.selection_process: Five stages: an eligibility check, ranking by academics, an online or in-person interview and questionnaire for shortlisted applicants, nomination by DHET, and a final admission decision by TMU.
opportunities.about_provider: The Department of Higher Education and Training is the South African government department responsible for universities and colleges. Its international scholarships office manages government-to-government and partner-university scholarships for South Africans.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Prepare all documents as clearly named PDFs and send the complete package to DHET by email using the contact on the official page before 8 January 2027. Late or incomplete applications are not considered.
opportunities.notes: Use the official GPA calculator; applications without it may be rejected. Make sure your passport is ready by April 2027.

opportunities.title: ISTA Funded PhD Programme 2027
opportunities.provider: Institute of Science and Technology Austria
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Bachelor's or master's graduates of any nationality in the sciences, mathematics or computer science can apply to the ISTA PhD programme by 8 January 2027 for a September 2027 start.
opportunities.description:
The Institute of Science and Technology Austria (ISTA) runs an interdisciplinary graduate school near Vienna that admits PhD students in biology, chemistry, physics, mathematics, computer science, neuroscience, earth sciences and related areas. The call for the 2027 intake is open, and the programme starts on 15 September 2027.

Students first join research groups through rotations and coursework before choosing a thesis group, so applicants apply to the programme rather than to a single supervisor. Applicants with a bachelor's degree may enter directly.

No nationality restriction appears on the official pages, which makes ISTA a strong option for African graduates who want a funded, research-intensive PhD in Europe.
opportunities.benefits: Funded PhD position at ISTA; employment terms are explained by ISTA on admission.
requirements: Bachelor's or master's degree in a relevant field (or about to complete one)
Strong undergraduate record
Documents in English
Available to start on 15 September 2027 (start date not negotiable)
documents: Transcripts and diplomas in English and in the original language
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are judged on undergraduate performance, reference letters (academic referees preferred), the statement of purpose, field-specific and transferable skills, and diversity. A first review runs in February, followed by mostly remote interviews in late February and early March; decisions come by early March.
important_dates: Reference letters due: 12 January 2027, 11:59 PM CET
Interviews: late February to early March 2027
opportunities.about_provider: ISTA is a research institute in Klosterneuburg, Austria, dedicated to basic research in the natural and formal sciences, with its own graduate school offering PhD degrees.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Register on the Apply@ISTA portal (apply.ista.ac.at) and complete the application on a desktop browser, uploading all documents there; emailed documents are not processed. Enter your referees early so they can submit letters by 12 January.
opportunities.notes: The portal does not work on mobile devices. You can still change referee details until the application deadline.

opportunities.title: NIMS International Cooperative Graduate Program 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Full-time graduate students enrolled at an NIMS partner university (none currently in Africa) can be nominated by 8 January 2027 for a 6-12 month research stay in Tsukuba, Japan.
opportunities.description:
The International Cooperative Graduate Program (ICGP) of Japan's National Institute for Materials Science (NIMS) brings graduate students from partner universities to Tsukuba for a research attachment in materials science. The 2027 call is open, with stays starting from July 2027 onward.

Stays last 6 to 12 months and can be split into several visits. Each student works under an NIMS co-supervisor while remaining registered at their home university, and English is the working language.

Partner universities are in North America, Europe and Asia; none is in Africa. African students can benefit only if they are enrolled full time at one of the listed partners.
opportunities.benefits: Living allowance of 120,000 JPY per month, accommodation at Ninomiya House in Tsukuba, and visa support; no training or facility fees. Utilities and insurance are paid by the student.
requirements: Full-time graduate student at an ICGP partner university
Registered as a student for the whole stay
Nominated by the partner university (maximum two per partner per year)
Working knowledge of English
Research insurance and Japanese National Health Insurance
opportunities.selection_process: The partner university selects and nominates candidates, NIMS finds a co-supervisor and may hold online interviews, and the NIMS president gives final approval. Results come in mid-March 2027.
important_dates: Application deadline (documents at NIMS via the home university): 8 January 2027
opportunities.about_provider: NIMS is Japan's national research institute for materials science, based in Tsukuba. It runs graduate education programmes with Japanese and international partner universities.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Send the application form and transcripts electronically to the ICGP contact at your partner university, who forwards nominations to the NIMS Graduate Program Section by 8 January 2027. Questions go to nims-graduate@nims.go.jp.
opportunities.notes: Family visas are not supported. Check whether your university is on the official partner list before applying.

opportunities.title: Surrey Vice-Chancellor's Future Leaders Award 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Self-funded overseas students domiciled in Algeria, Botswana, Egypt, Kenya, Mauritius, Morocco, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda or Zimbabwe with a Surrey offer can apply for a £7,500 first-year fee waiver.
opportunities.description:
The Vice-Chancellor's Future Leaders Award is a University of Surrey fee waiver for self-funded international students from a list of priority countries. It is available for full-time undergraduate degrees starting in September 2027 and for postgraduate taught degrees starting in February or September 2027.

Awards are made on a first-come, first-served basis and must be secured before the university issues your CAS for the visa, so early application matters. Applications are reviewed monthly.

Eligibility depends on where you live (domicile), not on nationality. Ten African countries are on the list, making this a useful discount for students from those countries applying to Surrey in Guildford, UK.
opportunities.benefits: £7,500 reduction in tuition fees for the first year of study only. It cannot be deferred or combined with other Surrey scholarships, alumni discounts or early-payment discounts.
requirements: Self-funded student paying overseas fees
Domiciled in an eligible country (for Africa: Algeria, Botswana, Egypt, Kenya, Mauritius, Morocco, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda, Zimbabwe)
Offer for a full-time degree at Surrey
Undergraduates: first-year entry with Surrey as firm UCAS choice; Clearing applicants need ABB or equivalent
Apply before your CAS is issued
Not for the International Study Centre, part-time, distance learning, the MBA or some named MSc programmes
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are assessed monthly on prior academic performance, predicted grades where relevant, and the personal statement, until awards run out.
important_dates: Postgraduate February 2027 intake: applications close 8 January 2027
Postgraduate September 2027 intake: applications close 20 August 2027
Undergraduate September 2027 intake: applications close 24 August 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Surrey is a public research university in Guildford, England, known for engineering, health, business and hospitality programmes.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for your Surrey degree first, then use the 'Apply now' form on the award page for your intake, quoting your offer and student ID. Contact international@surrey.ac.uk with questions.
opportunities.notes: Applications without both an offer and a student ID are not assessed. Students from non-listed countries can look at Surrey's International Excellence Award (£5,000).

opportunities.title: Heinz Heinen Fellowships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Doctoral candidates near completion, postdocs, professors and non-academic knowledge producers working on slavery and strong dependency can apply by 10 January 2027 for a 2027/2028 fellowship in Bonn.
opportunities.description:
The Heinz Heinen Fellowships are offered by the Bonn Center for Dependency and Slavery Studies (BCDSS), a Cluster of Excellence at the University of Bonn. They bring international researchers to Bonn to work on strong asymmetrical dependencies, including slavery, with proposals expected to address periods before 1900 and to take a comparative view.

The 2027/2028 call offers fellowships starting no earlier than 1 October 2027 in several categories: doctoral (up to 6 months), junior postdoctoral and postdoctoral (up to 12 months), senior for full professors (up to 6 months in the call), and alternative knowledge producers such as journalists, artists and curators (up to 6 months).

No nationality limits are stated, and the programme's focus on slavery and dependency makes it highly relevant to African historians and scholars of the African past and its diasporas.
opportunities.benefits: Monthly stipend of €1,700 (doctoral), €2,600 (junior postdoc), €3,100 (postdoc) or €3,600 (senior); outward and return travel allowance; accommodation lump sum of up to €1,000 per month (€1,250 with children) for fellows from outside Bonn; desk and computer, workshop funding and childcare support.
requirements: Doctoral: close to finishing the PhD and enrolled
Junior postdoc: PhD awarded at most 4 years ago
Postdoc: PhD awarded more than 4 years ago
Senior: full professor
Alternative knowledge producers: journalists, artists, curators and similar
Project on strong dependency or slavery, ideally pre-1900 and comparative
Application in English
documents: Research statement (max 9,000 characters for doctoral, 6,000 for postdoc, excluding spaces)
List of principal publications (postdoc and senior)
Two reference letters (doctoral: one from the supervisor; postdoc: two)
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are judged on how well the project fits the BCDSS research areas and on its relevance. Applicants are notified by April 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: BCDSS is a Cluster of Excellence funded under Germany's Excellence Strategy at the University of Bonn. It studies slavery and other forms of strong asymmetrical dependency across history and regions.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Combine all documents into a single English PDF and email it to application@dependency.uni-bonn.de by 10 January 2027. There is no online portal; questions go to researchandstudy@dependency.uni-bonn.de.
opportunities.notes: Late or incomplete applications are not considered. Check the five BCDSS research areas and make the fit explicit in your statement.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Three-month summer research program in Laxenburg, Austria, for PhD students close to finishing, with funding available for selected participants.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus European Forestry Scholarship 2027-2029
opportunities.provider: European Forestry consortium (University of Eastern Finland)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduates of any nationality with a three-year bachelor's in forestry or a related field and strong English can apply from 2 December 2026 to 13 January 2027 for the August 2027 European Forestry Erasmus Mundus master's.
opportunities.description:
MSc European Forestry is an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master coordinated by the University of Eastern Finland with AgroParisTech, the University of Freiburg, the University of Lleida, BOKU Vienna, Transilvania University of Brașov and Wageningen University. Students move between consortium universities during the two-year programme.

The next intake starts in August 2027. The application window runs from 2 December 2026 to 13 January 2027, followed by a short recorded motivation video.

The programme is open to applicants worldwide, and top candidates receive EU-funded Erasmus Mundus scholarships. That makes it a strong route for African forestry, environmental and natural-resource graduates who want a European master's.
opportunities.benefits: Erasmus Mundus scholarship (competitive): consortium fees and full insurance plus €1,400 per month for up to 24 months, the same for EU and non-EU students. Some of the best non-EU applicants without a scholarship may receive a 50% or 100% fee waiver (non-EU fee €9,000 a year). Student union and Kela health fees are not covered.
requirements: Bachelor's or higher in forestry or a related field, at least three years of full-time study
Good grades
IELTS Academic 7.0 (at least 6.0 in speaking and writing), TOEFL iBT, Cambridge C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency, taken from 2 December 2024
English exemption for degrees taught in English in the EU/EEA, UK, US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Ireland, Singapore or South Africa
Not a previous Erasmus Mundus scholarship holder
documents: Bachelor's certificate and transcript (with English translations if needed)
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are ranked competitively; all applicants are automatically considered for Erasmus Mundus scholarships and fee waivers. Results are given by 31 May 2027.
important_dates: Motivation video deadline: 20 January 2027, 23:59 Helsinki time
Final documents for graduating applicants: 30 July 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Eastern Finland coordinates the European Forestry consortium of seven European universities with strong forestry and environmental research.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit the application form on Finland's Studyinfo portal during the call window, upload your documents, then record the motivation video on the online platform by 20 January 2027. No separate scholarship application is needed.
opportunities.notes: Applicants still finishing their bachelor's must submit final documents by 30 July 2027.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to bachelor's graduates in IT, computer science, electrical engineering, photonics or a related field, with full EMJM scholarships for the best applicants.

opportunities.title: KAIST Scholarship for International Undergraduates, Fall 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International applicants admitted through KAIST's Fall 2027 international undergraduate round (applications by 14 January 2027) are automatically considered for full tuition plus a monthly allowance.
opportunities.description:
KAIST, South Korea's leading science and technology university in Daejeon, awards the KAIST Scholarship to international students admitted to its undergraduate programmes. There is no separate scholarship application: every applicant to the international admission track is reviewed for it during admission.

The Regular round for Fall 2027 runs from 10 November 2026 to 14 January 2027, with recommendation letters due a week later and results announced on 25 March 2027. Studies begin at the end of August 2027.

For African students interested in engineering, natural sciences or computing, it is a rare undergraduate award in Asia that combines full tuition with a living allowance for the whole degree.
opportunities.benefits: Full tuition waiver for 8 semesters, a living allowance of 350,000 KRW per month, and medical health insurance. Travel and other fees are not covered.
requirements: Applicant through KAIST International Student Admission
Keep a GPA above 2.7 out of 4.3 after the freshman year to retain the scholarship
opportunities.selection_process: All applicants are reviewed equally during admission, with interviews on 3 March 2027 if required; scholarship decisions come with the admission result.
important_dates: Regular round applications: 10 November 2026 - 14 January 2027, 6:00 PM KST
Recommendation letters due: 21 January 2027, 6:00 PM KST
Start of studies: end of August 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST) is a public research university in Daejeon founded in 1971, ranked among Asia's top institutions in science and engineering.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online through the KAIST international undergraduate admission portal by 14 January 2027 and select the KAIST scholarship in the financial resources statement. Ask your recommender to submit by 21 January.
opportunities.notes: The Early round closed on 22 October 2026. Check the eligibility page for rules on dual nationality.

opportunities.title: ARES Development Cooperation Scholarships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Master's and training scholarships in Belgium for nationals of partner developing countries.

opportunities.title: Aarhus University Danish State Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-EU/EEA applicants who apply for an Aarhus University master's by 15 January 2027 (summer intake) are automatically considered for a Danish State tuition waiver, sometimes with a living grant.
opportunities.description:
Aarhus University awards Danish State Scholarships, funded by the Danish government, to a small number of highly qualified non-EU/EEA students admitted to its master's programmes. The university has no scholarship fund of its own, so these are the main awards available.

There is no separate application. Everyone who applies for a master's by the deadline is assessed automatically, and offers are sent with the admission letter. Typically only one or two awards are made per programme.

What the award covers varies by faculty: Arts and Business and Social Sciences combine a tuition waiver with a monthly grant, while Natural and Technical Sciences give 100% tuition waivers. For African applicants, applying early and presenting excellent grades is key.
opportunities.benefits: Full or partial tuition fee waiver; in some faculties also a monthly living grant, usually for the whole programme.
requirements: Non-EU/EEA/Swiss applicant who must pay tuition
Applied for an Aarhus master's by 15 January (summer intake) or 15 September (winter intake)
Excellent academic record
Sufficient funds for any costs not covered (for waiver-only offers)
documents: No extra documents: the regular master's application is used (do not upload scholarship documents)
opportunities.selection_process: Faculties rank applicants on academic excellence when assessing admission; some faculties focus on particular countries or programmes. Offers have a short acceptance window.
important_dates: Acceptance of tuition waiver: by 1 April 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Aarhus University is Denmark's second-largest university, founded in 1928, with faculties of arts, natural sciences, technical sciences, health and business and social sciences.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for your chosen Aarhus master's programme through the university's application portal by 15 January 2027. If offered a scholarship, accept it by the stated date or it lapses.
opportunities.notes: The scholarship is tied to one programme and cannot be transferred.

opportunities.title: American Antiquarian Society Short-Term Fellowships 2027-28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Doctoral candidates, postdocs and independent scholars of any nationality researching early American history and culture can apply by 15 January 2027 for one- or two-month AAS fellowships in Worcester, Massachusetts.
opportunities.description:
The American Antiquarian Society (AAS) offers 19 different one- to two-month residential fellowships through a single application, for scholars who need to work in its library in Worcester, Massachusetts. The library holds one of the largest collections of printed material from early America.

Fellowships can be taken at any time between 1 June and 31 May; a second month is rarely granted. Most awards are open to doctoral candidates working on dissertations, and several also accept postdocs, independent researchers and holders of terminal degrees such as MLS or MFA.

International scholars are explicitly welcome, so African researchers working on Atlantic history, slavery, print culture or the African diaspora in early America can apply.
opportunities.benefits: Stipend of $2,400 per month. Rooms in the AAS scholars' housing (about $600 to $1,000 a month) can be deducted from the stipend.
requirements: Doctoral candidate, postdoc, independent scholar or terminal-degree holder (depending on the fellowship)
Project that needs the AAS collections
Preference for applicants without an AAS fellowship in the past three years
Arrange your own visa: AAS cannot sponsor J-1 visas
documents: Statement of previous support and current appointment
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are judged on scholarly qualifications, the significance of the project and how well it fits the AAS collections.
opportunities.about_provider: Founded in 1812, the American Antiquarian Society is a national research library and learned society focused on American history and culture up to 1876.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Combine all documents into one PDF and submit it through the AAS online fellowship form (Breezy portal) by 15 January 2027. One application covers all 19 short-term fellowships.
opportunities.notes: Some named fellowships have extra restrictions (for example one reserved for German citizens or residents).

opportunities.title: American University Emerging Global Leader Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International secondary-school students who need a US student visa and have not started university can apply by 15 January 2027 for American University's EGLS, with two full awards and partial awards up to US$40,000 a year.
opportunities.description:
The Emerging Global Leader Scholarship (EGLS) is American University's flagship award for international first-year students who will study in Washington DC on a student visa. It targets young people who have shown leadership, a commitment to social change in their communities and resilience in overcoming obstacles.

For Fall 2027 entry, two students receive a full award covering all billable university costs, and other strong applicants receive partial awards. Awards renew for up to four years with satisfactory progress.

African secondary-school students who are ambitious about public service, international affairs or community leadership are a natural fit for this scholarship.
opportunities.benefits: Full award (two students): full tuition, room and board for up to four years. Partial awards: up to US$40,000 a year, with no separate application. Not covered: health insurance, books, airfare, taxes and personal costs (about US$4,000 a year).
requirements: Not a US citizen or permanent resident, and will need an F-1 or J-1 visa
Has not enrolled in or started university study
Finished secondary school no earlier than 2024 (preference for students graduating by June 2027)
Proof of English proficiency
Evidence of leadership and community commitment
Able to show at least US$4,000 a year for uncovered costs
documents: Common Application with AU's international checklist documents
AU EGLS essays (submitted in the applicant portal)
Official English test score (TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo, PTE, LanguageCERT or Cambridge) sent by the testing agency
Bank letter and signed AU Declaration of Finances showing at least US$4,000
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are reviewed for merit, leadership, commitment to social change and obstacles overcome. Semi-finalists and finalists may be asked for Zoom interviews or extra essays, and winners are told by 1 April 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: American University is a private research university in Washington DC, known for international service, public affairs, law and communication.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply to American University through the Common Application (Regular Decision recommended) before 15 January 2027, then complete the EGLS essays in the AU applicant portal by the same date. Late applications are not considered.
opportunities.notes: Only two full awards are given, so also present yourself well for the partial awards, which need no extra application.

opportunities.title: Amsterdam Merit Scholarship (Amsterdam Law School LLM) 2027-28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-EU/EEA applicants with top grades applying to one of four Amsterdam Law School LLM programmes can apply by 15 January 2027 for the single Amsterdam Merit Scholarship (amount to be announced).
opportunities.description:
The Amsterdam Merit Scholarship (AMS) at the University of Amsterdam's Amsterdam Law School supports one excellent non-EU/EEA student each year in a full-time LLM (Master of Laws) programme. The 2027-2028 call applies to four LLM programmes: International and European Law, Transnational and European Private Law, Law and Finance, and International Criminal Law.

The scholarship is meant for applicants with outstanding grades who do not qualify for Dutch student finance. The amount for 2027-2028 has not yet been announced by the faculty, so applicants should treat it as a partial award and plan other funding.

African law graduates aiming at an international or European law career are eligible, provided they meet the grade threshold and can obtain a Dutch study visa.
opportunities.benefits: A scholarship towards the LLM year; the amount for 2027-2028 is to be announced by the university. Only one scholarship is awarded each year.
requirements: Non-EU/EEA passport and not eligible for Dutch student finance (studiefinanciering)
Applying for a first master's at the UvA
Full-time enrolment in one of four LLM programmes (International and European Law; Transnational and European Private Law; Law and Finance; International Criminal Law)
Previous degree grades comparable to a 4.0 US GPA, UK first-class honours or 8.0 on the Dutch scale (for a non-law bachelor, only law courses count)
Able to meet Dutch visa requirements
documents: Motivation letter of up to 500 words
All documents required for the LLM application (incomplete files are not considered)

opportunities.title: Folger Short-Term Scholarly Fellowships 2027-28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Scholars with a PhD, or PhD candidates at the dissertation stage, of any nationality, can apply by 15 January 2027 for a one- to three-month Folger fellowship paying USD 5,000 a month in residence or USD 4,000 virtually.
opportunities.description:
The Folger Shakespeare Library in Washington, DC offers short-term scholarly fellowships for researchers whose projects need its collections of early modern books, manuscripts and other materials. The 2027-2028 round funds stays of one, two or three months, and fellows may choose to work on site in Washington, virtually, or in a hybrid arrangement.

The fellowships are run by the Folger Institute, the library's research and scholarly programmes arm. They exist to support original research that makes real use of the Folger holdings, and the selection committee aims for a mix of disciplines, methods and geographical backgrounds among fellows.

There is no nationality restriction, so African doctoral candidates who have reached the dissertation stage and early-career or established scholars working on the early modern world, Shakespeare, book history, the Atlantic world or related topics can apply on equal terms with everyone else.
opportunities.benefits: USD 5,000 per month for fellows in residence in Washington, DC, or USD 4,000 per month for virtual fellows, for one to three months. The stipend is meant to cover travel, housing and living costs.
requirements: A terminal degree (such as a PhD), or PhD candidacy at the all-but-dissertation stage, or an international equivalent
A research project that needs the Folger collections
Open to applicants of any nationality
Fellowship of one, two or three months, held on site, virtually or in hybrid form
documents: Project abstract of up to 250 words
Project description of up to 1,500 words, stating the months requested and how each month will be used
One-page list of the Folger primary sources you plan to use
One letter of recommendation submitted through the portal
opportunities.selection_process: An external committee reviews applications for their likely impact, relevance to the field, originality and sophistication, feasibility, and how well they will use the Folger collections. The committee also aims for disciplinary, methodological and geographical diversity.
important_dates: Information sessions: 9 October and 1 December 2026 (12 pm ET, online)
opportunities.about_provider: The Folger Shakespeare Library in Washington, DC holds one of the world's largest collections of Shakespeare and early modern printed and manuscript material. Its Folger Institute runs fellowships, seminars and other programmes for researchers.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Prepare the abstract, project description, CV and source list, then apply through the Folger fellowship portal (onlineapplicationportal.com/folgerfellowships). opportunities.notes: Use the Folger catalogue and finding aids to name concrete items in your source list; vague lists weaken an application. The online information session on 1 December 2026 is a good chance to ask questions.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers of any nationality, from doctoral students to independent scholars and archive professionals, can apply by 15 January 2027 for a USD 4,500 Houghton Library visiting fellowship of at least four weeks at Harvard.
opportunities.description:
Houghton Library, Harvard University's main library for rare books and manuscripts, offers visiting fellowships for researchers who need to work with its collections. For the 2027-2028 fellowship year (July to June), the library is awarding fellowships from 15 endowed funds; applicants submit one application and the committee decides which fellowship fits each project.

Fellows must spend at least four weeks in residence at Houghton Library in Cambridge, Massachusetts. The library is keen on projects with a global outlook and contemporary relevance, and some of the named fellowships have a specific focus, for example the Hyde Fellowship for research on early modern Black lives, including Africa and the African diaspora between 1500 and 1800.

The programme is open to all nationalities and to a wide range of researchers, from doctoral students to independent scholars and museum or archive professionals, which makes it a realistic option for African researchers working with historical, literary or archival sources held at Harvard.
opportunities.benefits: A stipend of USD 4,500 for the fellowship, paid two to three weeks after arrival. Fellows pay their own travel, housing and taxes; non-US fellows need a J-1 visa, which Harvard sponsors, but the visa fees are paid by the fellow.
requirements: Open to all nationalities
Doctoral students, postdocs, faculty, independent scholars, curators and library, archive or museum professionals
Aged 18 or over
Must not live within commuting distance of Harvard
Research must use Houghton Library holdings
At least four weeks in residence during July 2027 to June 2028
Past fellows must wait five years before applying again
documents: Project proposal of up to 500 words
Preliminary list of Houghton holdings you will consult
opportunities.selection_process: A selection committee reviews all applications and assigns each successful applicant to one of 15 endowed fellowships. Proposals that do not name Houghton materials are not considered; the library favours projects with a global lens and present-day relevance. Some fellowships carry extra conditions, such as ASECS membership for the Bate/Bryant ASECS fellowship.
important_dates: Fellowship year: July 2027 to June 2028 (minimum four weeks in residence)
opportunities.about_provider: Houghton Library is Harvard University's principal repository for rare books, manuscripts and archives. It supports outside researchers through a programme of endowed visiting fellowships.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the Houghton Library Visiting Fellowship Program 2027-2028 form on Submittable (houghtonlibrary.submittable.com), uploading the proposal, holdings list and CV and arranging one reference letter. You do not need to choose a particular named fellowship. Questions go to Peter X. Accardo at Houghton Library.
opportunities.notes: Search HOLLIS and the Houghton finding aids before applying so that your holdings list is precise. Budget for travel, housing and J-1 visa fees, since the USD 4,500 stipend does not cover everything.

opportunities.title: Lalor Foundation Postdoctoral Fellowship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Early-career PhD or MD researchers of any nationality in mammalian reproductive biology can apply by 15 January 2027 for a USD 67,000 one-year postdoctoral fellowship at a nonprofit research institution.
opportunities.description:
The Lalor Foundation's Postdoctoral Fellowship Program supports early-career scientists who want to do research in mammalian reproductive biology, especially work connected to the regulation of fertility. The foundation funds one year of postdoctoral training at a nonprofit research institution, with the possibility of a second, renewal year.

Fellowships usually begin in May or June and last 12 months. Applicants of any citizenship may apply, and the host institution can be in any country, provided it is a nonprofit research organisation that can prove its status.

For African PhD and MD graduates in reproductive biology, endocrinology, veterinary science or related fields, the fellowship offers a well-funded first postdoc, either at an institution abroad or at an eligible nonprofit institute at home.
opportunities.benefits: USD 67,000 per year, covering the fellow's stipend, fringe benefits and institutional overhead (overhead may not exceed 5%). Other costs are not allowed. One renewal year may be granted.
requirements: Any citizenship
PhD or MD level training (or in the final year of the doctorate, with the degree expected in the application year)
No faculty appointment at instructor level or above
The foundation prefers applicants who received their doctorate no more than two years before
Host must be a nonprofit research institution (US hosts need 501(c)(3) status and an IRS 'not a private foundation' letter; non-US hosts must prove nonprofit status)
Research in mammalian reproductive biology related to fertility regulation
documents: Appendix A: project narrative of up to 5 pages including figures and references
Appendix B: four letters (two independent expert reviews, one reference letter and one sponsor/mentor letter), with NIH-style biographical sketches
Appendix C: signed institutional representation form
opportunities.selection_process: A confidential scientific review committee scores each application on three equally weighted criteria: the host institution and its resources, the applicant's merit, and the scientific merit of the proposal. The top 8 to 12 are ranked for the trustees, who make the final awards.
opportunities.about_provider: The Lalor Foundation is a US private foundation that advances research and innovation in reproductive health. It has long supported early-career researchers in mammalian reproductive biology.

Facilities, equipment and sample numbers needed
One reference letter from a scholar in the field
Statement of expected contributions to the Laboratory and the School

opportunities.about_provider: The American School of Classical Studies at Athens, founded in 1881, is a leading centre for research on Greece. Its Wiener Laboratory specialises in archaeological science.

opportunities.description:
Pomona College, a liberal arts college in Claremont, California, gives need-based financial aid to international students. There is no separate named scholarship: aid is awarded from the college's own funds based on each family's financial need, and it is set at the time of admission.

Admission for international students is need-aware, which means the admission committee takes financial need into account. Students who do not apply for aid when they apply cannot ask for it later, so applicants who need support must apply for aid at the same time as admission.

The remaining deadlines are 15 January for Early Decision II and Regular Decision (the Early Decision I deadline of 15 November has passed). For African students, Pomona's need-based aid can cover a large part of the cost of a US liberal arts degree.

opportunities.selection_process: Aid is calculated on demonstrated need, and financial need is considered by the Admissions Committee when it decides on international applicants.

opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply to Pomona and, by the same deadline, submit the CSS Profile (or Pomona's international aid form) and translated income documents. Admitted students who did not apply for aid cannot appeal for aid later.
opportunities.notes: The CSS Profile opens on 1 October. The deadlines page does not print a year; the January dates apply to the current admission cycle for fall 2027 entry.

opportunities.title: Reading AHRC Doctoral Landscape Awards 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Prospective arts and humanities PhD students, including international applicants, who apply to an eligible Reading PhD by 15 January 2027 can be considered for one of three AHRC studentships paying home fees and a GBP 21,805 stipend.
opportunities.description:
The University of Reading offers three AHRC Doctoral Landscape Award studentships a year for PhD study in the arts and humanities, starting in October 2027. The awards are funded by the Arts and Humanities Research Council through its Doctoral Landscape scheme and administered by Reading's Doctoral and Researcher College.

Applicants first apply for a place on an eligible Reading PhD programme by 15 January 2027 and then complete an expression of interest. Departments nominate their strongest candidates to a university panel.

International applicants, including Africans, can win up to 30% of the awards, but the studentship pays fees only at the home rate, so they must find the difference between home and international fees themselves.
opportunities.benefits: Tuition fees at the UK/Republic of Ireland rate, a tax-free stipend (2026/27 rate GBP 21,805 a year) and limited research and training funds. Visa costs and the immigration health surcharge are not covered.
requirements: Apply for a place on an eligible arts and humanities PhD programme at Reading by 15 January 2027
Full-time or part-time study, not by distance learning
Not already a Reading PhD student
International applicants must pay the difference between home and international fees (at least GBP 16,512 a year full-time)
documents: Expression of interest form for the studentship
Revised research proposal if invited (by 1 March 2027)
opportunities.selection_process: Departments review applicants and nominate candidates to a university panel, which judges academic excellence and readiness for research, the quality of the proposal and the supervision arrangements. Nominated applicants are asked to revise their proposal by 1 March 2027.
important_dates: Revised proposals from nominees: by 1 March 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Reading is a research-intensive UK university. Its Doctoral and Researcher College manages doctoral funding, including UKRI-funded studentships.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for an eligible Reading PhD programme by 15 January 2027, then complete the studentship expression of interest form linked from the funding page. Discuss your proposal with a potential supervisor first.
opportunities.notes: Only three awards are made each year. International applicants should plan how they will cover the fee difference before applying.

opportunities.title: Rider University First-Year Merit Scholarships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: First-year applicants for 2027 entry who apply to Rider University by 15 January 2027 with at least a 2.7 GPA are automatically considered for merit scholarships of USD 15,000 to 28,000 a year.
opportunities.description:
Rider University, a private university in Lawrenceville, New Jersey, awards merit scholarships to first-year students entering in Spring 2027, Fall 2027 or Spring 2028. The awards are given automatically on admission, with no separate application, and can be renewed for up to four years.

Rider is test-optional and considers students for most merit awards without SAT or ACT scores. To be considered for the merit scholarships, students should submit their admission application by 15 January.

The official pages do not describe a separate scholarship just for international students, but they also set no citizenship condition on the merit awards, so international applicants who meet the grade threshold are considered as part of admission. African applicants should confirm with Rider's international admissions office.
opportunities.benefits: Merit scholarships of USD 15,000 to 28,000 per year, renewable for up to four years. Smaller awards include a USD 1,000-a-year Bronc Visit Award for eligible campus visitors and subject awards such as USD 2,000 a year in accounting and up to USD 5,000 a year in teacher education.
requirements: Admissible as a full-time first-year student
Minimum unweighted cumulative GPA of 2.7 on a 4.0 scale
Audition where the programme requires one
Test-optional: SAT/ACT not needed for most merit awards
Keep a 2.0 cumulative GPA to renew
documents: Audition materials for performing arts programmes
opportunities.selection_process: Admitted first-year students are automatically reviewed for merit awards based on their academic record; no separate scholarship application is required.
important_dates: Musical Theatre and Acting applicants: by 15 November
Application for merit consideration: by 15 January 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Rider University is a private university in Lawrenceville, New Jersey, offering undergraduate and graduate programmes in business, education, arts and sciences, and the performing arts.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for first-year admission through Rider's international admissions process by 15 January 2027; scholarship decisions arrive with the admission offer. Contact Rider One Stop (onestop@rider.edu) with aid questions.
opportunities.notes: The New Jersey Tuition Guarantee applies only to New Jersey residents. Need-based aid at Rider uses the FAFSA, which is generally for US citizens.

opportunities.title: Schwarz Fellowship for Research on Music 2027-28 (Gennadius Library)
opportunities.provider: American School of Classical Studies at Athens
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to career musicians, PhD candidates and scholars within five years of the PhD, of any nationality, researching music; apply by 15 January 2027.
opportunities.description:
The Schwarz Fellowship supports research on music, including Greek and Byzantine musical traditions, carried out with the collections of the Gennadius Library at the American School of Classical Studies at Athens (ASCSA).

The award supports research in Athens during the 2027-28 academic year, and fellows are expected to make full use of the library's rare books, archives and open-stack collections.

The ASCSA states that the fellowship is open to all nationalities, so African doctoral students and early-career researchers working on Greek, Byzantine, Ottoman or Mediterranean topics can apply.
opportunities.benefits: Stipend of US$11,500 for the academic year, as listed on the ASCSA fellowships page.
requirements: Eligible career stage: career musicians, PhD candidates and scholars within five years of the PhD
Research that requires the Gennadius Library collections
Open to all nationalities
documents: Online application on the ASCSA Submittable portal
Reference letters as requested on the form
opportunities.selection_process: A School committee reviews the applications; awards are announced in the spring.
opportunities.about_provider: The American School of Classical Studies at Athens, founded in 1881, is a leading research centre on Greece. Its Gennadius Library holds more than 150,000 titles on Greece from antiquity to the present.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Complete the fellowship form on the ASCSA Submittable portal before the deadline, uploading your CV and project description and arranging the requested references.
opportunities.notes: Application form: https://ascsa.submittable.com/submit/189405/schwarz-fellowship-at-the-gennadius-library-for-research-on-music

opportunities.title: Smith College Need-Based Financial Aid for International First-Year Students (Fall 2027 entry)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-US citizens applying as first-year (or transfer) students for September 2027 can receive need-based aid that meets their full documented need, but only if they apply for aid together with their admission application and by the aid deadlines.
opportunities.description:
Smith College, a private liberal arts college for women in Northampton, Massachusetts, offers need-based financial aid to international students who are not US citizens. Aid for the September 2027 entry is awarded alongside the admission decision, and for admitted students who applied for aid on time the college commits to covering their full documented financial need with grants rather than loans.

The main award is the Smith Grant, which is sized from the family's assessed ability to pay against the full cost of attendance (tuition, housing, food, fees, insurance, books, travel and personal costs). The college adjusts the grant over the years so that the family's expected contribution stays broadly stable. International students who receive need-based aid also get a grant covering the college health insurance.

The programme matters for African applicants because Smith is one of a small group of US colleges that meet full need for international students, which can make a degree costing over USD 100,000 a year affordable. The pool is very competitive, and the college states that the level of support varies widely between students. The timing rule is strict: an international student who does not ask for aid before being admitted can never receive institutional aid at Smith later.
opportunities.benefits: A need-based Smith Grant that, together with any outside support, meets 100% of the documented need of admitted students who applied for aid by the deadlines; undergraduate institutional packages contain no loans. Recipients also receive a health grant that covers the college health insurance. For reference, the published 2026-27 cost of attendance is: tuition USD 70,460; food and housing USD 24,520; student activities fee USD 308; health insurance USD 4,030; books USD 800; international transport (average) USD 1,000; personal costs USD 1,910.
requirements: Not a US citizen (international applicant)
Applying for first-year (or transfer) entry in September 2027
Must apply for financial aid at the same time as applying for admission and by the aid deadlines; no institutional aid is ever offered to international students who did not apply before admission

English proficiency (TOEFL, IELTS, PTE or Duolingo) unless English is the first language, secondary school was taught in English, the student had two years of US English-medium schooling, or holds an IB Diploma or A-levels taught in English
SAT/ACT scores are optional
Women's college: applicants apply under Smith's admission policy for women
documents: Secondary school report with official transcript
Midyear report (by 15 February for Regular Decision)
CSS Profile 2027-28 (Smith code 3762; fee waivers available)
Translated and signed 2025 parent tax return, or the International Parent Non-Filer form plus a translated employer statement of income
Optional standardised test scores and English test results where required
opportunities.selection_process: Admission is holistic, looking at the student's academic record, recommendations, writing and activities. Financial aid staff then review the CSS Profile and income documents using federal and institutional methods to work out the family contribution and the student's need against the cost of attendance. Admission of international applicants is competitive and aid amounts differ widely between students.
important_dates: Early Decision I application and CSS Profile: 15 November 2026
Early Decision II application: 5 January 2027 (aid forms 6 January 2027)
opportunities.about_provider: Smith College is a private women's liberal arts college in Northampton, Massachusetts, USA. It admits first-year and transfer students and awards both need-based aid and merit awards, with merit decided only at the time of admission.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the Common Application or Coalition on Scoir (no application fee) and mark that you are applying for aid. Complete the 2027-28 CSS Profile on the College Board site and upload translated tax or income documents through IDOC; Smith then emails instructions for its Net Partner aid portal. Meet the deadline for your chosen round (Early Decision I, Early Decision II or Regular Decision).
opportunities.notes: Early Decision is binding, but a student can be released if the aid offered makes attendance impossible. Outside scholarships first reduce the work-study portion and then the Smith Grant; state or federal grants reduce the Smith Grant dollar for dollar. International students may not take off-campus jobs. Contact Student Financial Services at sfs@smith.edu or +1 413-585-2530.

opportunities.title: Stockholm University Scholarship Scheme 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Fee-paying non-EU/EEA applicants who apply to a Stockholm University master's by 15 January 2027 and are admitted can receive a full tuition scholarship.
opportunities.description:
Stockholm University's Scholarship Scheme pays the full tuition fee for selected fee-paying students from outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland who are admitted to a master's programme starting in autumn 2027. It does not cover living costs.

To be considered, students must apply in the first, international admission round on universityadmissions.se, which closes on 15 January 2027. After the selection results on 1 April, eligible admitted students receive an electronic scholarship application form in their University Admissions account.

Awards are based on academic merit, and priority goes to students who ranked Stockholm University as their first choice, which is a useful tip for African applicants choosing between Swedish universities.
opportunities.benefits: Covers the whole tuition fee for the master's programme. Living costs are not covered.

Admitted to a master's programme in the first (international) admission round for autumn 2027
Bachelor's degree of at least 180 ECTS or equivalent
English equivalent to Swedish upper-secondary English 6/B
Stockholm University listed as first choice gives priority
documents: Application on universityadmissions.se with degree certificates, transcripts and English proof
Application fee paid and documents uploaded by 1 February 2027
Scholarship form sent after admission results
opportunities.selection_process: Scholarships are awarded on academic merit among admitted fee-paying students, with priority for those who ranked Stockholm University first.
important_dates: Scholarship results: by end of April 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Stockholm University is one of Sweden's largest universities, with a broad range of English-taught master's programmes in the sciences, humanities, social sciences and law.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for your master's programme on universityadmissions.se by 15 January 2027 and rank Stockholm University first. Pay the fee and upload documents by 1 February; if admitted and eligible, complete the scholarship form that appears in your account.
opportunities.notes: Business programmes may require GMAT or GRE. Also look at the Swedish Institute scholarships, which are limited to citizens of selected countries.

opportunities.title: University of Copenhagen Danish Government Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-EU/EEA applicants admitted to a University of Copenhagen master's who apply by 15 January 2027 are automatically considered for a full tuition waiver plus living allowance.
opportunities.description:
The University of Copenhagen awards a limited number of Danish Government Scholarships each year to non-EU/EEA students admitted to its MA and MSc programmes. The scholarships are funded by the Danish state and are given purely on academic merit; financial need is not considered.

There is no separate application. Every eligible non-EU/EEA applicant to a master's starting in September 2027 is considered automatically, provided they apply in the round that closes on 15 January 2027.

For African students, this is one of the most generous master's awards in the Nordic countries, covering both tuition and basic living costs for the whole two-year degree.
opportunities.benefits: Full tuition fee waiver and basic living costs for 22 months (DKK 11,225 per month at the 2026 level).
requirements: Citizen of a country outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland
Admitted to a University of Copenhagen MA or MSc programme
Granted a time-limited Danish residence permit for study
Not entitled to Danish citizen rights or the Danish SU state grant
Strong academic record (merit-based)
documents: Regular master's application documents (no separate scholarship application)
Payment of the DKK 1,120 application fee
opportunities.selection_process: Awards are made on academic criteria during the admission assessment. Offers must be accepted by the stated deadline or they are withdrawn.
opportunities.about_provider: Founded in 1479, the University of Copenhagen is Denmark's oldest and largest university and one of the leading research universities in Europe.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Pay the application fee, then apply for your chosen master's through the University of Copenhagen application portal by 15 January 2027. Eligible applicants are considered automatically and must accept any scholarship offer by the deadline.
opportunities.notes: Estimated living costs are €1,280-1,800 a month; the allowance covers basic costs only.

opportunities.title: University of Notre Dame Need-Blind Admission and Financial Aid for International Undergraduates (Fall 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International first-year applicants are admitted need-blind and considered for need-based University scholarships by submitting the 2027-28 CSS Profile by 15 January 2027 (application due 1 January 2027).

opportunities.title: University of South Florida Green and Gold International Scholarships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International first-year applicants for Summer or Fall 2027 who complete their USF application by 15 January 2027 are automatically considered for Green and Gold tuition waivers worth up to USD 11,000 a year.
opportunities.description:
The University of South Florida (USF), a large public research university in Tampa, Florida, gives Green and Gold tuition waivers to international first-year students it admits for Summer or Fall 2027. These are merit awards that reduce tuition each year for up to four years.

There is no separate scholarship form. Every international first-year applicant who submits a complete application by the scholarship consideration date is automatically reviewed, using the same academic record that the admissions team uses. The number of awards is limited, so applying early and completely matters.

For African school leavers who want a US bachelor's degree, the waivers can cut the cost of an international tuition bill substantially, but they do not cover the full cost of study, so applicants should plan for the remaining tuition, housing and living costs.
opportunities.benefits: Green and Gold Presidential Waiver of about USD 44,000 in total (up to USD 11,000 a year); Directors Waiver of about USD 36,000 (up to USD 9,000 a year); Scholars Waiver of about USD 20,000 (up to USD 5,000 a year). These cannot be combined with USF's out-of-state merit tuition waivers.
requirements: International applicant for first-year (freshman) entry in Summer or Fall 2027
Complete application, including test scores, transcripts and fee, by 15 January 2027

For applicants whose first language is not English: SAT Reading and Writing 490+, or ACT English 17+ and Reading 19+, or CLT Verbal Reasoning and Writing 38+ (TOEFL, IELTS and Duolingo are not accepted in place of these for this purpose)
Awards are based on the academic record used for admission
documents: USF online application or Common App
STARS self-reported record or official secondary school transcripts
Official SAT, ACT or CLT scores sent by the testing agency (SAT code 5828, ACT code 0761)
