important_dates: Take SAT/ACT before December so scores arrive in time for Fall decisions
Award notice: by post, also visible in the Student Self-Service portal
opportunities.about_provider: The University of South Florida is a public research university based in Tampa, Florida, with campuses in St. Petersburg and Sarasota-Manatee. Its Office of Admissions handles international first-year applications and merit awards.

No extra scholarship form is needed; track your file and any award in the USF applicant and Self-Service portals.
opportunities.notes: Questions go to USF International Admissions (international@usf.edu). Because English is assessed through SAT, ACT or CLT section scores, plan your test dates early.

opportunities.title: XJTLU Postgraduate Research Scholarships for funded PhD projects (2027 intakes)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants with a bachelor's and master's (or equivalent) and an English test who apply to a listed XJTLU PhD project.
opportunities.description:
Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool University (XJTLU) in Suzhou, China, funds full-time PhD students through its Postgraduate Research Scholarships. Students join a listed research project, study for three years, and receive a University of Liverpool PhD degree after a final review by Liverpool.

There are three levels of award: a full scholarship (tuition waiver plus a monthly stipend), a fees-only scholarship, and a partial award that cuts tuition by up to half. Funded projects are advertised across areas such as AI and advanced technology, life and natural sciences, design and semiconductors, and each stays open until filled.

For 2027 entry, applications for existing funded projects close on 15 January 2027 (start 1 June 2027) and 30 April 2027 (start 1 September 2027). The scheme sets no nationality limit, so African master's graduates can compete for a funded PhD with a UK degree while living in China.
opportunities.benefits: Full scholarship: tuition waiver worth RMB 297,000 over three years plus a stipend of RMB 5,000 per month for three years (RMB 180,000 in total); holders must take a teaching or research assistant role. Fees-only scholarship: tuition waiver worth RMB 297,000. Partial scholarship: up to 50% off tuition for three years (worth RMB 148,500). Paid TA/RA roles may also be offered to other award holders.
requirements: Full-time PhD study at XJTLU in Suzhou
Bachelor's and master's degree (or enrolment statement if not yet completed)
English test certificate (IELTS or equivalent)
Application to a specific advertised funded project, ideally after contacting the supervisor
documents: Two references, at least one academic, on letterhead with a handwritten signature
Master's dissertation (Business, Humanities and Social Sciences applicants)
opportunities.selection_process: XJTLU reviews the application first and the University of Liverpool makes the final decision. Merit-based awards are judged on academic excellence, research potential, research experience and achievements.
important_dates: Self-funded / merit scholarship round 2: 15 January 2027 (start 1 September 2027)
opportunities.about_provider: Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool University is a joint-venture university in Suzhou, China, founded by Xi'an Jiaotong University and the University of Liverpool. Its PhD degrees are awarded by the University of Liverpool.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Choose a funded project on the scholarships page and contact the supervisor, then apply through XJTLU's online 'Apply Now' form, uploading the proposal, transcripts, English test and references (each file under 2 MB, in English or with certified translations). Questions go to doctoralstudies@xjtlu.edu.cn.
opportunities.notes: Projects close once filled, so apply early. Minimum English scores are on XJTLU's PhD entry requirements page.

opportunities.title: CEGA Visiting Fellowship for African Researchers 2027/2028
opportunities.provider: Center for Effective Global Action (UC Berkeley)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Social science researchers and practitioners from East and West Africa with at least a master's can apply by 17 January 2027 for a 16-week CEGA impact-evaluation fellowship at Berkeley or online.
opportunities.description:
The Center for Effective Global Action (CEGA) at the University of California, Berkeley runs a 16-week Visiting Fellowship that trains East and West African researchers and practitioners in impact evaluation. The 2027-2028 cohort can join in Fall 2027 (August to December) or Spring 2028 (January to May), either as Resident fellows at Berkeley or as Non-Resident fellows working online.

There are two tracks: a Practitioner track (about 7 places) for staff of NGOs, think tanks and ministries, and an Academic track (about 4 places) for doctoral students and university or research staff. Fellows build skills in rigorous evaluation, research design and evidence use, and are expected to return to an institution in East or West Africa.

Alumni can later compete for CEGA's catalyst, pilot and research grants, so the fellowship is also an entry point into a wider research network on development economics.
opportunities.benefits: Resident fellows: round-trip flights, accommodation, meals, visa fees, health insurance and a stipend. Non-Resident fellows: a stipend for internet and data costs. No salary or family support is provided.
requirements: National of an East or West African country (not open to Southern, Central or North Africa)
Completed at least secondary school in Africa
At least a master's degree, or enrolled in a PhD, or PhD completed within the last 8 years, in a social science
Fluent English
Plan to return to an institution in East or West Africa
Resident track only: national of a J-1-eligible country (Djibouti, Ethiopia, Ghana, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Kenya, Liberia, Madagascar, Mauritius, Mozambique, Rwanda, Seychelles, Uganda)
Practitioner track: works for an NGO, think tank or ministry; Academic track: doctoral student or university/research staff
Employer leave or support for 40 h/week (Resident) or 15-20 h/week (Non-Resident) for four months
documents: Policy statement (Practitioner) or research proposal (Academic), max 2 pages
Letter from employer approving leave or time commitment
opportunities.selection_process: CEGA reviews applications by track, looking at academic and professional background, quantitative preparation, the policy statement or research proposal, and the applicant's plans to apply evaluation skills in East or West Africa.
opportunities.about_provider: CEGA is a research centre at UC Berkeley that connects researchers and policymakers to generate rigorous evidence on poverty and development. Its African fellowship programme builds evaluation capacity among researchers from the region.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit the application through CEGA's Submittable portal (2027-28 CEGA Visiting Fellowship). Prepare the statements, CV and employer letter in advance, and register for the 2 December webinar from the call page. Questions go to global-networks-cega@berkeley.edu.
opportunities.notes: Non-Resident priority countries include Benin, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Côte d'Ivoire, Gambia, Malawi, Mali, Mauritania, Niger, Nigeria, Senegal, Sierra Leone, Tanzania, Togo, Zambia and Zimbabwe. The full call is also available as a PDF from the CEGA page.

opportunities.title: CUHK School of Journalism and Communication Internationalization Scholarship 2027-28

Programme deadlines are 7 December 2026 for the priority round and 18 January 2027 for the final round; the MSc in AI and Communication accepts applications until 31 March 2027. Applying in the priority round gives the best chance of being considered.

For African journalists and communication graduates the award offers a useful contribution towards the cost of a one-year master's at one of Asia's leading communication schools.
opportunities.benefits: HK$80,000 per award; five awards are available each year.

Strong academic merit
Able to add to the international mix of the class

opportunities.title: IJP Southern Africa Federal President Horst Köhler Fellowship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Journalists aged 25-40 from SADC countries or Kenya can apply by 20 January 2027 for a two-month placement in a German newsroom with a EUR 3,500 bursary.
opportunities.description:
The International Journalists' Programmes (IJP) run the Federal President Horst Köhler Fellowship, an exchange that places journalists from Southern Africa in German newsrooms for about two months. In 2027 the Southern African fellows are expected to travel in July and August (to be confirmed), starting with an introductory conference in Berlin.

During the placement, fellows work at a German media outlet and produce stories for their home newsroom, building contacts and reporting on Germany and Europe. German journalists take part in the reverse exchange to Southern Africa.

The programme is mainly funded by the German Federal Foreign Office. It is open to journalists from SADC member states and Kenya, and up to five Southern African journalists are chosen each year.
opportunities.benefits: A fixed bursary of EUR 3,500, expected to cover most travel, accommodation and living costs during the fellowship. The full grant depends on a report of at least three pages and copies of published work after the fellowship.
requirements: Journalist from a SADC member state or Kenya
Aged 25 to 40
Working regularly for a media organisation
Strong English; German is an advantage
Employer must agree to the leave of absence
documents: CV with passport photo (and language certificates if available)
Essay of about 800 words: why Germany, three research topics, future role at your home outlet, planned use of the bursary
Reference from your editor-in-chief or head of department that also confirms leave
opportunities.selection_process: A selection committee chooses up to five fellows, and its decision is final. Applicants rank preferred host outlets, and IJP agrees the final placement with each fellow.
important_dates: Fellowship: July and August 2027 (to be confirmed), starting in Berlin
opportunities.about_provider: IJP is a German non-profit organisation that runs exchange programmes for journalists from many world regions. Its Southern Africa programme is named after former German Federal President Horst Köhler.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Email the CV, essay, work samples and editor's reference to IJP (office@ijp.org) between 1 November 2026 and 20 January 2027. Read the 2027 call PDF on the programme page for the list of eligible countries.
opportunities.notes: Programme coordinator: Marco Vollmar at IJP. Plan research topics that suit German host outlets, as they influence placement.

opportunities.title: Kupcinet-Getz International Summer Program 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Bachelor's or master's students past their first year, or recent bachelor's graduates, with a GPA of at least 3.6 can join an eight-week summer research program with a $1,100 stipend and a flight subsidy.

opportunities.title: LISS DTP ESRC Open Competition 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Social science graduates with strong grades, including international applicants, can apply by 20 January 2027 for ESRC-funded doctoral studentships at King's, Queen Mary or Imperial through LISS DTP.
opportunities.description:
The London Interdisciplinary Social Science Doctoral Training Partnership (LISS DTP) is funded by the UK Economic and Social Research Council and led by King's College London with Imperial College London and Queen Mary University of London. Its open competition offers social science doctoral studentships starting in October 2027.

Applicants choose one of two formats: 1+3.5 (a master's year followed by a PhD) or +3.5 (PhD only). They must also apply to a relevant programme at one of the three partner universities and secure supervisor support.

Both home and international students may apply, but UKRI rules cap international awards at 30%, so competition for those places is strong. African social scientists with excellent grades and a well-developed project are eligible.
opportunities.benefits: ESRC studentship covering tuition fees and a stipend for the length of the award; the international fee difference is covered only for a limited number of international students. Visa, immigration health surcharge and travel costs are not covered.
requirements: First degree at first class or upper second (average of 65% or above)
For the +3.5 route, a master's at distinction or high merit
Apply to a relevant programme at King's, Queen Mary or Imperial
Not already holding a PhD, and at least 50% of study time remaining if already enrolled
Live within reasonable travel distance of London once funded
Home and international applicants eligible (international awards capped at 30%)
documents: Online application in the LISS DTP portal (liss-dtp.flexigrant.com)
Official transcripts showing modules, credits and grades (certified translations if needed)
One reference from someone who is not your supervisor, on letterhead
KCL fee-waiver form (by 18 January) or Imperial departmental support form where relevant
opportunities.selection_process: Academic reviewers longlist applications, which are then scored, discussed by research-area panels and finalised by a high-level panel. No individual feedback is given.
important_dates: Final outcomes: end of April 2027 (offers week of 27 April)
opportunities.about_provider: LISS DTP is one of the ESRC's doctoral training partnerships, bringing together King's College London, Imperial College London and Queen Mary University of London to train social science researchers.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Agree a project with a supervisor at King's, Queen Mary or Imperial, apply for the PhD (or master's plus PhD) there, and submit the LISS DTP application in its portal by 20 January 2027. Contact liss-dtp@kcl.ac.uk with questions.
opportunities.notes: Apply for one format only (1+3.5 or +3.5). LISS also offers CASE studentships with partner organisations.

opportunities.title: University of York AHRC Doctoral Landscape Awards in the Arts and Humanities 2027/28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK and international applicants with an outstanding record and a York PhD offer in an AHRC subject can apply by 20 January 2027; international winners must cover the gap between home and international fees.
opportunities.description:
The University of York awards six AHRC Doctoral Landscape Awards for PhD students in the arts and humanities who start in September 2027. The studentships are funded by the Arts and Humanities Research Council, part of UK Research and Innovation, and cover research within the AHRC's remit, whether based in York's Faculty of Arts and Humanities or in its science and social science faculties.

Each award pays a tax-free living stipend and waives tuition at the UK (home) rate. International applicants, including those from Africa, are eligible, but the award does not pay the difference between home and international fees, so they need other funds to cover it.

York runs an online information session on 18 November 2026 and an application-writing workshop on 25 November 2026 for interested applicants.
opportunities.benefits: A stipend of GBP 21,805 a year (2026/27 rate; 2027/28 rates published early 2027) plus a tuition fee waiver at the UK home rate. International students must pay the difference between home and international fees themselves.
requirements: An offer of a PhD place in a relevant York department, starting September 2027 (no deferrals)
Outstanding academic record, usually a first-class degree and a master's Distinction or equivalent experience
Research within the AHRC subject remit
Must live in the UK within reasonable distance of York during the PhD; distance learning is not funded
Not already a doctoral student and not in full-time employment at the start
documents: Separate PhD application to York (advised by early December 2026)
opportunities.selection_process: Each department ranks its candidates, and a Faculty of Arts and Humanities panel then ranks the whole group. The process finishes by the end of March 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of York is a UK research university and member of the Russell Group. The AHRC is UK Research and Innovation's council for arts and humanities research.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for a PhD place at York, ideally by early December 2026, and complete the AHRC DLA online studentship form by 20 January 2027.
opportunities.notes: Six awards are available. Part-time paid work of up to about six hours a week is allowed with supervisor approval. Contact: pgr-finance@york.ac.uk.

opportunities.title: Wolfson Postgraduate Scholarships in the Humanities, University of York 2027-28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Outstanding humanities graduates of any nationality applying for a York PhD in history, literature or languages can apply by 20 January 2027 for a Wolfson scholarship worth GBP 38,000 a year for three years.
opportunities.description:
The University of York, with funding from the Wolfson Foundation, offers three doctoral scholarships in the humanities for PhD study starting in September 2027. The awards cover history, literature and languages, and are among the most generous humanities PhD awards in the UK.

Each scholarship provides GBP 38,000 a year for three years. It pays home-rate tuition fees and the rest goes towards maintenance, research, travel and training. Overseas students receive the home fee rate only, so they need to cover the difference between home and international fees.

The scholarships are open to all nationalities, so outstanding African humanities graduates with a master's can apply, provided they can arrange the extra fee funding.
opportunities.benefits: GBP 38,000 per year for three years (GBP 114,000 in total), covering home-rate tuition fees and, from the balance, maintenance, research, travel and training costs. Overseas students receive home-rate fees only.
requirements: Applied for (ideally holding an offer for) a PhD in a relevant York department in history, literature or languages, starting September 2027 (no deferral)
Outstanding academic record, usually a first-class undergraduate degree and a master's
Live in the UK for the duration of the award
Open to all nationalities; full-time or part-time
International students must fund the gap between home and international fees
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are passed to scholarship panels, which choose three scholars on academic excellence and the strength of the research project.
important_dates: Submit PhD application: ideally by early December 2026
opportunities.about_provider: The University of York is a research-intensive UK university. The Wolfson Foundation is a UK charity that supports excellence in research and education, including its Wolfson Postgraduate Scholarships in the Humanities.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for your PhD at York (ideally by early December), then complete the online Wolfson scholarship form by 20 January 2027. Questions on funding go to pgr-finance@york.ac.uk.
opportunities.notes: York also offers AHRC Doctoral Landscape Awards in the arts and humanities in the same window.

opportunities.title: ACM CHI 2027 Posters, Demos and Student Research Competition (Pittsburgh)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Posters, interactive demos and Student Research Competition entries for CHI 2027 in Pittsburgh (10-14 May 2027) are due 21 January 2027; no travel funding is stated on the homepage.

opportunities.title: CERN Summer Student Programme 2027 (Member and Non-Member States)
opportunities.provider: CERN, the European Organization for Nuclear Research
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Bachelor's and master's students of any nationality in physics, engineering, computer science or maths, with at least three years of full-time study by the start date, can apply by 21 January 2027 for a paid summer at CERN.
opportunities.description:
Every summer CERN, the particle physics laboratory near Geneva, hosts several hundred university students from around the world for its Summer Student Programme. Students spend between eight and thirteen weeks working on a research or technical project in one of CERN's teams, attend a lecture series given by CERN scientists, visit the facilities and write a short final report. The 2027 programme ideally starts on 14 June 2027 and is fully on site.

The programme is open to students of all nationalities, with separate funding channels for member and non-member states; in 2025 CERN's donor-funded programme alone supported 60 students from non-member states. Projects span experimental and theoretical physics, computing, engineering and mathematics.

For African science and engineering students it is one of the best-known paid research placements in Europe, combining hands-on work at the world's largest physics laboratory with an international network of peers.
opportunities.benefits: A net subsistence allowance of 94 CHF per calendar day, health insurance (the contribution is deducted from the allowance), travel expenses depending on individual circumstances, help finding accommodation on or near site, and the summer lecture programme.
requirements: Bachelor's or master's student (not PhD)
At least 6 semesters (3 academic years) of full-time university study in a relevant field by the start date
Field: physics, engineering, computer science or mathematics
Enrolled full time for the whole stay
Good knowledge of English
Not previously a CERN summer student and not at CERN for more than 3 months under another status
Open to all nationalities
documents: Official transcripts in English or French
opportunities.selection_process: CERN reviews the applications and may invite candidates to an online interview, followed by an offer and onboarding.
opportunities.about_provider: CERN is the European Organization for Nuclear Research, an intergovernmental laboratory on the Franco-Swiss border near Geneva. It operates the Large Hadron Collider and hosts scientists from more than 100 countries.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the 'CERN Summer Student Programme 2027' posting on CERN's careers site, which opens an online form (allow about 15 minutes). Upload your CV, transcripts and enrolment certificate, and arrange your academic reference letter.
opportunities.notes: CERN's general page says applications should arrive by the end of January, but the job posting gives 21 January 2027; use the earlier date. A separate CERN openlab summer programme in computing also runs in 2027.

opportunities.title: CERN openlab Summer Student Programme 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Bachelor's or Master's students of any nationality with at least six semesters completed can spend two paid summer months in Geneva working on computing projects.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master SpaceMed (Space Medicine) 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants from all countries with a relevant bachelor's, an engineering master's or a medical degree and B2 English can apply for this space-medicine master's with EMJM scholarships.

opportunities.title: Hanken GBSN Scholarship for Students from Developing Countries 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Students or alumni of listed GBSN member schools in countries including Egypt, Ghana, Kenya, Morocco, Nigeria, Senegal, South Africa and Tunisia can apply by 21 January 2027 for one of two two-year tuition waivers at Hanken.
opportunities.description:
Hanken School of Economics in Finland awards two GBSN scholarships each year to master's applicants who are students or alumni of specific Global Business School Network (GBSN) member schools in listed developing countries. The scholarship waives the full tuition fee for two academic years of an English-taught master's programme.

The award is made only within Hanken's main admission round for English-taught master's degrees, which runs from 7 to 21 January 2027. Applicants are ranked on academic merit, and the best-ranked eligible applicants receive the scholarship.

African countries on the list are Egypt, Ghana, Kenya, Morocco, Nigeria, Senegal, South Africa and Tunisia, so graduates of GBSN member business schools there should check whether their school qualifies.
opportunities.benefits: Full tuition fee waiver for two academic years, equivalent to EUR 15,000 a year. Living costs are not covered.
requirements: Student or alumnus/alumna of a specified GBSN member school in a listed developing country
Applying in the main admission round for an English-taught Hanken master's
Bachelor's degree with at least 25-30 ECTS in relevant subjects
English language requirement met
GMAT, GRE or GTEBS aptitude test, or the GPA route, as required
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants are assessed on academic success and skills from previous studies, scored from 1.00 to 5.00 (minimum 3.00) and ranked; the two scholarships go to top-ranked eligible applicants.
opportunities.about_provider: Hanken School of Economics is a business school in Helsinki and Vaasa, Finland. It is a member of the Global Business School Network, which links business schools working on management education in developing regions.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for an English-taught master's at Hanken through Studyinfo.fi between 7 and 21 January 2027 and indicate your GBSN member school. Contact Hanken admissions if unsure whether your school is eligible.
opportunities.notes: Only two scholarships are awarded a year, so meet all main-round requirements, including the aptitude test, early.

opportunities.title: McGill Major Entrance Scholarships (applicants from outside Canada)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: First-year undergraduate applicants from schools outside Canada can apply separately for renewable merit awards from $3,000 a year, based on academics and leadership.

opportunities.title: University of Eastern Finland Early-Bird Tuition Discount 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-EU/EEA students admitted to a UEF international master's for September 2027 get 30% off first-year tuition if they accept and pay within 21 days; applications close 21 January 2027.
opportunities.description:
The University of Eastern Finland (UEF) gives a 30% early-bird discount on first-year tuition to non-EU/EEA students admitted to its English-taught master's programmes starting in September 2027. Tuition is EUR 10,000 to 12,000 a year, so the discount is worth EUR 3,000 to 3,600.

The discount applies automatically if the student accepts the study place and pays the fee (or the first instalment) within 21 days of the admission results. A further 30% waiver for the second year is available to students who complete at least 55 ECTS in year one and apply separately.

UEF does not offer full tuition waivers or humanitarian scholarships, so African applicants should budget for the remaining fees and living costs of about EUR 900 to 1,000 a month.
opportunities.benefits: 30% off first-year tuition (EUR 3,000 on a EUR 10,000 fee or EUR 3,600 on EUR 12,000); a possible 30% second-year waiver; Finnish Proficiency waivers of EUR 2,500 (A) or EUR 1,500 (B) from 2027-28.
requirements: Non-EU/EEA/Swiss student liable for tuition fees
Admitted to a UEF international master's for the September 2027 intake
Accept the offer and pay the fee or first instalment within 21 days of results
Second-year waiver: at least 55 ECTS completed in year one and a separate application
documents: Studyinfo.fi application with degree certificates, transcripts and English proof
Non-refundable application fee for non-EU applicants
opportunities.selection_process: No separate scholarship selection for the first year: the discount applies to every fee-liable admitted student who accepts and pays on time.
important_dates: Payment for the discount: within 21 days of admission results
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Eastern Finland is a multidisciplinary university with campuses in Joensuu and Kuopio. It offers international master's programmes in fields such as forestry, health sciences, computing and education.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for a UEF international master's on Studyinfo.fi between 7 and 21 January 2027. When admitted, accept the place and pay within 21 days to receive the early-bird discount automatically.
opportunities.notes: Finnish immigration requires proof of EUR 800 a month for living costs; UEF recommends EUR 900-1,000.

opportunities.title: Åbo Akademi University International Master's Tuition Fee Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Fee-paying international applicants admitted to an August 2027 master's programme (apply 7 to 21 January 2027) automatically get EUR 4,000 off in year one and EUR 4,000 in year two.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers can submit abstracts by 22 January 2027 for the ACM conference on user modelling, adaptation and personalization in Chicago.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Visiting fellowship at Cambridge for arts, humanities and social science scholars from the Global South.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Erasmus Mundus master's in geospatial data science and Earth observation that welcomes students worldwide; call open until 22 January 2027.

opportunities.title: EMBO Postdoctoral Fellowships (January 2027 round)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to researchers of any nationality within two years of their PhD who have a first-author publication and are moving to a lab in another country; 22 January 2027 is the cutoff for the next selection round.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus CLMCE - Children's Literature, Media and Cultural Entrepreneurship
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Graduates of any nationality with a first degree and good English may apply by 22 January 2027 for a fully funded two-year Erasmus Mundus master's in children's literature, media and cultural entrepreneurship.
opportunities.description:
Children's Literature, Media and Cultural Entrepreneurship (CLMCE) is a two-year, full-time Erasmus Mundus International Master that looks at books, media and creative industries made for young audiences, combining literary and cultural study with the business side of producing and selling cultural content. The University of Glasgow coordinates the programme on behalf of a European university consortium, and the course is co-funded by the European Union through the Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters scheme.

Students spend their study periods at different partner universities in at least two countries; the third semester is taken at a consortium institution allocated according to the student's ranking. The intake covered here is the fourth edition (2027-2029), starting in September 2027.

Across its four editions the consortium can offer up to 90 Erasmus Mundus scholarships (60 regular and 30 targeted places). These awards pay all tuition plus a monthly allowance, which makes the programme a fully funded route into Europe for African graduates interested in publishing, children's media, storytelling, education or cultural entrepreneurship.
opportunities.benefits: Erasmus Mundus scholarship holders have all tuition fees and travel insurance covered and receive EUR 1,400 per month for 24 months (up to EUR 33,600 in total). Students can instead choose three advance payments of EUR 1,000 (to help with visa and travel costs) followed by EUR 1,275 per month.
requirements: A first higher-education degree (bachelor's or recognised equivalent); final-year students may apply if they graduate before the course starts
Proof of English for applicants whose first language is not English, uploaded by the scholarship deadline (minimum score set by the University of Glasgow)
Must not have held an Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters scholarship before
At most six scholarships per nationality across the four editions; dual nationals must say which nationality they apply under
Study must take place in at least two countries different from the country of residence at enrolment
documents: CLMCE scholarship application form (uploaded as PDF)
Degree certificate(s), if completed, in the original language
Transcripts with grades, plus official English translations
Two reference letters on letterhead (one academic; the second academic or professional)
opportunities.selection_process: Stage 1 checks eligibility and shortlists candidates on academic excellence. Stage 2 ranks shortlisted applicants on their personal statement and motivation, academic record and English, other relevant experience, and references. Results are emailed in April 2027; appeals are possible within 14 days on procedural grounds only.
important_dates: Erasmus Mundus scholarship deadline: 22 January 2027, 13:00 UK time
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Glasgow, founded in 1451, is one of the UK's oldest universities and acts as coordinating institution for the CLMCE consortium. Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters are flagship EU-funded programmes run jointly by several universities in different countries.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online through the University of Glasgow postgraduate application portal using the Apply Now link on the CLMCE how-to-apply page, and upload the scholarship form and all documents. Once started, an application must be completed within 42 days. Questions go through the university's online enquiry form, choosing Erasmus as the level of study.
opportunities.notes: Applicants without a master's degree may be preferred when required. Leave time for referees to prepare letters on letterhead before the January deadline.

opportunities.title: Fordham University International Student Merit Scholarships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International first-year applicants to Fordham are automatically considered for merit awards of USD 10,000-25,000 a year.
opportunities.description:
Fordham University in New York City considers every complete first-year application from international students for merit scholarships of USD 10,000 to 25,000 a year. No separate scholarship application is needed: the award, if any, is shown in the online admission letter.

Awards are renewed at the same amount for up to four years as long as the student keeps the required GPA and satisfactory academic progress. Fordham also gives a limited amount of need-based aid to international students, but its admission is need-aware and need-based awards do not cover the full cost.

For the current admission cycle, the Regular Decision deadline has been extended from 3 January to 22 January, and Early Decision II to 15 January. African students applying to a US university in New York can be considered for these merit awards simply by applying on time.
opportunities.benefits: Merit scholarships of USD 10,000 to 25,000 per year for highly qualified first-year international applicants, renewable at the same amount for up to four years. Transfer students can receive up to USD 25,000. Separate need-based aid is limited and does not cover the full cost.
requirements: International applicant on a non-immigrant visa (US citizens and permanent residents use the domestic process)
Complete first-year application through the Common Application
English test (TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo or Pearson) for non-native speakers without four years of recent English-medium schooling
For need-based aid: CSS Profile and an expected family contribution of at least USD 50,000 a year
Keep the required GPA to renew the award
documents: CSS Profile (school code 2259) if applying for need-based aid
opportunities.selection_process: Merit awards are decided automatically from the complete admission file; there is no separate merit application. Need-based aid is awarded to about 5% of aid applicants.
important_dates: Early Decision II: 3 January, extended to 15 January
Regular Decision: 3 January, extended to 22 January
CSS Profile: 15 January for Regular Decision
opportunities.about_provider: Fordham University is a private Jesuit university in New York City, with campuses at Rose Hill in the Bronx and Lincoln Center in Manhattan.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply to Fordham through the Common Application by the Regular Decision or Early Decision II deadline; you are then considered for merit awards automatically. If you also need need-based aid, submit the CSS Profile by its deadline.
opportunities.notes: Fordham does not give CSS Profile fee waivers or loans in international aid packages. Applying for need-based aid can affect admission, because admission is need-aware for international students.

opportunities.title: OMBEE27: OpenMBEE Workshop 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers worldwide can submit papers by the deadline for this conference (Pasadena, 3 February 2027).

opportunities.title: UNIST International Undergraduate Scholarships, Fall 2027
opportunities.provider: Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International high-school graduates can apply for tuition waivers renewable on credits and GPA.

opportunities.title: Maryam Mirzakhani Scholarships 2027 (master's plus PhD in mathematics)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Women of any nationality who are finishing a bachelor's or first year of master's, preferably in mathematics, and plan to join an eligible Paris-Saclay or IP Paris mathematics master's can apply.
opportunities.description:
The Maryam Mirzakhani Scholarships are part of the Women in Mathematics programme of the Fondation Mathématique Jacques Hadamard (FMJH). They fund talented female students from anywhere in the world through a master's in mathematics and then a three-year PhD at the Hadamard Doctoral School (EDMH) in the Paris region.

Winners join the master's 'Mathematics and Applications' at Université Paris-Saclay or Institut Polytechnique de Paris, entering in the first or second year depending on their background. They receive an excellence scholarship of €11,000 a year during the master's and a commitment of doctoral funding worth a minimum of about €82,800 gross over three years.

The call for 2027 opened on 21 October 2026 and closes on 24 January 2027. Because it is open to every nationality, it is an outstanding route for African women in mathematics into one of Europe's strongest mathematical communities.
opportunities.benefits: A master's excellence scholarship of €11,000 per year for one or two years, followed by three years of doctoral funding with a minimum total gross amount of about €82,800. A contribution to master's and PhD tuition is included.
requirements: Female applicant of any nationality
Completing a bachelor's degree or the first year of a master's at the time of application, preferably in mathematics
Intends to enrol in an eligible M1 or M2 of the 'Mathematics and Applications' master's at Paris-Saclay or IP Paris
Plans to continue to a PhD at EDMH
documents: Referee letters (submitted by referees by 31 January 2027)
opportunities.selection_process: An award jury makes a preliminary selection, then shortlisted candidates have a video interview in English or French.
opportunities.about_provider: The Fondation Mathématique Jacques Hadamard brings together the mathematics departments and laboratories of Université Paris-Saclay, Institut Polytechnique de Paris and partner institutions. It funds students, researchers and programmes and runs the Hadamard Doctoral School of Mathematics (EDMH).
opportunities.how_to_apply: Check the list of eligible master's courses on the FMJH site, then complete the online Maryam Mirzakhani application form before 24 January 2027. Ask your referees to submit their letters by 31 January 2027.
opportunities.notes: The number of awards is not stated. Questions go to the FMJH contact email.

opportunities.title: Perimeter Scholars International Full Scholarship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Students with a strong physics or maths bachelor's can apply for the fully funded PSI master's covering tuition, housing, meals, stipend and health insurance.

opportunities.title: Sophie Germain Master Scholarships 2027 (Wave 1)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Mathematics students of any nationality entering the Paris-Saclay Mathematics and Applications master's may apply by 24 January 2027 for EUR 11,000 a year plus travel and housing support.
opportunities.description:
The Sophie Germain Master Scholarships fund talented students from around the world who join the Mathematics and Applications master's programme in the Paris-Saclay area, either at Université Paris-Saclay or at Institut Polytechnique de Paris. Around fifty scholarships are given each year, and selection is made without regard to where applicants come from.

The awards are run by the Fondation Mathématique Jacques Hadamard (FMJH) and cover either the first (M1) or second (M2) year of the master's in one of the listed research-oriented courses. The 2027 Wave 1 call is reserved for students who are currently outside the Paris-Saclay institutions.

For African mathematics students the scholarship is a strong route into one of Europe's largest mathematics research clusters: it pays a living allowance, helps with registration fees and travel, and offers housing to first-time international students. English-speaking students can follow the English-taught Jacques Hadamard M1 tracks.
opportunities.benefits: EUR 11,000 net per year; a flat-rate contribution to university registration fees; for first-time international students, up to EUR 2,000 (depending on country) towards one return trip and visa costs, an offer of an individual studio in Orsay or Evry and a housing kit worth about EUR 100; access to French language courses.
requirements: Admission to one of the listed research courses of the Mathematics and Applications master's (M1 or M2) at Université Paris-Saclay or Institut Polytechnique de Paris
Wave 1 is only for students coming from outside the Paris-Saclay institutions
Strong academic record in mathematics, shown by transcripts and references
Non-European students must obtain a French student visa and a Campus France file number
Cannot be combined with another excellence scholarship
documents: Transcripts for each year of the bachelor's and first year of master's (or equivalent)
Names and emails of two referees, who upload their letters
opportunities.selection_process: A jury appointed by the FMJH steering committee together with the heads of the master's programmes judges applications on academic criteria, mainly transcripts and recommendation letters. Results are announced about five weeks after the closing date.
important_dates: Results: about five weeks after the deadline
opportunities.about_provider: The Fondation Mathématique Jacques Hadamard is a research foundation that brings together the mathematics laboratories of the Paris-Saclay area. It runs graduate programmes and scholarships, including the Sophie Germain master's awards and the Maryam Mirzakhani doctoral scholarships.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Fill in the FMJH online scholarship form and, separately, apply for admission to the chosen master's through Université Paris-Saclay or Institut Polytechnique de Paris. Give the names of two referees, who must send their letters by 31 January 2027.
opportunities.notes: Students who do not speak French are pointed to the English-taught M1 Jacques Hadamard tracks. Contact: contact@fondation-hadamard.fr.

opportunities.title: Erasmus Mundus Master in Food Innovation and Product Design (FIPDes)

The Graduate Research School Scholarships (UQGRSS), which include the Australian Government Research Training Program, are the University of Queensland's main awards for research degrees. They support students doing a PhD, an MPhil or a research-focused professional doctorate at UQ, and both domestic and international applicants can compete.

opportunities.title: Institute for Law & AI Summer Fellowship 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Law graduates and researchers from any country can apply by 29 January 2027 for a paid 2027 AI law summer fellowship in Cambridge (UK) or a remote-first track with a Washington, DC convening.
opportunities.description:
The Institute for Law & AI (LawAI) runs paid summer research fellowships for people who want to work on the legal questions raised by advanced artificial intelligence. For 2027 there are two tracks. The EU Law fellowship runs from 28 June to 3 September 2027, mostly in person in Cambridge, United Kingdom, and starts with a Convening Week there on 5-9 July. The Legal Frontiers fellowship is remote-first and lasts ten weeks, from 14 June to 20 August 2027, with a Convening Week in Washington, DC on 21-25 June.

Fellows carry out a research project with guidance from LawAI staff, take part in seminars and meet others working on AI law and policy. Applicants from all countries are welcome, and prior AI research is not required.

The fellowship is a well-paid way for African law graduates and researchers with an interest in technology regulation to build a network and a publication record in a fast-growing field.
opportunities.benefits: EU Law track: GBP 1,000 per week (more for exceptional candidates), a GBP 7,000 relocation payment for fellows who move to Cambridge for the whole fellowship, travel for the Convening Week for those who cannot relocate, and the UK visa fee and Immigration Health Surcharge. Legal Frontiers track: a weekly subsidy of USD 1,800 (US-based) or GBP 1,000 (EU/UK-based), travel, accommodation and meals for the Washington Convening Week, and admission to the 2027 Workshop on Law-Following AI.
requirements: A background in law (degree, legal training or legal research) is preferred; Legal Frontiers also considers exceptional candidates from computer science, policy, economics, history, philosophy or psychology
EU Law track: EU law experience is desirable but not required
Legal Frontiers track: good understanding of law and policy in at least one of the US, EU or UK
Full-time availability for the whole fellowship period and attendance at the Convening Week
Right to work or a visa for in-person work (LawAI may sponsor case by case)
opportunities.selection_process: Step 1 is the online form. Step 2 is a recorded screening interview of about 20-30 minutes. Step 3 is a 30-45 minute research interview. Decisions are made by LawAI staff by the end of March 2027; AI tools may assist in reviewing applications.
important_dates: Applications close: 29 January 2027 (Legal Frontiers: 11:59 pm US Eastern time)
opportunities.about_provider: The Institute for Law & AI is an independent think tank that researches how law can help govern artificial intelligence safely. It runs fellowships, workshops and research programmes in the United States, the United Kingdom and Europe.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the application form on the relevant LawAI fellowship page. Applications for the EU Law track are reviewed on a rolling basis, so applying early helps.
opportunities.notes: Contact: programs@law-ai.org. The fixed relocation payment is taxable. The fellowship can be extended by up to five weeks on the EU Law track.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Third-year bachelor's and master's students worldwide with a space-related project may apply by 29 January 2027 (or 28 May 2027) for up to EUR 1,200 a month to study or intern in the Paris region.
opportunities.description:
The Space Academy of Île-de-France offers incoming international mobility scholarships for students who want to come to the Paris region for space-related study or research. The scholarship gives a monthly living stipend either to follow one semester or one year of a master's programme belonging to the Academy, or to do a research internship in one of its laboratories while still enrolled at a university abroad.

The Academy is a France 2030 project that links eight Île-de-France institutions working in space science and engineering, including Université Paris-Saclay, Sorbonne Université, ONERA, Université Paris Cité, UPEC, UVSQ, Institut Polytechnique de Paris and PSL. The 2027 call has three deadlines; the first (30 October 2026) has passed, so the next one is 29 January 2027, followed by 28 May 2027.

The programme is open to third-year bachelor's and master's students worldwide, so African students in physics, engineering, Earth observation or related fields can use it to join a French space master's or gain lab experience in Paris.
opportunities.benefits: A monthly living stipend of up to EUR 1,200 for one semester or one academic year (master's study can be supported for up to two years if the student re-applies for M2). Tuition may be waived only under specific exchange agreements; research interns pay no tuition. Flights and travel are not covered, and an intern's total income including other grants must not exceed the stated amount.
requirements: Third-year bachelor's student or first/second-year master's student
Project must be exclusively linked to the space field
Master's route: must name a specific Academy master's programme, have the programme head's support, and not have studied at a French university before
Internship route: must be enrolled at a university abroad and have a supporting lab supervisor
PhD students are not eligible
documents: Support from the master's head or lab supervisor
All files merged into a single PDF named SPACE-IDF-IntMobility-Incoming2027-Form_StudentName.pdf
opportunities.selection_process: The Space Academy International Mobility Committee reviews applications first. Final approval also depends on the master's programme head, the host department and, for internships, the host laboratory. Answers are given about four weeks after each deadline.
important_dates: Response: about four weeks after each deadline
opportunities.about_provider: The Académie Spatiale d'Île-de-France is a French Government France 2030 project that coordinates space-related education across eight universities and research organisations in the Paris region. It also funds outgoing mobility and apprenticeships.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Biomedical researchers of any nationality under 40 (PhD students to postdocs) may apply by 31 January 2027 for one of seven EUR 32,000 one-year fellowships.
opportunities.description:
The IBSA Foundation Fellowships give young biomedical researchers a year of funding to carry out a research project in a host laboratory, university, hospital or research centre of their choice. The 2026 call offers seven fellowships in dermatology, endocrinology, fertility and urology, orthopaedics and pain medicine, and healthy ageing. Projects must start by 2027 and last 12 months.

The programme is run by the IBSA Foundation for scientific research in Lugano, Switzerland. It is open to researchers of any nationality under 40, from PhD students and residents to postdocs, who hold a degree in medicine, biology, pharmacy, biotechnology or bioengineering.

Alongside the fellowships, a separate Research Equity Prize of EUR 5,000 rewards the best project hosted in a developing country, including any African country, which gives African-based labs and researchers an extra chance of support.
opportunities.benefits: Each fellowship is worth EUR 32,000 gross (before tax), meant to cover salary and mobility costs for 12 months, paid half before the project starts and half by the end of 2027. It does not cover bench fees, overheads or consumables. The Research Equity Prize pays EUR 5,000 in one instalment.
requirements: Any nationality
Under 40 years old on the deadline
Degree in medicine, biology, pharmacy, biotechnology or bioengineering
PhD students, PhD holders, postdocs and medical residents may apply; holders of permanent positions such as professors may not
Must be based at the host institution for the whole grant
Project in dermatology, endocrinology, fertility/urology, orthopaedics/pain medicine or healthy ageing
documents: List of one to three best peer-reviewed publications
Project proposal entered on the online platform
Acceptance letter from the host institution (within one week of being notified as a winner)
opportunities.selection_process: The IBSA Scientific Board peer-reviews proposals for feasibility, originality and scientific value, along with the candidate's CV (especially research experience) and the suitability of the host lab. opportunities.about_provider: The IBSA Foundation for scientific research is a Swiss non-profit foundation in Lugano linked to the pharmaceutical company IBSA. It promotes biomedical research and science communication through fellowships, scholarships and events.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit the proposal and the three documents as separate files on the foundation's application platform (ibsafoundation.poliresearch.com). Only online applications are accepted.
opportunities.notes: Winners must answer a yearly survey and acknowledge the foundation in publications. Contact: info@ibsafoundation.org, +41 58 360 10 00.

Excellent GPA

Statements shared: International Women's Day, March 2027

opportunities.description:
beVisioneers: The Mercedes-Benz Fellowship is a two-year programme for young people who want to turn an early idea for an environmental solution into a working project. The first year is an intensive, mostly online training year (at least 24 hours a month) in which fellows build a prototype with venture coaching, mentoring and project scholarships. The second year is an acceleration year with continued support and a cost-of-living stipend.

The fellowship is funded by Mercedes-Benz and run by The DO School Fellowships in Hamburg, Germany. It is delivered in English in a hybrid format and includes regional summits where fellows meet in person. Applications are now open for the 2027/28 fellowship year.

Eligibility depends on where you live, not your passport. In Africa, residents of Kenya, Rwanda, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda and Zimbabwe can apply, alongside residents of Europe, India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Mexico, Türkiye, the UK and the US.
opportunities.benefits: Project scholarships of up to EUR 15,000, available at the end of the first year; a cost-of-living stipend in the second year (amount not stated); innovation training, one-to-one mentoring and travel to regional summits.

Strong command of English
Has identified an environmental problem to solve
Neither you nor a parent or guardian works for Mercedes-Benz
Able to commit at least 24 hours a month in year one
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants are assessed on their written answers and their recorded interview video, which is also used to judge English ability. The number of fellows is not stated.
opportunities.about_provider: beVisioneers was launched in 2023 by Mercedes-Benz and is delivered by The DO School Fellowships gGmbH, a Hamburg-based organisation that trains young changemakers to launch social and environmental projects.

opportunities.description:
The NL Scholarship at Radboud University in Nijmegen is a one-off award of €5,000 for students from outside the EU/EEA who start an English-taught master's programme. It is paid for jointly by the Dutch Ministry of Education and the university, and up to 32 awards are available for 2027-28.

It is a partial award, not a full scholarship, and can only be given together with the Radboud Scholarship Programme (RSP), so applicants must apply for both. Faculties judge candidates on academic excellence and ambition.

African students who hold a bachelor's degree from outside the Netherlands and are fully admitted to a regular English-taught master's (not an Erasmus Mundus or joint degree) can apply. The application must be in OSIRIS by 31 January 2027 and complete by 14 February 2027.
opportunities.benefits: €5,000, awarded once for one year. It does not cover the full cost of study.

Bachelor's degree obtained outside the Netherlands, with no previous Dutch education
Meet the English proficiency requirement
Full admission to an English-taught Radboud master's (not Erasmus Mundus or joint-degree)
Apply also for the Radboud Scholarship Programme
Full-time enrolment and compliance with visa rules
documents: Master's application in OSIRIS with the NL Scholarship indicated
opportunities.selection_process: Each faculty assesses academic excellence (grades, test scores, publications, relevance of the degree, standing of the university) and ambition (motivation, promise, life experience and extracurricular activities). Decisions are expected around mid-April 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: Radboud University is a public research university in Nijmegen, the Netherlands, with about 24,000 students. It offers many English-taught master's programmes and runs its own scholarship programme for talented non-EU students.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for your English-taught master's in OSIRIS and indicate the NL Scholarship by 31 January 2027, then make sure the application is complete by 14 February 2027. The fellowships come with the PhD programmes in economics, finance and management for the 2027/28 intake, and no separate scholarship application is needed: applying to the PhD is enough to be considered.

For African graduates aiming at an academic or research career in economics or business, it is a funded doctorate at an internationally accredited European school. The same page also lists other funding sources for PhD students, such as FCT studentships, La Caixa INPhINIT and Camões Institute cooperation scholarships.

Fellowships go to the top-ranked applicants

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Non-EU/EEA students admitted to an English-taught Radboud master's starting September 2027 may apply by 31 January 2027 for one of 32 tuition-reduction scholarships.
opportunities.description:
The Radboud Scholarship Programme helps highly talented students from outside the EU/EEA take a full English-taught master's at Radboud University in Nijmegen, the Netherlands. It is very selective: for 2027/2028 there are at most 32 scholarships spread across the faculties of Arts, Law, Management, Philosophy and Theology, Science and Social Sciences.

The scholarship does not pay living costs, but it cuts the tuition fee to the much lower Dutch statutory level and covers the costs of the visa and residence permit as well as health and liability insurance. It is funded from the university's Profiling Fund and lasts for the nominal length of the master's; the second-year grant requires all first-year courses to be passed.

For African students who can fund their living costs, it turns a costly Dutch master's into an affordable one. Erasmus Mundus and joint-degree master's are excluded.
opportunities.benefits: Tuition reduced from the full non-EU rate (around EUR 19,000, depending on the programme) to about EUR 2,771 (amount to be confirmed), plus the costs of the visa and residence permit, health insurance and liability insurance through Aon Student Insurance. Living costs are not covered.

Bachelor's degree obtained outside the Netherlands, with no previous Dutch degree or education
Meets the English requirement of the chosen master's
Full admission to an English-taught master's starting 1 September 2027

opportunities.title: University of Glasgow Computing Science PhD Scholarships 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants with a good computing degree, including international students, can apply by 31 January 2027 for Glasgow Computing Science PhD funding starting October 2027.
opportunities.description:
The School of Computing Science at the University of Glasgow funds PhD students who start in October 2027 or soon after through one competition that covers several scholarship schemes. Applicants are considered for whichever schemes suit them, including the College of Science and Engineering Graduate School Scholarships, College Scholarships, Excellence Bursaries and the part-time Minerva Scholarships.

Coverage differs between schemes. The Graduate School Scholarships pay fees (home or international) and a stipend for three years, while the Excellence Bursary for international students is a fee discount of GBP 10,000 a year. Stipends usually follow the UKRI rate, which is GBP 22,437 for 2027-28.

International applicants, including those from Africa, apply through the normal PhD admission system and simply select the university scholarship as their funding source. The school suggests PhD projects on its website, and contacting a potential supervisor first helps.
opportunities.benefits: Depending on the scheme: tuition fees (home or international) plus a stipend of GBP 22,437 for 2027-28 for three years (Graduate School Scholarships); home-level fees plus UKRI stipend (College Scholarships); a GBP 10,000 a year fee discount for three years for international students (Excellence Bursaries); or a five-year part-time Minerva post with home-level fees and pay of at least GBP 24,000 a year.
requirements: Upper second-class honours undergraduate degree (or equivalent) or a master's degree in computing science or a related field
Applying for a PhD in the School of Computing Science starting October 2027 or shortly after
Meets the University of Glasgow English requirements
documents: Documents listed on the university's before-you-apply page (transcripts, references, research proposal or statement)
opportunities.selection_process: Academic admission and scholarship applications are processed separately; scholarship decisions are confirmed with candidates around April 2027. The number of awards and detailed criteria are not stated.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Glasgow is one of the UK's oldest universities and a member of the Russell Group. Its School of Computing Science is consistently ranked among the top ten in the UK.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online through the University of Glasgow postgraduate research application, and choose 'Univ of Glasgow Scholarship' as your funding source. Look at the school's suggested PhD projects and contact a supervisor before applying.

opportunities.description:
Centre College, a private liberal arts college in Danville, Kentucky, offers Language Scholarships to incoming first-year students who want to pursue a language and its culture. The award is open to both international and domestic students entering in Fall 2027, and no major or minor in the language is required.

The scholarship is worth up to USD 5,000 a year, is renewable, and can be combined with Centre's general merit scholarships, which for international applicants are typically USD 15,000 to 30,000 a year and awarded automatically. Recipients must keep at least a 3.0 GPA in their language courses and are expected to study abroad.

For African students this is a way to reduce the cost of a US liberal arts education, especially combined with general merit aid. Applicants may even apply in their native language, but only one language scholarship can be held, and Spanish applicants must record a short video in Spanish.
opportunities.benefits: Up to USD 5,000 per year, renewable, stackable with general merit scholarships (USD 15,000-30,000 per year for international applicants). International students should plan for roughly USD 25,000 a year in remaining costs according to the college.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Early-career researchers living in a low- or middle-income country, mainly nationals of DGD partner countries, with an ITM supervisor and a home-institute supervisor, can apply for 3 to 6 months of pre-PhD training in Antwerp.
opportunities.description:
The ITM-DGD Predoctoral Research Training Grants let promising early-career researchers from low- and middle-income countries spend three to six months at the Institute of Tropical Medicine (ITM) in Antwerp, Belgium, to prepare a PhD project. The training is not a degree; it is meant to build the skills and proposal needed to start doctoral research.

The grants are funded by the Belgian Directorate-General for Development Cooperation (DGD). At most five grants are available in the 2027 call, to be taken up between 15 June 2027 and 14 June 2028, preferably before the end of 2027.

Most eligible countries are in Africa, including Benin, Burkina Faso, Burundi, DR Congo, Ethiopia, Guinea, Kenya, Madagascar, Mali, Morocco, Mozambique, Niger, Rwanda, Senegal, South Africa, Tanzania and Uganda. Applicants need both an ITM supervisor and a supervisor at their home institute.
opportunities.benefits: A living allowance of €28 per day (up to 6 months in Antwerp), a housing allowance, a bench fee of €1,470 per month, a return ticket, insurance (€63 per month) and €200 for indirect travel costs. Grantees have student status, not employee status.

Nationality of a DGD-eligible country (a limited number of grants for other LMIC nationals)
Formal supervisor at ITM and at the home institute
Early-career researcher with strong potential for PhD research
Not a dual national of a high-income country
No more than one year of employment in a high-income country in the three years before 1 February 2027
Never on the ITM payroll

Master Mind is a Flemish Government scholarship that the University of Antwerp uses to attract outstanding international students to its master's programmes. For 2027-28 the university can award five scholarships across 15 eligible one- and two-year programmes.

Each winner receives a one-time grant of €5,375, and non-EEA winners pay the much lower EEA tuition fee instead of the international rate (€1,181.40 for 60 credits in 2026-27). Winners are chosen for their academic record and potential, motivation, maturity and relevant work experience.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers who are US citizens or foreign nationals with the required US documents can apply for a $5,000 stipend for at least six weeks of research across several New England archives.
opportunities.description:
The New England Regional Fellowship Consortium (NERFC) is a group of 29 libraries, archives and historical societies coordinated by the Massachusetts Historical Society. Each year it funds researchers to work in the collections of several member institutions.

Each fellowship pays $5,000 for at least six weeks of research between 1 June 2027 and 31 May 2028. The plan must include at least two weeks at each of two institutions and at least one week at a third, with the remaining time at any member institution. The consortium expects to make at least two dozen awards.

Foreign nationals may apply if they hold the necessary US government documents, and should talk to MHS staff about stipend eligibility before applying. Applicants without a doctorate need a recommendation letter from a faculty member.

The International Merit Scholarship is a tuition reduction offered by ACAP University College to new international students who enrol in one of its eligible bachelor's or master's courses. For the Trimester 2, 2027 intake it takes 20% off the published tuition fees, spread evenly across all the units of the course.

ACAP teaches in Adelaide, Brisbane, Melbourne, Perth and Sydney, and the award applies to courses in psychology, counselling, social work, management and criminology. It can run for the full normal length of the course: up to four years (12 trimesters) for a bachelor's degree and up to two years (6 trimesters) for a master's degree of full-time study.

The official page places no limit on nationality, so African students who apply to ACAP as international students can compete. Candidates are judged on their academic record and on a written statement about leadership, community contribution and their future goals.

Only one scholarship, bursary or discount can apply to a unit; if several apply, the highest one is used.

Study full time

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Nationals and residents of Malawi, Zambia or Zimbabwe with a good engineering degree and an offer for a one-year engineering master's at Strathclyde in 2027/28 can apply.
opportunities.description:
The Beit Strathclyde (BStrath) Scholarship is a full award for one-year taught master's study in the Faculty of Engineering at the University of Strathclyde in Glasgow. It is run jointly by the university and the Beit Trust, and one scholarship is offered for the 2027/28 academic year.

The award covers the whole cost of the course, including tuition and living costs, for the one-year programme. Eligible departments are Architecture; Biomedical Engineering; Chemical and Process Engineering; Civil and Environmental Engineering; Design, Manufacturing and Engineering Management; Electronic and Electrical Engineering; Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering; and Naval Architecture, Ocean and Marine Engineering.

The scholarship is aimed at future leaders from Malawi, Zambia and Zimbabwe, the three countries the Beit Trust serves. Applicants are expected to return home after their studies and use what they have learned for the benefit of their country.
opportunities.benefits: Full tuition fees; a living allowance; UK visa and Immigration Health Surcharge, TB test and biometrics costs; arrival, laptop and departure allowances; and economy return flights. Dependants are not funded.
requirements: National and permanent resident of Malawi, Zambia or Zimbabwe at the time of application
A good engineering degree from a recognised university (Distinction or Upper Second preferred)
An offer for a one-year taught master's in one of the eight eligible Strathclyde engineering departments for 2027/28
International fee status
About three years of work experience is a guide
Commitment to return home after the course
Must not have started the course already
documents: Offer letter from the University of Strathclyde
Personal statement of up to 300 words on how the study will benefit your country
Three references (academic, character and employer if applicable)
opportunities.selection_process: The Beit Trust selects on merit and eligibility, looking at degree results, work experience, leadership potential, commitment to return home and the relevance of the course. Shortlisted candidates are usually interviewed in person in April in Lusaka, Harare or Blantyre.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Strathclyde is a public technological university in Glasgow, Scotland, with a large engineering faculty. The Beit Trust is a UK charity that has supported education and development in Malawi, Zambia and Zimbabwe for over a century, including postgraduate scholarships at partner universities.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Secure an offer for an eligible Strathclyde engineering master's first. Referees can also send forms to the Beit Trust scholarships email address.
opportunities.notes: Only one award is available. You can submit only one Beit Trust application and cannot save and return to the form. Strathclyde contact: Robert Graham. Late applications are not processed.

ISCB UK 2027, the UK meeting of the International Society for Computational Biology, will be held at the University of Strathclyde in Glasgow from 20 to 22 April 2027 under the theme "Biology in the Age of AI". The organisers are inviting abstracts for talks and posters, and the first day includes a student symposium for PhD students and postdocs.

Topics include artificial intelligence and machine learning in biology and medicine; bioinformatics infrastructure, training and community; genomics, evolution and multi-omics; structural, molecular and systems biology; translational and precision medicine; and emerging areas of computational biology.

Presenters must register for the conference
Student symposium option for PhD students and postdocs

Printed poster up to 46 x 46 inches, or a PDF poster and 5-7 minute video for the virtual hall, if accepted
opportunities.selection_process: Submissions are reviewed for talks and posters; abstracts submitted for 'talk and poster' that are not chosen for a talk are automatically considered for a poster.

BI is a member of the Global Business School Network (GBSN), and this award is one of two scholarships it uses to support initiatives in Africa. opportunities.eligibility_summary: African-domiciled passport holders with first-class-equivalent grades who hold or are seeking an offer for a one-year taught master's at Glasgow starting September 2027 can apply for a 75% tuition fee waiver.
opportunities.description:
The University of Glasgow African Excellence Award is a merit scholarship for outstanding students from across Africa who want to take a one-year, full-time taught master's degree at Glasgow in Scotland. The 2027/28 round is for the September 2027 intake and covers almost every subject the university teaches.

The award takes the form of a 75% reduction in tuition fees, which in most colleges is worth more than £20,000. Up to 16 awards are available, and shortlisted applicants are invited to an interview.

Applicants must live in Africa and hold a passport from an African country, have grades equivalent to a UK first-class degree, and set out a clear career or development plan. You can apply for the award before you have an offer, but you need an offer to be considered for interview.
opportunities.benefits: A 75% tuition fee waiver for one year of study. Examples given by the university: about £20,543 off in Arts and Humanities, £25,281 in Medical, Veterinary and Life Sciences, £26,111 in Science and Engineering and the Adam Smith Business School, and £21,206 in Social Sciences. The actual value depends on the fee in your offer letter.
requirements: Domiciled in Africa and holding a passport from an African country
Grades equivalent to a UK first-class honours degree
Holding or applying for an offer for a one-year full-time taught master's starting September 2027
International fee status
Clear career and/or development plan
Must meet the UKVI living-cost requirement
documents: Online scholarship application form, including your career or development plan
Offer for an eligible master's programme (needed before interview)
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants are judged on academic excellence and their plans. Shortlisted candidates are invited to interview and contacted by 7 May 2027. Up to 16 awards are made.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Glasgow, founded in 1451, is one of the oldest universities in the English-speaking world and a member of the UK's Russell Group of research-intensive universities.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for your master's programme at Glasgow, then complete the African Excellence Award form on the university's scholarship portal (linked from the award page). Questions go to student.recruitment@glasgow.ac.uk.
opportunities.notes: Postgraduate diplomas and certificates are not eligible. The award cannot be combined with other Glasgow scholarships or discounts except the alumni discount; if you are offered more than one award, the lower one is withdrawn.

opportunities.title: Bocconi4Access to Education: 100% Tuition Waivers for International Bachelor's and Law Students 2027-28
opportunities.eligibility_summary: International students entering the first year of a Bocconi Bachelor's or Law programme in 2027-28 can apply, after enrolling, for a full tuition and fees waiver based on their family's economic situation.
opportunities.description:
Bocconi University in Milan runs the Bocconi4Access to Education scheme to make its degrees affordable for students from families with limited means. For the 2027-28 academic year it offers a waiver of 100% of Bocconi's ordinary tuition and fees to international students starting the first year of a Bachelor's or Law degree. Applicants who do not qualify for the full waiver are automatically considered for one of the university's other benefits.

The waiver is assessed mainly on the family's economic and asset situation under Bocconi's rules, rather than on a single requirement. It is renewable each year as long as the student meets the merit requirements, so it can fund a whole degree.

For African students admitted to Bocconi, this is one of the most valuable awards available in Italy, because it removes tuition entirely at one of Europe's leading business and economics universities. The application is only possible once the student has completed enrolment, so timing matters.
opportunities.benefits: A 100% waiver of Bocconi's ordinary academic tuition and fees, renewable each year if merit requirements are met. Students who miss the full waiver are considered for other partial benefits. The first tuition instalment is paid upfront and refunded by the end of December if the conditions are met.
requirements: International student starting the first year of a Bocconi Bachelor's or Law programme in 2027-28
Assessment of the family's economic and asset situation under Bocconi rules
Must have completed enrolment before applying
Must keep meeting merit requirements to renew each year
documents: Bocconi4Access to Education 2027-28 application in MyApplication
Required documentation on family income and assets (listed on Bocconi's documentation page)
Documents signed by hand, with the signature matching your ID
opportunities.selection_process: Bocconi evaluates the family's economic and asset situation according to its general rules; awards are not decided on any single criterion. Results for the early session come by 25 February 2027 and for the winter session by 27 May 2027. Winners must formally accept the benefit or lose it.
important_dates: Early Session and HEC 1st round: apply 12-30 November 2026, results by 25 February 2027
Winter Session and HEC 2nd round: apply 15 March - 5 April 2027, results by 27 May 2027
HEC 3rd round: 27 May - 4 June 2027, results by 8 July 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Bocconi University is a private university in Milan, Italy, specialising in economics, management, finance, law and data science. It consistently ranks among Europe's top business schools.
opportunities.how_to_apply: After enrolling at Bocconi, wait about two hours for portal access, then submit a single 'Bocconi4Access to Education a.y. 2027-28' application through MyApplication within your session's window. Upload all required documents, signed by hand; incomplete applications receive no benefit.
opportunities.notes: The early window applies to early-session admits; later admits use the March-April window. Remember to accept the award formally when offered.

opportunities.description:
ICANN's Fellowship Program brings newcomers and returning fellows to its public meetings so they can learn how the internet's domain name system is governed and join its policy work. The ICANN90 Annual General Meeting takes place in Adelaide, Australia, from 30 October to 4 November 2027.

Unlike the ICANN89 Policy Forum round, which is limited to alumni, this round is open to first-time applicants. Applications open on 22 March 2027 and close on 22 April 2027.
